2610.07774.title: Reading, Not Manipulating: Leveraging Router Logits for Multimodal Safety in MoE Vision-Language Models
2610.07774.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) face compositional safety risks where harmful intent emerges from the interaction between visual and textual inputs. As mixture-of-experts (MoE) VLMs become increasingly common, recent work has explored various safety interventions, including prompting, supervised fine-tuning, and routing-based expert steering. However, these methods show inconsistent improvements across models and evaluation distributions, and the intervention into model behavior or internal states introduce safety-utility tradeoffs by over-refusal. Rather than manipulating internal states to steer model behavior, we instead ask whether routing states can serve as diagnostic signals for multimodal safety. We find that router logits indeed provide highly predictive signals of whether a multimodal input is safe or not. Motivated by this observation, we introduce a lightweight router-logit safety detector that reads out routing signals during prompt prefill and identifies unsafe requests before generation, without modifying model parameters or expert routing. Across Qwen3-VL and Kimi-VL, the proposed detector substantially reduces safety errors on the HoliSafe benchmark and resoundingly generalizes to out-of-distribution safety benchmarks featuring different safety patterns, including MISHard and MM-SafetyBench. The success of the proposed router-logit detector also suggests a broader perspective on model internals: rather than focusing only on manipulating internal components to steer behavior, simply reading naturally emerging signals and linking them to an external safety mechanism can provide a simple, effective, and non-intrusive complement to existing safety interventions.

2610.07696.title: ESP: Energy-Score Policy for One-Step Multimodal Action Generation
2610.07696.abstract: Generative action models based on diffusion and flow matching have been increasingly adopted in vision-language-action (VLA) policies for their ability to capture diverse behaviors, including multiple valid action sequences under the same observation and instruction. Their iterative sampling procedures, however, require repeated network evaluations to generate each action chunk, increasing inference latency in closed-loop control. We propose ESP (Energy-Score Policy), a teacher-free approach that maps policy context and noise directly to an action chunk in a single network evaluation. ESP trains the action head with the energy score rather than mean squared error. Whereas squared-error regression targets the conditional mean, the energy score is strictly proper: its expected value is uniquely minimized by the target distribution. This provides a principled objective for learning multimodal action distributions without iterative sampling, with exact recovery at the population optimum when the model can represent the target distribution. Experiments on both simulation and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate competitive task success with substantially lower action-generation latency than the flow matching baseline. These results support direct distributional learning as an efficient alternative to iterative generative robot policies.

2610.07689.title: Unlocking Fine-Grained Perception in CLIP via Structurally-Aware Latent Masked Modeling
2610.07689.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as CLIP excel in global semantic alignment but often lack fine-grained perceptual capabilities. This hinders dense prediction tasks and bottlenecks the visual potential of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). Existing research has attempted to enhance CLIP's visual representations by incorporating geometric priors from vision-centric models. However, these strategies often struggle to achieve deep alignment for both local spatial structures and global semantics, potentially even distorting the original image-text space. To address these limitations, we propose SALM, an unsupervised embedding alignment framework based on structurally-aware latent mask modeling. SALM effectively synergizes local and global alignment via a dual-path design combining explicit and implicit mechanisms, without requiring any image-text pairs. First, we introduce a dual-matrix alignment strategy that explicitly calibrates intra-sample spatial correlations and activation intensities, thereby effectively injecting local geometric priors. Based on this, we further design a latent mask modeling mechanism to guide CLIP to restore the missing semantic details of the target model, thereby implicitly aggregating fine-grained structures into the global semantic space. Furthermore, driven by the empirical observations that CLIP's shallow features inherently possess strong spatial observational capabilities, we naturally extend SALM to a highly efficient self-distillation paradigm, SALM-Self. This unlocks CLIP's intrinsic fine-grained potential without relying on any external models. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SALM not only significantly improves performance in dense prediction tasks but also boosts CLIP's zero-shot accuracy, effectively enhancing the fine-grained understanding capabilities of MLLMs. Project page at https://qzfm.github.io/salm_project_page/.

2610.07590.title: Portfolio Design and Pricing for Multimodal Mobility-on-Demand Services Considering Traveler Responses
2610.07590.abstract: Mobility-on-demand (MoD) platforms can offer exclusive, pooled, and transit-connected services to accommodate different passenger needs. However, determining which services to offer and at what prices is challenging because profitability depends on both passenger choices and operational feasibility. This paper proposes a real-time framework that jointly optimizes service menus, fares, and vehicle trip plans for individual MoD requests. Passenger choices are modeled using a generalized nested logit (GNL) model that captures correlated substitution among service options based on vehicle sharing and transit use. To solve the resulting nonlinear fare-optimization problem, we use Fenchel duality to transform the nonlinear objective from the fare domain to the choice-probability domain, yielding a concave maximization involving a generalized entropy term. We evaluate the framework through operational simulations using real-world New York City trip records. Joint portfolio design and pricing improve operator service margins by 28.4% and 8.5% compared with optimizing only service menus and only fares, respectively. Furthermore, the proposed reformulation is up to 18.8 times faster than solving the original pricing problem directly in fare space, improving computational efficiency for real-time MoD operations.

2610.07540.title: Preserving Unstable Modes Through Inverse Dynamics in JEPA World Models
2610.07540.abstract: Robotic systems often exhibit unstable modes, along which small perturbations and disturbances can cause unbounded growth unless corrected through feedback. Controlling such systems from high-dimensional visual observations requires representations that preserve these modes. Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) provide a natural framework for learning such representations and their dynamics from visual data. However, we demonstrate that next step prediction combined with anti-collapse regularization does not guarantee that controllable unstable modes are preserved: the training loss can be minimized while these modes are collapsed, making stabilization from the learned representation impossible. To address this, we augment world-model training with an action reconstruction objective (i.e., an inverse dynamics loss) that encourages control-aware representations, namely, visual representations that preserve crucial features for control. We prove that exact action reconstruction makes the encoder injective on the finite-horizon reachable subspace. Thus, the encoder cannot discard any state direction reachable by an action sequence within $H$ steps. Moreover, we show that, as $H$ grows, the dominant eigenspace of the finite-horizon controllability Gramian converges to the controllable unstable subspace. We establish our theoretical results for linear systems and demonstrate empirically that our findings extend to nonlinear visual control tasks (CartPole, Walker2D, and PointMaze), highlighting the benefits of control-aware representation learning.

doi:10.1109/tim.2025.3559575.title: Maritime Infrared Ship Detection in AAV Imagery Based on Two-Stage Region-Segmentation-Guided Learning Network
doi:10.1109/tim.2025.3559575.venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
first_author_affiliations: School of Instrumentation and Optoelectronic Engineering, Beihang University, Beijing, China
doi:10.1109/tim.2025.3559575.abstract: Infrared (IR) ship detection in unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) imagery under maritime environments encounters challenges due to the complexity of sea-sky backgrounds. Current research efforts have not fully leveraged the unique characteristics of maritime scenes to distinguish this task from general IR target detection. To overcome these limitations, we propose a Two-Stage Sea-Sky Region-Segmentation-Guided IR Ship Enhancement and Detection (TIRSD) learning network, specifically designed for targeted ship enhancement and detection in maritime environments. The process is structured into two main stages: enhancement and detection. In the enhancement stage, pixel-level sea-sky region segmentation is accomplished via sea-sky line (SSL) detection, which is followed by precise IR ship enhancement and interference suppression, utilizing specially designed morphological filters. For the detection stage, the Bilateral Hierarchical Target Encoding Module (BHTEM) is introduced to encode both high- and low-dimensional features, ensuring optimal detail retention and extraction. Additionally, the Iterative Fusion Enhancement Midlayer (IFEM) with neighborhood reinforcement operations is presented. Furthermore, a newly controllable Local Discrete Attention Mechanism (LDAM) is utilized to focus on small ships, thereby improving detection efficiency. TIRSD surpasses the current leading methods in terms of accuracy, achieving a Mean Average Precision (mAP) of 76.9% on the proposed dataset and 52.4% on a public dataset. Comprehensive experimental results underscore TIRSD’s effective utilization of the unique characteristics of maritime environments, indicating promising application prospects.

translation.zh: 红外线( IR)) 船舶检测 无人驾驶飞行器 (UAV) 海洋环境下的图像由于复杂性而面临挑战。 海天背景. 目前的研究工作没有充分利用海洋场景的独特性来区分这项任务和一般的IR目标探测。 为了克服这些限制,我们提议采用两层海基区域-区间-导航的IR型船舶增强和探测系统。 (TIRSD) 学习网络,专门为在海洋环境中有针对性的船舶增强和探测而设计. 这一过程分为两个主要阶段:增强和检测。 在增强阶段, 像素级 海天区域分割 是通过 海天线 (SSL) 探测,然后使用专门设计的形态过滤器进行精确的IR船增强和干扰压制。 关于探测阶段,双边分级目标编码模块 (BHTEM) 用于编码高维和低维特性,确保最佳细节保留和提取。 此外, 迭代融合增强中间层 (IFEM) 提供邻里支援行动 此外,一个新的可控制 局部离散注意力机制 (LDAM) 用于关注小型船舶,从而提高探测效率。. TIRSD 在准确性方面超过目前的主要方法,实现 平均精度均值 (mAP) 在拟议数据集中占76.9%,在公共数据集中占52.4%。 综合实验结果强调 TIRSD’有效利用海洋环境的独特性,显示有希望的应用前景.

metadata_records.title: Ais-based event detection for offshore wind maintenance vessel operations: A validated framework
metadata_records.abstract: Enhancing the efficiency of offshore wind farm (OWF) operation and maintenance requires understanding vessel movements, turbine visit sequences, vessel–turbine interaction duration as vessel–turbine interaction durations, and transit times. However, detailed operational records are often unavailable because manual logging adds workload for operators. This study proposes an automatic identification system (AIS)-based framework for reconstructing turbine-level maintenance vessel operations from vessel trajectories and turbine coordinates. The framework combines heuristic vessel identification, geospatial filtering, and rule-based event detection to infer visited turbines, visit sequences, service timing, and vessel–turbine interaction durations from AIS data. It is developed using AIS data from maintenance operations at Horns Rev 3 in Denmark and externally validated using operator logs from a vessel operating at three German offshore wind farms: Amrumbank West, Kaskasi, and Nordsee Ost. For a representative validation day, the framework exactly reconstructed the full turbine visit sequence and achieved minute-level temporal accuracy. Across three months of validation, it achieved 100% visit-sequence accuracy, a mean Interaction-Duration MAE of 1.36 min, and a mean mission-duration error of 1.29%. The results show that AIS data can support reliable reconstruction of turbine-level offshore maintenance operations when proprietary records are unavailable, enabling improved vessel scheduling, routing, and maintenance planning.

metadata_records.title: Applications of ship digital twins in maritime transport: A systematic review
metadata_records.abstract: Ship digital twins are increasingly recognised as enabling technologies for intelligent and sustainable maritime transport; however, their large-scale deployment remains constrained by significant technical, operational, and organisational challenges. To address the fragmented nature of existing research, this study proposes a two-layer analytical framework that integrates quantitative bibliometric mapping with qualitative critical synthesis. First, a PRISMA-guided scientometric analysis of 739 publications was conducted using CiteSpace to reveal the intellectual structure, thematic evolution, and emerging trajectories of ship digital twin research. The results indicate a clear transition from early modelling-oriented studies towards increasingly integrated, intelligent, and application-driven maritime cyber–physical systems. The analysis identified three key dimensions for characterising the current state of ship digital twin research: modelling methodologies, system hierarchy, and model validation and maturity. Second, 214 empirical studies were further selected for in-depth qualitative analysis focusing specifically on ship-based digital twins. These studies were systematically examined across three analytical dimensions: modelling methodologies, system hierarchy, and validation maturity. The review reveals that current ship digital twin research is evolving from isolated component-level simulations towards fleet-scale, interoperable, and adaptive cyber–physical ecosystems. In addition, six representative application domains were critically analysed, while explicitly distinguishing one-way digital shadows from bidirectional digital twins. Based on this two-layer analysis, six key deployment challenges are identified, including interoperability limitations, cybersecurity exposure, ethical and human-centred concerns, real-time operational constraints, legacy system barriers, and limited model generalisability. In response, four strategic research directions are proposed to support the development of scalable, trustworthy, and resilient maritime digital twin ecosystems. This study contributes a structured analytical framework and critical synthesis of ship digital twin research, providing both theoretical insights and practical guidance for advancing next-generation maritime digitalisation.

metadata_records.title: Software-defined radio sensing for self-harming behaviour detection using CWT transformation and deep learning
Software-defined radio sensing for self-harming behaviour detection using CWT transformation and deep learning
metadata_records.abstract: Self-harming, prevalent among youths and adolescents, is highly linked to coping difficulties, emotional distress, trauma, and low self-esteem. Such behaviors are a serious problem as regards social well-being, mental health and emotional stability, which are detrimental to individuals, society and healthcare systems. Early detection of self-harming behavior is vital for enabling timely intervention and mitigating long-term psychological risks. In this article, we propose an intelligent human self-harming behavior detection system leveraging Software Defined Radio (SDR) signals-based non-contact platform and deep learning. The proposed system uses a multi-carrier orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) signal to extract wireless channel state information for self-harm detection. It employs the Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) to convert raw one-dimensional (1D) OFDM signals into two-dimensional (2D) spectrogram representations, enriching the feature set for deep learning models. A customised convolutional neural network (CNN) is designed to capture abrupt physical movements associated with self-harm while maintaining low computational complexity for real-time deployment. The customised CNN is rigorously evaluated against benchmark pre-trained deep learning models, including AlexNet, ResNet18, and GoogleNet, to demonstrate competitive sensitivity and specificity. Comprehensive comparisons are conducted based on performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and computational efficiency parameters. The proposed customised model achieves competitive accuracy (96%) and F1-score (94%) while being significantly more computationally efficient, requiring only 3,305,801 trainable parameters, 12.61 MB of memory, and 45.09 ms inference time.
first_author_affiliations: College of Information Technology, United Arab Emirates University, Al Ain, United Arab Emirates

metadata_records.title: Cross-dataset Transfer and Unknown-Class Detection in Imbalanced SAR Ship Classification
metadata_records.abstract: Ship classification from Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery is a critical computer vision task, yet the robustness of models under deployment shifts remains unclear. While models are often trained on one dataset and deployed on another, we lack a comprehensive understanding of their cross-dataset generalization. To address this, we evaluate six pretrained models on two SAR ship datasets in three settings: in-domain classification, cross-dataset transfer, and unknown-class detection. For unknown detection, we hold out all classes one at a time. In-domain, SARDet100K gives the best balanced accuracy on both datasets (73.4\% on FUSARShip and 53.2\% on OpenSARShip). In cross-dataset transfer, we observe strong failures: some models show moderate accuracy but near-chance balanced accuracy (for example, 64.5\% accuracy but 33.3\% balanced accuracy for OpenSARShip to FUSARShip). In unknown detection, performance depends on the held-out class and dataset, while MC-dropout variance is often close to random. These findings show that cross-dataset generalization in SAR remains limited and that task-specific uncertainty scores are often more informative than MC-dropout variance for held-out-class detection, although their relative ranking depends on the dataset and held-out class.

metadata_records.title: Explainable Failure Prediction and Prevention in Maritime
metadata_records.abstract: Maritime systems operate in highly dynamic environments where unexpected equipment failures can compromise safety, reliability, and operational efficiency. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, digital twins, and predictive maintenance enable proactive failure prediction and prevention. However, ensuring trustworthy and explainable decision-making remains a major challenge in safety-critical maritime applications. This chapter reviews key AI technologies required for explainable failure prediction and prevention in maritime systems and presents a conceptual architecture capable of supporting autonomous or human-in-the-loop corrective actions. This architecture integrates data acquisition, time-series forecasting, anomaly detection, risk assessment, decision-making, and explainable AI into a closed-loop framework. With reference to the architectural components, a review and discussion of relevant maritime studies is performed, outlining their methods, advantages, and limitations. Furthermore, it highlights current challenges, including uncertainty and robustness, model generalization, explainability, limited availability of maritime datasets, and operational deployment, and identifies future research directions toward trustworthy AI-assisted maritime decision-making.

metadata_records.title: Digital twins across the ship lifecycle: Implementation patterns, MBSE integration, and contributions to ship maintenance
metadata_records.abstract: This study aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the current technological landscape regarding Digital Twins (DT) in the shipbuilding industry, including their integration with Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) and their effects on maintenance. The maritime industry is characterized by high levels of asset complexity and long lifecycles, which often result in information gaps and a heavy reliance on reactive maintenance practices. In order to overcome these difficulties, a systematic literature review was carried out following PRISMA protocols, complemented by a scientometric analysis using VOSviewer. Following an initial search in Scopus and Web of Science, 227 relevant papers were selected, categorized, and thoroughly reviewed. The findings show a significant paradigm shift, with a move from simple condition monitoring to advanced hybrid modeling, incorporating physical principles and real-time operational data. The research, led by China, Norway, and Korea, shows that the most prominent areas of DT implementation are Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) and condition-based predictive maintenance to optimize overall efficiency. However, the findings have also confirmed the existence of significant obstacles, including inadequate standardization, poor system interoperability, highly complex modeling requirements, and substantial implementation costs. Ultimately, the research indicates the clear need to articulate a strategic roadmap for the future. Overcoming current limitations requires emphasizing the transformative potential of Digital Healthcare Engineering (DHE) and the synergy between DT and MBSE, alongside the establishment of rigorous industry standards. This strategic transition toward a fully connected, data-driven ecosystem is absolutely essential for optimizing vessel lifespans and ensuring sustainable operations.

metadata_records.title: SAR object detection via adaptive shift-wise downsampling and frequency-spatially modulated feature fusion
metadata_records.abstract: Object detection in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery is challenged by speckle noise, background clutter, and large variations in target scale. We present ASCE-SAR, a YOLO11-based detector that coordinates adaptive shift-wise downsampling with frequency-spatially modulated multi-scale fusion. In the backbone, the Adaptive Downsampling with Shift-Wise Convolution (ADSC) block combines structure-preserving downsampling and enlarged receptive-field modeling. In the neck, Dynamic Shift-wise Feature Fusion (DSFF) uses content-aware resampling and frequency-spatial modulation to improve cross-scale feature alignment and weak-target representation. On the OGSOD-1.0 and HRSID test sets, ASCE-SAR achieves AP values of 59.9% and 67.9%, respectively, corresponding to gains of 7.1 and 1.8 percentage points over the YOLO11 Baseline under the same evaluation protocol. Under synthetic Gamma speckle perturbations on HRSID, the full model retains a 0.8–2.0 percentage-point mAP \(_{50{:}95}\) advantage over the Baseline across the clean condition and the evaluated noise levels. The full model contains 3.17 M parameters and requires 14.94 GFLOPS; its profiling results are reported with forward latency and peak memory to make the accuracy-cost trade-off explicit. These results indicate improved detection accuracy and noise-perturbed performance, accompanied by a measurable computational cost.

metadata_records.title: Tracking Control of a Pan–Tilt Camera System in Maritime Search and Rescue
metadata_records.abstract: Maritime search and rescue requires target detection and tracking systems that are highly accurate and capable of achieving the shortest possible response time. Therefore, pan–tilt–zoom (PTZ) camera systems must satisfy these requirements. This study proposes an intelligent pan–tilt camera system for maritime search and rescue under conditions of fluctuating water surfaces, changing illumination, and targets that are easily obscured by waves. Previous methods mainly relied on PTZ tracking, You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8) combined with tracking algorithms, and several image enhancement techniques; however, they remained limited in terms of real–time stability and adaptability to nonlinear noise in the marine environment. In this paper, YOLOv8 is integrated for human detection, while the ByteTrack algorithm is used to maintain object identity and estimate the image–centering error. An optimized Adaptive Neuro–Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) controller is designed for the two pan–tilt axes based on red–green–blue (RGB) and thermal imaging. Experimental results in four scenarios demonstrate that the target tracking system is stable, with the error gradually decreasing to acceptable limits. The YOLOv8 model achieved a precision above 0.8, a recall of approximately 0.7–0.75, and a mean Average Precision at an Intersection over Union threshold of 0.50 (mAP@50) of approximately 0.7. In real–world testing, the pan error was reduced from –674 pixels to 5 pixels.

metadata_records.title: DAA-YOLOv8s with downsampling aware high resolution fusion for real time tiny vehicle detection in UAV imagery
metadata_records.abstract: Detecting very small vehicles in UAV imagery remains challenging due to severe scale variations, dense object distributions, diverse viewing directions, and the loss of fine-grained spatial information caused by repeated downsampling. To address these limitations, we propose DAA-YOLOv8s (Downsampling-Aware Architecture for YOLOv8s), a lightweight detection framework that explicitly preserves high-resolution spatial information for improved tiny-object localization in aerial scenes. The proposed model integrates a Multi-Receptive Field Downsampling (MRFD) module, a C2f-Partial Residual Bottleneck (C2f-PRB), and a High-Resolution Rebalanced Fusion (HRRF) neck to preserve complementary spatial cues, reduce redundant computation, and strengthen high-resolution multi-scale feature representation. By operating the detection head on \(160\times 160\) , \(80\times 80\) , and \(40\times 40\) feature maps, the framework retains fine-grained structural and boundary information that supports reliable localization of vehicles under varying viewing directions, scales, and partial occlusion. Experimental results on the VisDrone2019-DET dataset demonstrate that DAA-YOLOv8s achieves 52.70% mAP@50 and 32.20% mAP@50–95, representing improvements of 11.10 and 7.60 percentage points, respectively, over baseline YOLOv8s. At the same time, the proposed model reduces the parameter count from 11.13M to 3.29M, corresponding to a reduction of approximately 70.4%, while maintaining comparable computational complexity, with GFLOPs decreasing slightly from 28.70 to 28.60. In real-time deployment, DAA-YOLOv8s achieves an end-to-end latency of 11.8841 ms and a throughput of 84.15 FPS, exceeding the 25 FPS input stream used in the deployment experiment. These results demonstrate that the downsampling-aware design provides a favorable balance between tiny-object localization capability, model compactness, and practical real-time inference. Furthermore, DAA-YOLOv8s achieves 80.89% mAP@50 and 57.50% mAP@50–95 on the VEDAI dataset, providing additional validation on an aerial vehicle detection benchmark. Overall, the proposed framework offers an efficient architecture for tiny vehicle detection in UAV imagery, with potential applicability to real-time aerial surveillance and intelligent transportation systems.

metadata_records.title: Low-cost and robust docking angle estimation for miniature USVs through the integration of camera and multi-zone ToF sensor
metadata_records.abstract: Autonomous docking of miniature unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) requires compact, low-cost, and robust sensing for estimating angles within short ranges. To fulfill these requirements, this work presents a dual-sensing strategy that combines a camera and an 8 × 8 multi-zone time-of-flight (ToF) sensor. In this strategy, the camera-based method can estimate the docking angle through calibrated AprilTag pose estimation, while the ToF-based method can derive angular information from column-wise range gradients. Experiments covering 20–80 cm and 10°–50° demonstrate that both methods can achieve reliable angle estimation, with an overall mean absolute error (MAE) of angle below 1.5°. The results further show complementary performance of the proposed design: ToF sensing is more stable at small angles while camera-based estimation performs better at larger angles. Moreover, experiments validate the robustness and practical use of the proposed system under varying illumination scenarios.

To fulfill these requirements, this work presents a dual-sensing strategy that combines a camera and an 8 × 8 multi-zone time-of-flight (ToF) sensor. In this strategy, the camera-based method can estimate the docking angle through calibrated AprilTag pose estimation, while the ToF-based method can derive angular information from column-wise range gradients. Experiments covering 20–80 cm and 10°–50° demonstrate that both methods can achieve reliable angle estimation, with an overall mean absolute error (MAE) of angle below 1.5°. The results further show complementary performance of the proposed design: ToF sensing is more stable at small angles while camera-based estimation performs better at larger angles. Moreover, experiments validate the robustness and practical use of the proposed system under varying illumination scenarios.

metadata_records.title: Review of Applications, Technologies and Future Trends of Maritime UAV Systems for Smart Ocean Operations
metadata_records.abstract: Maritime unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly transforming ocean, coastal, port, and offshore operations through rapid sensing, intelligent communication, autonomous perception, and cooperative decision support. This trend-oriented review analyses 471 peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2020 and March 2026, supported by selected foundational pre-2020 studies, to examine the evolution, technological structure, methodological maturity, and deployment readiness of maritime UAV systems. The bibliometric analysis shows rapid publication growth, from 22 papers in 2020 to 160 in 2025, and identifies five interconnected research clusters centred on maritime communications and networking; artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled perception, surveillance, and search and rescue; navigation and cooperative operations; distributed and federated intelligence; and multi-agent autonomous systems. The literature further shows a transition from task-specific aerial monitoring toward integrated maritime cyber–physical systems combining UAVs with vessels, unmanned surface vehicles (USVs), unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs), edge computing, next-generation communication networks, digital twins, and AI-enabled decision support. However, evidence maturity remains uneven: many AI, communication, optimisation, and cooperative-autonomy methods are still evaluated predominantly using datasets or simulation, while fewer studies provide integrated system-level evidence under representative maritime conditions. The review therefore advocates a layered validation strategy combining high-fidelity scenario-based simulation, hardware-in-the-loop testing, controlled experiments, and representative maritime trials, with traceability between simulated and observed system behaviour. Deployment readiness additionally depends on environmental robustness, interoperability, cybersecurity, energy feasibility, human oversight, maintainability, and regulatory assurance. The review therefore proposes an evidence-gated roadmap to progress maritime UAV technologies from promising algorithms and prototypes to reliable, operationally deployable smart-ocean systems.

metadata_records.title: SOTIF‐Oriented Perception Uncertainty Analysis and Risk‐Aware Sensor Layout Optimization for Autonomous Navigation System
metadata_records.abstract: ABSTRACT Maritime autonomous surface ships (MASS) rely on multi‐sensory perception systems to detect navigation obstacles, but design and performance limitations may cause safety of the intended functionality (SOTIF) issues even when no component failure occurs. This study proposes a SOTIF‐oriented framework integrating perception uncertainty analysis, collision‐risk assessment, and sensor layout optimization. First, a scenario‐function‐architecture framework is established to identify perception‐related SOTIF issues and formulate quantitative requirements. Second, sensor detection probabilities and state‐estimation uncertainties are modeled and evaluated at the multi‐sensor architecture level. Third, an ellipse‐based deformable safety envelope provides a spatial reference for multi‐ship collision risk assessment, with fused range, bearing, and relative‐speed uncertainties incorporated into the risk indicator. Sensor positions and orientations are optimized to maximize coverage within a fixed reference region under detection performance and measurement error constraints for daytime and nighttime conditions. A synthetic encounter scenario involving ten ships illustrates the envelope evolution and the prescribed response of the risk indicator to perception uncertainty. Across five independent optimization runs, the mean combined coverage was 68.49%, with a sample standard deviation of 0.02% points, compared with 67.89% for a fixed heuristic layout. The selected configuration achieved daytime and nighttime coverage of 74.45% and 62.56%, respectively. These results illustrate the application of the framework to sensor‐configuration evaluation under the adopted SOTIF‐oriented perception constraints.

metadata_records.title: MarVAIS: A Dataset of Paired Video and AIS Telemetry for Coastal Maritime Monitoring under Adverse Weather Conditions
metadata_records.abstract: Title: MarVAIS: A Dataset of Paired Video and AIS Telemetry for Coastal Maritime Monitoring under Adverse Weather Conditions Abstract: This dataset provides synchronized monocular video recordings and Automatic Identification System (AIS) telemetry designed to support maritime domain awareness and object detection research. It is specifically built for the development, validation, and benchmarking of computer vision models (such as YOLO architectures), digital twins, and hybrid tracking systems aimed at identifying collaborative and non-collaborative vessels in coastal regions. Dataset Contents: Due to the large file sizes, the physical dataset is securely hosted on an external cloud (Google Drive). The dataset consists of: Video Data: 40 minutes of continuous footage, divided into 4 individual video sequences of 10 minutes each. All videos are recorded in Full HD (1920x1080 pixels) at 30 frames per second (FPS), yielding approximately 72,000 frames. Each sequence represents distinct environmental and lighting challenges to test model robustness: Clear Weather: Provides high-visibility baselines for accurate bounding box regression and classification. Fog: Challenges contour detection and tracking algorithms due to atmospheric scattering. Rain: Introduces visual artifacts, sensor noise, and partial occlusion of distant targets. Late Afternoon: Tests the impact of fading illumination, shadows, and color space degradation. Synchronized AIS Telemetry: 4 tabular CSV files containing the raw AIS messages corresponding to each video. The timestamps have been converted to a relative video time format (00:00:00) to facilitate immediate synchronization for sensor fusion algorithms. The data includes MMSI, Latitude, Longitude, and Distance. Access Conditions & Request Requirements: Due to the file sizes and the restricted nature of this maritime data, the actual video and CSV files are not available for direct download on Zenodo. This Zenodo record contains only a placeholder ReadMe file. Access to the external Google Drive folder will only be granted for academic and non-commercial research purposes. To request access, you must use the Zenodo "Request Access" button and explicitly provide the following information in the justification box: Full Name Institutional Affiliation (University, Research Institute, or Company) Purpose of Use (Briefly explain your research goals and how you intend to use this dataset) Google Account E-mail (Strictly required to grant you restricted reader permission to the Google Drive folder) Note: Requests missing any of these four fields will be automatically declined. metadata_records.title: Team cognition in remote maritime operations: a scoping review and cross-domain theoretical synthesis
metadata_records.abstract: Introduction Remote maritime operations increasingly depend on complex, distributed socio-technical systems in which safe and effective performance relies on team cognition rather than on individual decision-making alone. Despite its importance, the conceptualisation and measurement of team cognition in this domain remain fragmented and underdeveloped. Methods A scoping review was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Searches of SCOPUS, Web of Science, and EBSCOhost yielded 162 records, of which 51 publications (35 journal articles and 16 conference proceedings, published between 2010 and 2025) were included after screening, retrieval assessment, and expert recommendation. The included publications were thematically analysed using a hybrid deductive-inductive approach. Results Five themes emerged: (1) situation awareness and its measurement and modelling, (2) collective team cognition, learning, and training, (3) human-autonomy teaming and remote collaboration, (4) visualisation and interface design for shared cognition, and (5) maritime applications of distributed cognition. The evidence demonstrates a shift from static, individual-based models toward dynamic, interaction-driven, and system-level accounts, in which team cognition arises from ongoing interactions among human agents, technical artefacts, and environmental constraints. Discussion The findings indicate that shared and distributed situation awareness is central to coordination and safety in remote maritime operations. Key challenges include integrating autonomous systems, designing interfaces that support distributed sensemaking, and reliably measuring team cognition. Enhancing remote maritime safety requires aligning design, training, and regulatory frameworks with the principles of distributed cognition. Future research should prioritise longitudinal and intervention-based validation in real-world operational contexts.

metadata_records.title: Protecting Ports using Range-Free Triangulated Sensor Networks: A Case Study
metadata_records.abstract: Range-free wireless sensor networks rely on sensors that detect only the bearing of an incoming signal, so that localizing a transmitter requires simultaneous detection by at least three sensors, a condition known as triangulated coverage. This paper extends a previously developed geospatial computational framework with a formal treatment of sensor activation and applies it to the protection of the port of Thessaloniki, Greece. Eleven sensors, in the presence of seven known transmitters that induce angular blind zones, monitor four areas of interest that form successive protection layers: the dock, the gulf, the maritime passage, and the adjacent airport zone. We formulate the protection of several areas as a constrained combinatorial optimization problem over sensor activations and orientations, and present a group-based activation strategy, stated as an explicit algorithm, which restricts the problem to a feasible subset, determined by the geography of the deployment. Each group of sensors is oriented towards its nearest area, and neighboring sensors reinforce it only when coverage is insufficient. We further prove that the blind zones induced by the transmitters are invariant under rotation of a sensor’s field of view, so that the reachable set of the sensors yields a computable upper bound on the coverage that is attainable by any configuration of the network. We also show that the triangulated coverage ratio of an area is exactly the probability of detecting and localizing a new transmitter that is equally likely to appear anywhere in it. All four areas of interest achieve high triangulated coverage. The proposed group-based activation strategy is a practical, transparent, and computationally cost-effective approach to the protection of critical infrastructures.

metadata_records.title: PORTIA: A Large-Scale Port Acoustic Dataset with AIS-Grounded Annotations for AI-Based Vessel Monitoring
metadata_records.abstract: Monitoring underwater anthropogenic noise in busy commercial ports is critical for marine spatial planning, yet the development of AI-based tools is often limited by the scarcity of large-scale, annotated acoustic datasets from realistic high-traffic environments. We present PORTIA, a passive acoustic dataset collected over a 26-day campaign in the Port of Valencia, Spain. It comprises 260,932 three-second audio windows paired with synchronized Automatic Identification System (AIS) metadata. To facilitate direct reuse, we provide three task-oriented benchmarks: a Binary Detection subset (36,148 samples), a Single-Vessel Classification subset (39,125 samples), and a Multi-Label Monitoring subset (34,996 samples) explicitly designed to handle concurrent acoustic scenes and source proximity. All benchmarks were constructed using Maritime Mobile Service Identity (MMSI)-aware splitting to prevent identity leakage across partitions and utilized stratified sampling to preserve representative vessel-class distributions while remaining manageable for research. PORTIA serves as a realistic benchmark for vessel detection, typological classification, and proximity estimation in dense Mediterranean port soundscapes.

metadata_records.title: A framework for understanding automatic identification system (AIS) manipulation: purposes, goals, and strategies
metadata_records.abstract: Abstract There is increasing attention paid to the manipulation of ships’ Automatic Identification System (AIS) signals, with implications for maritime safety, law enforcement, and security. Based on the literature and narrative reports, this paper proposes a framework that answers why and when ships engage in AIS manipulations by tracing the purpose, goals, and strategies of their operators. Drawing from the academic literature and narrative reports on AIS manipulation cases by different countries’ shadow fleets, warships, fishing vessels, maritime pirates, and commercial vessels engaged in legitimate transits, the paper argues that AIS manipulation can be used to shield ships from both legitimate and illegitimate maritime actors by engaging in deception and denial through concealment and deterrence. Ships seeking protection from legitimate maritime actors while engaging in illegal activities are likely to use spoofing and falsification strategies, as well as strategies that strategically or intermittently drop the AIS signal. States seeking protection from hostile maritime actors (both legitimate and illegitimate), as they carry out legal activities, are likely to use both disruption strategies and strategic dropping of their AIS signals. This paper has implications for policies implemented by the shipping industry, maritime authorities, and regional and global networks. Effectively addressing AIS manipulation requires a multi-pronged approach that combines regulatory reform, stronger enforcement, technological solutions, and enhanced international cooperation and information sharing.

metadata_records.title: Smart Port Technologies: A Scoping Review
metadata_records.abstract: The maritime industry is undergoing a profound digital transformation, with smart ports emerging as critical nodes in global supply chains. This comprehensive literature review synthesizes current research on key enabling technologies for smart ports, including Digital Twins, Blockchain, Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things (IoT), Computer Vision, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), automation systems, and cybersecurity frameworks. This review identifies major technological trends, applications, benefits, challenges, and future research directions. The findings reveal that smart port technologies cluster around five core pillars: (1) Digital Twin, (2) Blockchain and Distributed Ledger, (3) Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics, (4) IoT, 5G, and Connectivity Infrastructure, (5) Computer Vision, UAVs, and Sensing for Smart Ports, and (6) Automation, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems. Cross-cutting themes emphasize the need for interoperability standards, human-centric research, and empirical deployment evaluations. Research gaps include limited empirical studies of real-world implementations, insufficient attention to workforce impacts, and lack of standardized frameworks for technology integration. This review provides a comprehensive foundation for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers working toward the realization of fully autonomous, sustainable, and efficient smart ports

metadata_records.title: A review of corrosion behavior of alloys in Arctic, Antarctic and cold regions: key factors, knowledge gaps, and the emerging role of metal additive manufacturing
metadata_records.abstract: The increasing strategic and economic importance of the Earth’s polar regions has created a growing need for metallic infrastructure that can withstand prolonged exposure to severe cold. Corrosion is an important factor affecting the reliability and service life of metallic components in these environments. Although the corrosion behavior of conventionally-manufactured alloys under cold-region conditions has been investigated through both field and laboratory studies, an integrated review covering these findings while considering the emerging application of metal additive manufacturing (MAM) is still lacking. This review examines the available literature on atmospheric and marine immersion corrosion of alloys in Arctic, Antarctic, and other cold environments, with particular attention to environmental and metallurgical factors such as chloride deposition, time of wetness, freeze-thaw cycling, and alloy microstructure. It also discusses powder bed fusion (PBF) and directed energy deposition (DED) as MAM technologies with potential for producing corrosion-resistant components for cold-region service. Particular emphasis is placed on the limited understanding of the relationship between MAM-induced microstructural features and corrosion performance at low temperatures. The major knowledge gaps are identified, and key research directions are proposed to support further development of corrosion science and additive manufacturing for polar applications.

metadata_records.title: A Survey of Computer Vision Applications in Industrial Environments
metadata_records.abstract: In recent years, Computer Vision (CV) has evolved rapidly, enabling enhanced automation, safety, inspection, and logistics across manufacturing, construction, and robotics. This systematic review surveys current computer vision applications in industrial environments, spanning factory defect inspection, construction-site safety, warehouse inventory tracking, and industrial robotics. From more than 8,700 initially identified studies, we selected 146 key papers representing cross-domain CV applications. The survey is organized into four thematic areas: visual inspection and defect detection, worker safety and monitoring, inventory and logistics tracking, and robotics and automation. For each area, we compare state-of-the-art approaches, datasets, and deployment settings while highlighting the factors that influence their performance under different operating conditions. For example, YOLO-based detectors dominate real-time edge deployment because of their high throughput, whereas transformer-based models often struggle to scale in resource-constrained environments despite their superior feature extraction capabilities. We also identify critical research gaps. Although manufacturing and construction benefit from numerous public datasets for quality inspection and safety monitoring, warehousing and robotics continue to lack large-scale, real-world benchmark datasets. Finally, we discuss emerging research directions, including domain adaptation, edge AI, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), to support the development of more robust, scalable, and balanced computer vision solutions for industrial applications.

metadata_records.title: Формування інноваційного потенціалу озброєння та військової техніки з урахуванням сучасних технологічних трендів
metadata_records.abstract: The article examines contemporary approaches to developing the innovation potential of armament and military equipment (AME) under the conditions of rapid technological transformation and the evolution of multi-domain warfare. Based on an analysis of NATO strategic documents, particularly the NATO Science & Technology Trends 2023–2043 reports, the study explores the role of Emerging and Disruptive Technologies (EDTs) in shaping future defense capabilities. A clear distinction is made between the concepts of priority technological domains and innovative technological trends, enabling the integration of fundamental scientific and technological research with the practical requirements of AME development and defense capability planning. The paper proposes a conceptual methodology for formalizing technological trends through the interaction of NATO priority technology areas, operational domains, current security challenges, and the defense capabilities required to address them. The proposed model describes the transformation of fundamental technologies into specific directions for the development of armament and military equipment under the influence of real operational challenges. It can serve as a practical analytical tool for forecasting military technological development, supporting military-technical policy, and facilitating decision-making within the defense planning process. The applicability of the proposed methodology is demonstrated across five operational domains: land, air, maritime, cyberspace, and space. Representative operational use cases are presented for each domain, illustrating current global trends in the development of advanced military capabilities. These include robotic combat and logistics platforms, intelligent active protection systems, connected soldier technologies, collaborative combat aircraft, autonomous drone swarms, hypersonic strike systems, autonomous surface and underwater platforms, artificial intelligence-based cyber defense, post-quantum cryptography, proliferated low Earth orbit satellite constellations, and space domain awareness systems. For each case, the interaction between priority technology areas, operational challenges, technological solutions, and the resulting defense capabilities is analyzed. Particular attention is devoted to the practical implementation of the proposed approach within Ukraine's military-technical policy framework. The study substantiates the principle of selective technological integration, according to which global technological achievements should be adapted to national defense needs rather than attempting to replicate the entire spectrum of fundamental research. Such an approach enables more efficient utilization of limited national resources, accelerates the integration of advanced technologies into domestic weapon systems, and supports the rapid development of critical defense capabilities required for modern multi-domain operations. The findings provide a comprehensive scientific and methodological foundation for improving defense planning, strengthening military-technical policy, and identifying long-term priorities for the development of armament and military equipment in Ukraine. The proposed conceptual model may serve as an analytical framework for forecasting future technological trends, supporting capability-based defense planning, and ensuring the technological superiority and resilience of Ukraine's Defense Forces in current and future conflicts.

A clear distinction is made between the concepts of priority technological domains and innovative technological trends, enabling the integration of fundamental scientific and technological research with the practical requirements of AME development and defense capability planning. The paper proposes a conceptual methodology for formalizing technological trends through the interaction of NATO priority technology areas, operational domains, current security challenges, and the defense capabilities required to address them. The proposed model describes the transformation of fundamental technologies into specific directions for the development of armament and military equipment under the influence of real operational challenges. It can serve as a practical analytical tool for forecasting military technological development, supporting military-technical policy, and facilitating decision-making within the defense planning process. The applicability of the proposed methodology is demonstrated across five operational domains: land, air, maritime, cyberspace, and space. Representative operational use cases are presented for each domain, illustrating current global trends in the development of advanced military capabilities. These include robotic combat and logistics platforms, intelligent active protection systems, connected soldier technologies, collaborative combat aircraft, autonomous drone swarms, hypersonic strike systems, autonomous surface and underwater platforms, artificial intelligence-based cyber defense, post-quantum cryptography, proliferated low Earth orbit satellite constellations, and space domain awareness systems. For each case, the interaction between priority technology areas, operational challenges, technological solutions, and the resulting defense capabilities is analyzed. Particular attention is devoted to the practical implementation of the proposed approach within Ukraine's military-technical policy framework. The study substantiates the principle of selective technological integration, according to which global technological achievements should be adapted to national defense needs rather than attempting to replicate the entire spectrum of fundamental research. Such an approach enables more efficient utilization of limited national resources, accelerates the integration of advanced technologies into domestic weapon systems, and supports the rapid development of critical defense capabilities required for modern multi-domain operations. The findings provide a comprehensive scientific and methodological foundation for improving defense planning, strengthening military-technical policy, and identifying long-term priorities for the development of armament and military equipment in Ukraine. The proposed conceptual model may serve as an analytical framework for forecasting future technological trends, supporting capability-based defense planning, and ensuring the technological superiority and resilience of Ukraine's Defense Forces in current and future conflicts.

metadata_records.title: Toward interoperable bathymetric data in ocean observing systems: integrating hydrographic standards and FAIR data practices
metadata_records.abstract: Bathymetric data are a fundamental component of ocean observing systems, supporting applications in ocean modelling, coastal hazard assessment, marine spatial planning, and navigational safety. However, these datasets remain highly fragmented due to the diversity of acquisition platforms, including hydrographic surveys, autonomous vehicles, satellite-derived bathymetry, and legacy chart products, which often differ in spatial reference systems, vertical datums, resolution scales, and metadata quality. This heterogeneity creates persistent barriers to interoperability, limiting data integration and reuse across ocean science and operational applications. This review examines best practices for improving bathymetric data interoperability within ocean observing systems by integrating hydrographic standards and FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) data principles. It synthesizes hydrographic measurement standards, quality assurance procedures, and spatial data processing techniques such as georeferencing, interpolation, digital bathymetric model generation, and uncertainty quantification. The review also evaluates FAIR implementation in bathymetric workflows, identifying gaps in metadata consistency, provenance tracking, and cross-platform compatibility. By linking hydrographic standards with FAIR practices, it highlights key barriers to seamless data integration, including inconsistent vertical datum usage, fragmented infrastructures, and uneven adoption of standardized protocols. Mapping the clauses of these standards onto the fifteen FAIR sub-principles shows that hydrographic standardisation already satisfies the reusability conditions demandingly, through mandatory paired depth and uncertainty encoding and quantified survey-order thresholds, while leaving findability largely unaddressed: identifiers specified by IHO S-100 are unique within an exchange set but not globally resolvable. Interoperability is met at the level of encoding but not of semantics, since the authoritative vocabulary of the domain is not published as dereferenceable identifiers. The review concludes that the binding constraint on bathymetric interoperability is not the absence of standards but the absence of machine-resolvable linkage between them, and that vertical-datum heterogeneity remains the barrier least tractable to specification alone.

translation.zh: 测深数据是海洋观测系统的一个基本组成部分,支持海洋建模、沿海灾害评估、海洋空间规划和航行安全方面的应用。 然而,由于获取平台的多样性,包括水文测量、自主飞行器、卫星测深和遗留图表产品,这些数据集仍然高度零散,在空间参考系统、垂直基准、分辨率尺度和元数据质量方面往往有所不同。 这种异质性为互操作性制造了持久的障碍,限制了数据集成和跨海洋科学和业务应用的再利用. 本次审查审查了通过将水文标准与海洋观测系统相结合改进海洋观测系统内测深数据互操作性的最佳做法。 FAIR (可查找,可访问,互操作,可再使用)数据原理. 它综合了水文测量标准,质量保证程序,以及地理参照,内插,数字测深模型生成,不确定性量化等空间数据处理技术. 审查还评价 FAIR 在测深工作流程中实施,找出元数据一致性、来源跟踪和跨平台兼容性方面的差距。 将水文标准与 FAIR 它强调了实现无缝数据整合的主要障碍,包括纵向基准使用不一致、基础设施支离破碎以及标准化协议的采用不均衡。 将这些标准的条款划入15个 FAIR 次级原则表明,水文标准化已经通过强制性的配对深度和不确定性编码以及量化的勘测顺序阈值,严格地满足了重复使用的条件,同时使可找到性基本上得不到解决: IHO S-100 在一个交换集中是独一无二的,但不能在全球范围解决。 互操作性在编码层面得到满足,但在语义层面则没有实现,因为域的权威词汇不作为可调试的标识符发布. 审查结论认为,对测深互操作性的约束性限制不是缺乏标准,而是它们之间缺乏机器可解决的联系,纵向-直肠异质性仍然是仅凭规格就最难理解的障碍。.

metadata_records.title: A Knowledge Graph-Based Question Answering System for Marine Diesel Engine Fault Diagnosis Integrating Intent Recognition and Named Entity Recognition
metadata_records.abstract: Abstract To address the challenges of knowledge acquisition and low information utilization efficiency in marine diesel engine fault diagnosis, this paper proposes a question answering system integrating intent recognition and named entity recognition. First, a domain-specific knowledge graph for marine diesel engine faults is constructed to achieve the structured representation of multi-source fault knowledge. In the semantic understanding module, RoBERTa-WWM is employed for intent recognition, and a RW-BiLSTM-SD-CRF (RoBERTa-WWM-BiLSTM-SDPA-CRF) model is proposed for named entity recognition to enhance entity extraction performance under complex semantic contexts. Based on semantic parsing, Cypher query statements are automatically generated and executed on the Neo4j graph database for knowledge retrieval and system deployment. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed named entity recognition model achieves an F1-score of 92.19%, while the end-to-end accuracy of the question answering system reaches 90%. The proposed system effectively integrates dispersed fault knowledge and provides technical support for intelligent operation and maintenance of marine diesel engines.

metadata_records.title: From track to impact: a review of multi-hazard typhoon forecasting and resilience
metadata_records.abstract: While recent advancements in tropical cyclone prediction have been extensively documented, existing review literature remains heavily fragmented into isolated academic domains, such as artificial intelligence, data assimilation, or coastal hydrodynamics. This fragmentation obscures the operational reality of disaster risk reduction. To address this critical gap, this paper presents a transdisciplinary systematic review of the entire end-to-end climate service value chain. First, the examination of the paradigm shift in atmospheric modeling, contrasting traditional Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) with the rapid emergence of pure deep learning and AI-physics hybrid frameworks. Second, the evaluation of multi-platform observational networks and the integration of Interpretable AI (XAI) for operational trust. Third, the bridging of the “scale gap” by analyzing how synoptic meteorological forcing is dynamically coupled with high-resolution hydrodynamic models to predict secondary hazards and compound extremes. Fourth, the review of the translation of these physical hazards into micro-scale structural engineering impacts. Finally, the synthesis of these domains into the framework of socio-economic Impact-Based Forecasting (IBF) and Forecast-based Financing (FbF). Ultimately, this review establishes that advancing modern typhoon resilience requires moving beyond isolated computational superiority toward a unified convergence of atmospheric physics, civil engineering, and user-centric climate services.

Second, the evaluation of multi-platform observational networks and the integration of Interpretable AI (XAI) for operational trust. Third, the bridging of the “scale gap” by analyzing how synoptic meteorological forcing is dynamically coupled with high-resolution hydrodynamic models to predict secondary hazards and compound extremes. Fourth, the review of the translation of these physical hazards into micro-scale structural engineering impacts. Finally, the synthesis of these domains into the framework of socio-economic Impact-Based Forecasting (IBF) and Forecast-based Financing (FbF). Ultimately, this review establishes that advancing modern typhoon resilience requires moving beyond isolated computational superiority toward a unified convergence of atmospheric physics, civil engineering, and user-centric climate services.

metadata_records.title: Using machine learning effectively in marine benthic ecology: a question-driven toolkit
metadata_records.abstract: Abstract Manual annotation of marine image datasets is time-consuming, driving interest in machine learning (ML) to automate image analysis. However, benthic ecologists often lack the expertise needed to determine when and how ML can be applied effectively to their datasets. To explore the practical use of ML in benthic ecology, user perceptions and model training experiences were collected during a workshop. RootPainter, an interactive, corrective-annotation ML software, was used to introduce ML concepts and workflows. Participants developed models to segment benthic organisms from time-lapse and remotely operated vehicle imagery. Real-time feedback during training improved efficiency and understanding of model behaviour. Pre- and post-project qualitative surveys identified ecological and technical factors influencing model performance. From these findings, we propose five questions to guide efficient, robust annotation of marine benthic images for ML model development: (i) ‘do you have expert taxonomic and machine learning knowledge?’; (ii) ‘what is your ecological research question?’; (iii) ‘is the species sufficiently abundant?’; (iv) ‘are you consistent in your selection of training data?’; and (v) ‘have you anticipated the strengths and limitations of your imaging tool?’. Responses to these questions can provide practical guidance to help marine ecologists make informed choices, accelerate model training and improve performance.

metadata_records.title: The Fortified Disposition, Part I: Strategic Complexes, Historical Attenuation, and the Return of the Guarded City
metadata_records.abstract: Fortification is better understood as a movement-slowing strategic complex than as a wall that either holds or fails. This paper traces the long attenuation of that disposition in the West, then shows how scarce manpower, costly platforms and persistent surveillance are bringing it back—first of all in the guarded, closable city assembled through dual-use fabric, regulation and urban air defence.

metadata_records.title: Hammers and Nails: Military Innovation as a Strategic Dead End
metadata_records.abstract: This article argues that contemporary Western military innovation has become a strategic dead end. Tracing the evolution of military innovation from the Revolution in Military Affairs through counterinsurgency adaptation to today’s emphasis on disruptive innovation, experimentation and artificial intelligence, it shows how technological change has increasingly become an end in itself. This technological determinism encourages governments and armed forces to substitute innovation for difficult choices about political purpose, force structure, industrial capacity and mobilisation. Growing dependence on private technology companies further constrains strategic autonomy. The challenge, therefore, is not whether militaries should innovate, but how innovation can be subordinated to strategy.

metadata_records.title: The Golden Dome, Missile Defenses and Deterrence
metadata_records.abstract: This article examines the Trump administration proposal for a Golden Dome missile defense system in terms of its implications for technology, strategy and U.S. national security policy. It also considers whether the proposed missile defense system, once having been deployed, will support deterrence as we now understand it, or require a rethinking of past assumptions about nuclear-strategic stability.

metadata_records.title: Tropical Bastions: It’s Time for a Pacific Bastion Strategy in the First Island Chain
metadata_records.abstract: This article proposes an operational approach to the use of naval forces in the first island chain of the Pacific vis-à-vis the threat of the People’s Liberation Army Navy of China and its attempts to enforce the nine-dash line. It argues that geography, deception, and mobility, particularly in the Philippine Archipelago, offer policy makers and military planners opportunity for the employment of naval forces in natural inland sea bastions. It also affords the opportunity for more security cooperation with the U.S. ally the Republic of the Philippines. Additionally, this approach informs both deterrence and presence in the Western Pacific Area of Operations for Pacific Command (PACOM).

metadata_records.title: Strategy and Contradiction: Towards a Theory of Strategic Judgement
metadata_records.abstract: Strategy is commonly concerned with relating political purposes to the means available for their achievement. This article asks a prior question: what conditions make strategic judgement necessary in the first place? It argues that strategic problems arise from the contradictory character of political life, in which competing purposes cannot be permanently reconciled, and every decision alters the circumstances confronting those that follow. Strategy therefore requires practical judgement rather than the application of predetermined solutions. Drawing upon Clausewitz and examining deterrence, alliances and insurgency, the article conceives strategy as an inherently recursive practice directed towards accommodating, rather than eliminating, political contradiction.

metadata_records.abstract: This article warns Western democracies against committing the Carthaginian error, that is, not taking a strategic rival seriously. It argues strategic rivals should be dealt with through a grand strategy of Outpacing, the aim of which is to establish a lead over them severe enough to cause their political and economic collapse, or their forfeiture of the competition.

metadata_records.title: Real-time and online fatigue assessment of metallic structures: A review and transferability assessment for mobile working machines
metadata_records.abstract: Fatigue damage limits the service life of metallic structures, including mobile working machines. Fatigue information available during operation can support monitoring, maintenance, and control. Deployment of fatigue monitoring is challenging under complex loading, limited sensing, and harsh environments. To the authors’ knowledge, this is the first scoping review of real-time and online fatigue-assessment approaches for metallic structures that examines their transferability to mobile working machines. An active-learning tool and large language models supported screening, extraction, and preliminary synthesis, with eligibility and final synthesis determined by the authors. Direct evidence for mobile working machines remains limited, as most of the 55 included studies originate from other engineering domains. Nonlinear damage accumulation and load-sequence effects were not addressed in damage-accumulation approaches, model updating was uncommon, and uncertainty was rarely propagated to the fatigue output. Practical requirements derived from the characteristics of mobile working machines and the authors’ engineering experience identified load-carrying structures and welded details under variable or stochastic loading as the most relevant reference cases. For machine-level monitoring, damage-accumulation approaches appear more directly compatible than crack-growth approaches, as they can use stress or strain histories estimated from limited sensing. As the review’s specific contribution, an idealised solution variant is proposed, combining virtual or indirect response estimation from minimum sensing with lifetime model updating, uncertainty-aware damage-accumulation-based fatigue assessment accounting for nonlinear effects, and onboard utilisation at update intervals matched to intended use. The hierarchical classification of the reviewed methods can also help define the scope of future systematic reviews.

metadata_records.title: The Role of High-Power Microwave Weapons in Modern Warfare
metadata_records.abstract: This book is the result of Dr. Latha Christie's deep understanding of high-power microwave devices, acquired over several decades, and her excellent ability to analyse and present a difficult subject in a comprehensive and convincing manner. The timing of this book is highly appropriate, as the character of warfare is rapidly evolving towards contactless, non-lethal capabilities that minimise human casualties and collateral damage. I recommend this book as a valuable resource not only for engineers, scholars and students, but also for defence analysts, military planners and all those interested in understanding The Role of High-Power Microwave Weapons in Modern Warfare in its totality. Prof. Lalit Kumar, BITS Pilani; formerly Chairman, CEPTAM, DRDO, New Delhi, and Director, MTRDC, DRDO, Bengaluru, India Key Features: Covers HPM source classes (relativistic, vacuum/vircator, NLTL/solid-state, gyro-devices), emission mechanisms and coupling into targets, providing a unified and detailed treatment. Presents a five-subsystem view (energy storage → pulsed-power → HV switching → source generation → emission & coupling) and follows through to antenna/coupling, EMC/EMI, measurement, test protocols and system integration—bridging component physics to fieldable capability. Uses concrete case studies and documented demonstrations (CHAMP, THOR and allied trials) to translate effects science into mission planning for counter-UAV, base and shipboard protection, expeditionary concepts and space/airborne options. Provides checklists, hardening and mitigation techniques, vulnerability trade-offs and test procedures to support acquisition, operations and sustainment teams. Addresses attribution, export-control/dual-use concerns and arms-control implications and concludes with an explicit research agenda to guide funders, policymakers and think tanks.

metadata_records.title: Product lifecycle management 5.0: a systematic literature review on human-centric, resilient, and sustainable systems
metadata_records.abstract: Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) is increasingly expected to support Industry 5.0 (I5.0) by enabling human-centric, resilient, and sustainable manufacturing systems. However, current research remains fragmented across technologies, lifecycle phases, functionalities, and value dimensions. This paper addresses this gap through a systematic literature review of 141 contributions at the intersection of PLM and I5.0, classified according to nine analytical dimensions. The findings show that resilience is the most frequent primary pillar, followed by human-centricity and sustainability; that human-centric PLM remains mainly concentrated in the Beginning-of-Life phase; and that End-of-Life applications are still limited across all pillars. Document management, configuration management, and product traceability emerge as transversal PLM functionalities, while Big Data Analytics and Simulation are the dominant technological enablers. The study contributes by synthesizing the literature into Human-Centric, Resilient, and Sustainable PLM and by proposing a PLM 5.0 conceptual framework that maps I5.0 capabilities across lifecycle phases, highlighting gaps in social sustainability, circular End-of-Life strategies, and integrated multi-pillar implementations.

2610.07499.title: Source-Learned Reliance for Selective Test-Time Adaptation of Multimodal Time Series
2610.07499.abstract: Multimodal wearable systems must remain reliable when sensor streams become noisy or unavailable. Existing multimodal test-time adaptation (TTA) methods often assess reliability online, but cross-modal agreement can be misleading when sensors measure different physical processes, and evaluating alternative modality configurations adds inference cost. We propose CARAT, which decouples model reliance from runtime corruption detection to guide omission or attenuation, amortizing reliance estimation through source training. An asymmetric modality-dropout curriculum prepares a missingness-resilient backbone for omission and derives a frozen, backbone-specific reliance proxy from windowed input-projection gradient norms. At deployment, a lightweight one-class detector flags suspect streams, and the proxy guides a joint choice between replacing the suspect set with the backbone's trained missingness symbol and attenuating its representations before fusion, without candidate-subset evaluation. Across four wearable datasets, five corruption types, three backbones, and eight TTA baselines, CARAT achieves the highest overall macro-F1 and best mean rank (2.42), exceeding EATA, the strongest baseline, by 1.58 F1 points across 12 equally weighted dataset-backbone settings. Across five profiled configurations, CARAT uses 9.49% fewer GFLOPs and updates 47.82% fewer parameters than EATA. A pattern also emerges across sensing regimes: multimodal TTA methods such as PTA are competitive on IMU-dominated homogeneous datasets, whereas unimodal TTA methods like TENT and EATA match or exceed it on heterogeneous datasets. These results position CARAT as a practical default to wearable TTA, offering competitive robustness with modest computational requirements and benefits that vary across backbones and dataset regimes.

2610.07340.title: CausalBind: Causal Modeling and Learning for Protein-Molecule Virtual Screening
2610.07340.abstract: Protein-molecule virtual screening is increasingly cast as a problem of representation learning in a shared embedding space. Existing methods rely on dense holistic alignment, entangling invariant binding determinants with nuisance correlations and limiting transfer to new targets. It has been noted that binding in protein-molecule systems involves sparse cross-modality interactions: binding is governed by a small contact interface and a few decisive local interactions (e.g., hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic contacts, and salt bridges) rather than the global structures of the protein and molecule. We hypothesize that uncovering and leveraging sparse interaction patterns is critical for generalization beyond the training data, as these patterns are reusable and expected to improve performance across different scenarios. In this paper, we aim to identify and leverage sparse interaction patterns, and verify our hypothesis. Since the training data contain only observed binding pairs, we formalize this prior via a V-structure causal model under Heckman-style selection, and establish three theoretical results: (i) the latent concepts of interacting proteins and molecules are not identifiable without appropriate sparsity constraints; (ii) these concepts and their sparse interactions are component-wise identifiable under structural sparsity conditions; and (iii) a low-rank relaxation of these conditions yields subspace identifiability of the concepts and interactions. Inspired by these principles, we propose CausalBind with three implementation variants. Extensive experiments on DUD-E and LIT-PCBA benchmarks show that all variants consistently outperform strong retrieval baselines, with the largest gains on LIT-PCBA early enrichment, and further generalize to target- and scaffold-level out-of-distribution splits. Code is available at https://github.com/lokali/CausalBind.
