metadata_records.title: Applied Mathematics for Data Science and Machine Learning
metadata_records.abstract: This book was designed to provide one answer to a common question that many practitioners eventually ask themselves: So what mathematics is behind the tools that I use on a daily basis? Anybody who has ever called a library function and watched as a model fit to their data has, wittingly or unwittingly, called on linear algebra, probability theory, calculus and optimization. This book was written to do just that: to make that machinery visible, and to make the mathematics that underlies the machine-learning systems that now customize industry, academia, and daily life more apparent. The book is arranged to be used in order not as a shelf of references. It starts with the classical pillars of linear algebra for machine learning, probability theory and statistical inference, and multivariable calculus, then delves into the machinery of optimization, with gradient descent, stochastic gradient descent and automatic differentiation, followed by back-propagation and the Adam optimizer, enabling contemporary training. The chapters that follow address the problems and motivation to trust (or not) models that fit well with training data to generalize: statistical learning theory, generalization error, the bias-variance tradeoff, VC dimension, and PAC learning. The mathematics is then carried forward in the chapters that explore systems underpinning current research: the transformer architecture, self-attention and multi-head attention used by large language models; generative AI such as diffusion models, variational autoencoders, and score based generative models; graph neural networks, spectral graph theory, and geometric deep learning in network science; and causal inference, structural causal models, and uncertainty quantification for creating not only accurate but also explainable and trustworthy ML systems. Encwoven throughout are themes on Bayesian inference, Bayesian networks and Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods as well as topics that just recently started entering the main stream curriculum, such as topological data analysis, differential privacy, and quantum machine learning. One theme that comes up quite frequently is the India applied maths ecosystem – the types of work that Indian researchers are doing about applied maths, experiences of data science in India and very specific issues around fairness, generalisation etc in the Indian context for low resource languages and diversity in population etc. This is not a mathematics sidebar, this is what the mathematics is for! This book is for data scientists, machine learning and artificial intelligence practitioners, and students who want more than a black box: engineers who need to diagnose mysterious behavior from their model; researchers who want the deep learning and applied classical mathematics serving as a foundation; and instructors who want a single book to bridge the gap between classical applied math and deep learning optimization, generative AI, and reproducible machine learning. Open problems are introduced in every chapter and can also be used as keywords and worked examples that allow students to use the book in the classroom or as a working reference. My hope is that readers will not just be able to add another formula to their toolbox, but will now, with real clarity, can see that data science and machine learning is the application of mathematics above all else.

metadata_records.title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning in Hydrology and Water Resources: A Systematic Bibliometric Analysis
metadata_records.abstract: This study presents a systematic bibliometric review of Physics-Informed Machine Learning (PIML) research in hydrology and water resources, examining the field's evolution in response to the limitations of traditional process-based models and data-driven approaches. Using a PRISMA-guided framework and a curated dataset from the Scopus database, the analysis evaluated publication trends, leading publication venues, national specialization patterns, international collaboration networks, and emerging research themes. The results reveal a rapidly expanding and increasingly collaborative field, led primarily by China and the United States, with applications concentrated in areas characterized by complex physical processes and limited data availability, particularly flood and disaster management and groundwater modeling and management. Citation patterns highlight the importance of physically consistent prediction and computationally efficient surrogate modeling as major drivers of the field's growth. Despite significant progress, challenges remain, including sensitivity to heterogeneous data, model transferability, and geographical disparities in research participation. Emerging advances in differentiable modeling, multimodal physics-informed frameworks, and domain-specific foundation models are expected to shape the next generation of hydrological intelligence systems. Overall, the findings demonstrate that PIML is becoming an increasingly important paradigm for developing physically consistent, interpretable, and scalable solutions to contemporary water resources and climate resilience challenges.

metadata_records.title: Advanced engineering of inorganic semiconductor nanowires: Materials-by-design for next-generation green energy technologies
metadata_records.abstract: Inorganic semiconductor nanowires (NWs) provide an unusually versatile platform for green-energy technologies because composition, crystal phase, defects, interfaces, morphology, and dimensionality can be engineered across multiple length scales. This review critically examines how these coupled design variables govern charge generation and transport, surface recombination, catalytic activity, ion diffusion, thermal transport, and operational stability. Rather than cataloguing individual materials, we identify transferable structure–property–performance relationships across photovoltaics, photoelectrochemical water splitting, photocatalysis, electrochemical energy storage, and thermoelectric conversion. A central conclusion is that nanoscale advantages are intrinsically conditional: reduced dimensions can enhance light trapping, carrier collection, reaction kinetics, and strain accommodation, but simultaneously intensify surface recombination, interfacial instability, defect sensitivity, and integration losses. We therefore evaluate competing engineering strategies in terms of these trade-offs and their implications for device-scale performance, durability, manufacturability, and sustainability. Recent advances in operando characterization, multiscale simulation, density functional theory, machine learning, and active learning are further assessed as tools for connecting synthesis conditions with experimentally validated material states and functional performance. Particular attention is given to the remaining gap between idealized computational predictions and structurally complex experimental NWs. Finally, we identify reproducibility, standardized data, device integration, scalable manufacturing, long-term stability, and uncertainty-aware human-supervised automation as critical requirements for translating semiconductor NWs from laboratory optimization toward deployable green-energy systems.

metadata_records.title: Robust Edge Trade-off Index (RETI): A multi-criteria framework for reliable and resource-aware deep learning model selection
metadata_records.abstract: The deployment of deep learning models on resource-constrained edge platforms requires model-selection strategies that account for predictive accuracy, reliability, robustness, and computational cost simultaneously. Conventional evaluation commonly treats these criteria independently, making the selection of an appropriate model difficult when candidate architectures exhibit conflicting performance characteristics. This study proposes the Robust Edge Trade-off Index (RETI), a calibration- and robustness-aware extension of multi-criteria decision-making for deployment-oriented edge-AI model selection. RETI integrates confidence-calibrated accuracy, composite robustness based on spatial and distributional behaviour, inference latency, memory usage, and model size within an accuracy-constrained ranking formulation. Fixed-weight and entropy-based variants are evaluated against Weighted Sum Model (WSM), TOPSIS, and Pareto analysis using lightweight and compressed convolutional models on the Stanford Dogs dataset. In the eight-class experiment, MNV3 achieved the highest RETI-Fixed score (0.7921), followed by EfficientNetV2B0 (0.7888) and Mag_20 (0.6828), while the top-three RETI selections achieved 100% Pareto coverage. Ranking agreement with WSM and TOPSIS yielded Spearman correlations of 0.864 and 0.817, respectively. Raspberry Pi 4B benchmarking showed that MNV3 achieved 0.18 ± 0.01 s latency, 5.47 ± 0.05 FPS throughput, 0.51 ± 0.03 MB RAM usage, and 0.86 ± 0.07 J estimated energy per inference. Cross-dataset evaluation altered the ranking, with EfficientNetV2B0 becoming the leading candidate, demonstrating that RETI is context-dependent rather than an absolute model ranking. The results establish RETI as a structured decision-support framework for balancing predictive reliability, robustness, and deployment efficiency in edge-AI model selection.
first_author_affiliations: Tshwane University of Technology

metadata_records.title: An integrated framework based on reinforcement learning for performance-driven residential block generation
metadata_records.abstract: Effective spatial planning of urban blocks is essential for improving environmental performance, especially in subtropical regions. Although AI-driven automation has broadened design exploration, existing generative approaches rarely optimize environmental performance while satisfying planning controls. This study proposes a reinforcement learning-based model chain for three-dimensional urban block generation that jointly optimizes building energy consumption and outdoor thermal comfort. A surrogate model enables real-time prediction of energy load and thermal comfort for candidate layouts. The generation task is formulated as a sequential decision-making problem, and U-GRPO is compared with PPO. Tested on two community sites in Shenzhen, U-GRPO outperformed the original schemes, reducing annual energy load by 1.08% and 2.36% and increasing thermally comfortable area by 0.56% and 0.37%, respectively. The optimized layouts suggest increasing FAR through higher building density and regulated heights while enhancing volumetric heterogeneity. This approach demonstrates RL's potential for performance-driven urban block generation.

metadata_records.title: Macro-Cybernetic Architecture of Planetary Systems: Integrating Quantum Epidemiology, Thermodynamic Hysteresis, and Dimensional Topologies
metadata_records.abstract: The complex interplay between microscopic pathogenic emergence, macroscopic geological events, and global sociopolitical shifts presents a significant challenge to classical, isolated scientific disciplines. This paper introduces a unified, interdisciplinary theoretical model—the Macro-Cybernetic Framework—which analyzes the terrestrial biosphere as a highly integrated computational and immunological network. By applying principles of cryptography, non-equilibrium thermodynamics, and quantum mechanics to biological and sociological phenomena, this framework proposes several novel mechanisms for planetary-scale events. First, we define "Pathogenic Steganography" and "Interferometric Illumination" to explain the camouflage and subsequent systemic unmasking of pervasive parasitic architectures. Second, we introduce the concept of the "Kinetic Echo" and "Pathological Hysteresis," utilizing classical mechanics and control systems engineering (PID overshoot) to model the thermodynamic lag between the cessation of systemic biological triggers and the physical dissipation of disease, offering a new etiology for post-acute infection syndromes. Third, we propose "Quantum Epidemiology," moving beyond classical vector-based transmission models to account for the simultaneous, non-local activation of pre-distributed dormant pathogens (the biospheric botnet), heavily modulated by the "Friction of Manifestation"—a localized ecological shield comprising climatic, nutritional, and microbial variables. Furthermore, this paper models historical macroeconomic and geopolitical isolationist shifts (the Khaldunian cycle) not as independent political events, but as automated "Geopolitical Tourniquets" and network edge deletions executing planetary autoimmune responses. Finally, the framework applies wave shoaling physics to multidimensional topologies, highlighting the critical vulnerability of modern 2-dimensional transactive memory systems (digital infrastructure) to impending high-kinetic electromagnetic events. Ultimately, this comprehensive matrix provides a robust theoretical foundation for predicting epidemiological trajectories, executing comparative shield extraction via subtractive genomics, and ensuring the resilience of complex civilizational networks.

metadata_records.title: Forest carbon sink estimation models: Progress, challenges, and opportunity of space–air–ground integrated assimilation
metadata_records.abstract: : Estimates of forest carbon sinks are essential for global carbon cycle studies, forest stewardship, and monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV); nonetheless, current methodologies exhibit limitations regarding scale conversion, mechanistic restrictions, spatial continuity, and uncertainty management. This document comprehensively evaluates seven methodological categories—empirical statistics, remote sensing inversion, ecological processes, biogeochemistry, flux observations and atmospheric inversion, machine learning, and integrated models—while contrasting their data prerequisites, relevant scales, and principal uncertainties. The research suggests that a singular model faces challenges in achieving a balance among estimation precision, ongoing coverage, dynamic process characterization, and result verifiability; thus, incorporating multi-source observations and models is essential for improving the dependability of forest carbon sink evaluations. This document suggests a “verifiable,” cohesive “space–air–ground” evaluation system. This system employs terrestrial observations to establish authenticity limits, aerial remote sensing to connect scales, and extraterrestrial observations to facilitate regional growth. In conjunction with data assimilation and uncertainty analysis, it facilitates the synchronized evaluation of carbon reserves, variations in carbon reserves, carbon fluxes, and net carbon sinks. Future endeavors ought to concentrate on delineating disturbance-recovery mechanisms, forest stewardship, and lateral carbon transfers linked to timber extraction to enhance forest carbon sink evaluations from static cartography to dynamic, interpretable, and verifiable comprehensive analyses.

metadata_records.title: Supporting AI Readiness Through Digital Workflows in Materials Science
metadata_records.abstract: Materials science produces heterogeneous data across experiments, simulations, and industrial processes that often remain bound to local formats, manual procedures, and project‐specific software. Digital workflows address this fragmentation through explicit, repeatable, and machine‐actionable pipelines. This article examines 13 workflow contributions from the second and third funding phases of the MaterialDigital initiative. The contributions cover data acquisition and FAIR storage, simulation automation, multiscale integration, and AI/ML‐driven optimization. Here, AI‐readiness denotes the documented capacity of workflows and their artifacts to be reliably interpreted, executed, assessed, reused, and, where intended, invoked or adapted by automated systems; it does not require the direct application of artificial intelligence. Eight comparison aspects capture data and metadata, reusable artifacts, orchestration, robustness, cross‐scale coupling, transfer validation, learning and optimization, and adaptive or agent‐accessible operation. By distinguishing demonstrated capabilities from plans, the comparison shows how workflows support AI‐ready research both through integrated AI methods and through structured, traceable, and reusable pipelines. Across the projects, stable data structures, persistent artifacts, executable orchestration, and scientific validation recur as foundations, whereas adaptive operation and agent‐accessible interfaces remain specialized. Wider interoperability would additionally benefit from shared interfaces and explicit, portable descriptions of workflow artifacts.
first_author_affiliations: Computational Materials Design (CM) Max‐Planck‐Institute for Sustainable Materials  Düsseldorf Germany

metadata_records.title: Lifelong small-object navigation in changing object layouts: a benchmark and method
metadata_records.abstract: Household robots need to continually navigate to different objects in the same environment, many of which are small and portable, such as tools and toys. Their small visual footprint and frequent occlusion make reliable observation difficult, and they may be moved by people without the robot observing the changes. We formulate this challenging task as Lifelong Small-object Navigation in Changing Object Layouts (LiSoNav-COL). Agents must seek suitable viewpoints for reliable observation, accumulate and reuse scene knowledge to efficiently locate subsequent targets, and update outdated memory after object relocation. To eliminate the need for prior scene scanning, we also require agents to start navigation with empty scene memory. Although practical, this task still lacks benchmarks designed around its defining assumptions. To bridge this gap, we introduce LiSoNav-Eval, a dedicated benchmark spanning 28 indoor scenes with 45 small-object categories. Its lifelong navigation sequences include both unchanged and relocated targets to evaluate memory reuse and adaptation to object relocation. To address this challenging task, we propose a navigation method based on multi-view Inspection with Viewpoint-Anchored Memory, dubbed IVAM-Nav. IVAM-Nav actively observes supporting surfaces from complementary viewpoints for reliable small-object perception and anchors the resulting memory to their observation viewpoints, supporting relational memory reuse and revalidation under similar viewing conditions. Extensive experiments on LiSoNav-Eval demonstrate favorable performance of IVAM-Nav against representative methods. Benchmark analyses also show that smaller objects, larger environments, and longer relocation distances pose greater challenges. The dataset and code are available here.

metadata_records.title: Visual Evidence Under Cross-Examination: Evaluating and Controlling Decision-Level Evidence Use in Vision-Language Models
metadata_records.abstract: Vision-language models increasingly reason through crops, regions, and tool-produced observations. Yet an observation can influence the answer without benefiting the candidate it supports. We study candidate-bound visual contribution: valid evidence should help, invalidating its supporting relation should remove its additional effect, and valid rebinding should redirect that effect to the newly supported candidate. We introduce CROSS-Bench, a benchmark of 28,000 decision problems, with matched invalidation and rebinding tests on a dedicated evaluation subset. Our RIVET interface preserves evidence identity and uncertainty, composes a candidate-conditioned response, and separately controls its strength. Shared-evidence experiments show that task accuracy and evidence ownership can diverge. Under matched capacity and training, RIVET increases normalized effect transfer from 0.512 to 0.651 where clean evidence has a positive effect. The advantage persists on common evaluation examples and across repeated decision-layer fits. With evidence predicted from raw inputs, RIVET improves CROSS-Bench accuracy by an average of 5.70 pp across four frozen backbones, relative to the same models without auxiliary evidence. These results separate the utility of visual evidence from the candidate-specific destination of its effect.

metadata_records.title: RT-DETR-World: Transferring Rich LLM Semantics to Real-Time Open-Vocabulary Detection
metadata_records.abstract: Open-vocabulary detection (OVD) recognizes categories unseen during training through textual category queries, yet achieving strong generalization with real-time efficiency remains challenging. Beyond vocabulary scaling, zero-shot generalization may benefit from reusable visual--semantic cues learned from seen data, including attributes, actions, states, and contextual relations. Existing real-time OVD methods primarily emphasize vocabulary coverage and efficient region/query--text matching; under strict efficiency constraints, compact detectors may struggle to absorb rich instance semantics and scene context. We propose RT-DETR-World, a compact DETR-style detector that transfers the rich semantics conveyed by descriptions during training while retaining lightweight query--text matching at inference. We construct GroundingCapv2 with three levels of supervision: category names for standard OVD, object descriptions conveying instance-level semantics, and image descriptions conveying object relations and scene context. These descriptions serve only as training-time semantic supervision. To help the compact detector absorb these semantics, we propose Dual-Path Description Alignment (DDA), combining a deployment-consistent MiniLM pathway with a training-only LLM teacher. MiniLM provides query--category supervision and object-description alignment, while offline teacher features supervise matched queries and global visual representations at the object and image levels, respectively. All teacher features are precomputed, and the teacher-side modules are removed after training. We further propose Relation-Aware Negative Relaxation (RNR), which uses teacher-derived semantic similarities to relax related negatives while preserving exact positives. Experiments demonstrate competitive zero-shot accuracy and a favorable accuracy--efficiency trade-off. The code will be released.
first_author_affiliations: Tianjin University

metadata_records.title: ROMA: LLM System for Real-World Object-Centric Multi-Sensory Active Perception
metadata_records.abstract: Humans inherently understand the physical world through an active process. When sensory evidence is insufficient to infer physical properties, we naturally interact with the environment by deciding what information is missing, how to acquire it, and when sufficient evidence has been obtained. In stark contrast, existing multi-sensory robot systems mainly integrate sensory inputs rather than actively acquiring missing evidence through interactions. In this work, we introduce ROMA, an LLM-based system for Real-World Object-Centric Multi-Sensory Active Perception. ROMA integrates vision, audio, tactile, and force sensing into a reasoning-interaction-feedback loop. The model identifies missing evidence and determines the target objects, interactions, and modalities, while a physical interface executes the selected interactions and collects the multi-sensory feedback. To support this capability, we construct ROMI-2K, a large-scale real-world multi-sensory object interaction dataset covering nearly 2,000 objects and 6 atomic interactions with synchronized sensory feedback. Building on these data, we develop a two-stage training framework that aligns sensory modalities and equips the LLM to assess evidence sufficiency, select informative interactions, and reason over the multi-sensory feedback. We further characterize active perception as perception chains, where acquired evidence guides subsequent interactions and reasoning, and establish ROMA Bench to evaluate single-attribute, long-horizon multi-attribute, and intent-driven active perception. Experiments show that ROMA can actively acquire missing evidence and solve complex, long-chain multi-sensory perception tasks that existing methods struggle to handle, laying a strong perceptual foundation for active multi-sensory embodied agents.

metadata_records.title: QuadTok: Quadtree Visual Tokenizer for Autoregressive Image Generation
metadata_records.abstract: We introduce QuadTok, a novel framework for visual tokenization and autoregressive image generation. Compared to traditional approaches using 2D grids or 1D token sequences, we propose a hierarchical quadtree structure, bridging the gap between 2D spatial binding and 1D sequence-level flexibility. The QuadTok tokenizer dynamically allocates representational capacity to visually intricate areas while leaving homogeneous regions at a coarse resolution. Compared with a fixed 256-token grid, our ImageNet-trained tokenizer saves approximately 10% of tokens on ImageNet and 9% when transferred zero-shot to the COCO dataset, while maintaining comparable reconstruction fidelity. Furthermore, the natural causality introduced by the tree structure seamlessly enables autoregressive image generation. Conditioned on a quadtree topology supplied before generation, our 947M GPT-style generative model achieves a 2.08 gFID on the ImageNet $256 \times 256$ benchmark. Additionally, leveraging the strong spatial correlation preserved by the quadtree structure, the QuadTok generator enables zero-shot spatially controlled image generation capabilities. Code: https://github.com/myc634/QuadTok.
first_author_affiliations: University of California , San Diego

metadata_records.title: UniMedSeg: Unified Multi-Modal Medical Image Segmentation via Uncertainty Guided Encoding and Frequency-Spatial Dual-Prompt Decoding
metadata_records.abstract: Text‑driven medical image segmentation demands unified models based on multi‑modal learning, capable of processing diverse imaging modalities while providing spatially reliable prediction estimates for clinical practice. Nevertheless, existing vision‑language model solutions suffer from poor domain generalization and exhibit limited capability for uncertainty estimation to model the cumulative unreliability of cross‑modal alignment across network layers. In this paper, we propose UniMedSeg, a unified vision‑language framework for multi‑modal medical image segmentation built upon frozen pre‑trained vision‑language backbones. Our framework incorporates modality‑aware adaptation, cross‑layer uncertainty‑guided encoding, and a frequency‑spatial dual‑prompt decoder, wherein the progressive uncertainty propagation mechanism of the encoder suppresses misleading cross‑modal features, whereas the decoder disentangles anatomical structure and boundary details in the frequency domain under dual textual prompts. Auxiliary losses further sharpen boundary representations and calibrate pixel‑wise uncertainty maps. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UniMedSeg preserves competitive in‑domain segmentation performance, improves domain generalization, and yields clinically useful spatial risk estimation.

metadata_records.title: UniMedSeg: Unified Multi-Modal Medical Image Segmentation via Uncertainty-Guided Encoding and Frequency-Spatial Dual-Prompt Decoding
metadata_records.abstract: ABSTRACT Text-driven medical image segmentation demands unified models based on multi-modal learning, capable of processing diverse imaging modalities while providing spatially reliable prediction estimates for clinical practice. Nevertheless, existing vision-language model solutions suffer from poor domain generalization and exhibit limited capability for uncertainty estimation to model the cumulative unreliability of cross-modal alignment across network layers. In this paper, we propose UniMedSeg, a unified vision-language framework for multi-modal medical image segmentation built upon frozen pre-trained vision-language backbones. Our framework incorporates modality-aware adaptation, cross-layer uncertainty-guided encoding, and a frequency-spatial dual-prompt decoder, wherein the progressive uncertainty propagation mechanism of the encoder suppresses misleading cross-modal features, whereas the decoder disentangles anatomical structure and boundary details in the frequency domain under dual textual prompts. Auxiliary losses further sharpen boundary representations and calibrate pixel-wise uncertainty maps. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UniMedSeg preserves competitive in-domain segmentation performance, improves domain generalization, and yields clinically useful spatial risk estimation. The source code is available at https://github.com/699zjl/UniMedSeg . Highlights We propose UniMedSeg , a unified vision-language model for five-modality medical segmentation that outputs segmentation masks and clinical-oriented pixel-level uncertainty maps. A cross-layer uncertainty propagation mechanism is designed to dynamically suppress unreliable vision-language alignment by recursively accumulating historical reliability signals. A frequency-spatial dual-prompt decoder disentangles anatomical structure and boundary details via FFT-based separation and branch-specific text-guided attention to reduce frequency-domain artifacts. Auxiliary boundary contrastive and uncertainty calibration objectives enhance boundary discrimination and enforce consistency between predicted uncertainty and segmentation errors. Extensive experiments on multi-modal medical datasets verify that UniMedSeg yields competitive in-domain performance and favorable out-of-distribution generalization capability.

Nevertheless, existing vision-language model solutions suffer from poor domain generalization and exhibit limited capability for uncertainty estimation to model the cumulative unreliability of cross-modal alignment across network layers. In this paper, we propose UniMedSeg, a unified vision-language framework for multi-modal medical image segmentation built upon frozen pre-trained vision-language backbones. Our framework incorporates modality-aware adaptation, cross-layer uncertainty-guided encoding, and a frequency-spatial dual-prompt decoder, wherein the progressive uncertainty propagation mechanism of the encoder suppresses misleading cross-modal features, whereas the decoder disentangles anatomical structure and boundary details in the frequency domain under dual textual prompts. Auxiliary losses further sharpen boundary representations and calibrate pixel-wise uncertainty maps. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UniMedSeg preserves competitive in-domain segmentation performance, improves domain generalization, and yields clinically useful spatial risk estimation. The source code is available at https://github.com/699zjl/UniMedSeg . Highlights We propose UniMedSeg , a unified vision-language model for five-modality medical segmentation that outputs segmentation masks and clinical-oriented pixel-level uncertainty maps. A cross-layer uncertainty propagation mechanism is designed to dynamically suppress unreliable vision-language alignment by recursively accumulating historical reliability signals. A frequency-spatial dual-prompt decoder disentangles anatomical structure and boundary details via FFT-based separation and branch-specific text-guided attention to reduce frequency-domain artifacts. Auxiliary boundary contrastive and uncertainty calibration objectives enhance boundary discrimination and enforce consistency between predicted uncertainty and segmentation errors. Extensive experiments on multi-modal medical datasets verify that UniMedSeg yields competitive in-domain performance and favorable out-of-distribution generalization capability.

metadata_records.title: RGBD-to-3D Object Mesh Refinement via Depth Matching and Symmetry Propagation
metadata_records.abstract: Single-view 3D reconstructors often produce plausible meshes that disagree with the input view, especially near depth discontinuities and self-occlusions. We present a lightweight, plug-and-play RGBD-to-3D refinement that improves any RGB-to-3D reconstructor without retraining. Given a depth map, we correct the visible surface by bipartite matching to back-projected depth points, mirror these corrections onto the occluded side across a detected symmetry plane, and propagate them with a smoothness solver. Every stage is closed-form, making the method orders of magnitude faster than optimization-heavy test-time refinement. On GSO and OmniObject3D with five backbones, it yields consistent gains, also with monocular pseudo-depth, benefits more from symmetry on symmetric objects, and compares favorably with prior refinement in accuracy and runtime. It further improves an RGB-D-to-mesh reconstructor and transfers to real captures with noisy sensor depth.

metadata_records.title: Examining Racial and Gender Bias in CLIP via Explainability-Based Visual Attention Analysis
metadata_records.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) such as CLIP are increasingly integrated into automated decision-making systems where unexamined social biases can directly harm racial and gender minorities through discriminatory outcomes and unjust content censorship. Despite strong multimodal performance, CLIP's susceptibility to demographic bias remains underexplored from a visual attribution perspective. Consequently, the mechanisms by which these biases emerge in visual processing remain opaque, both to researchers and to governance bodies concerned with the equitable and transparent deployment of AI. We address this diagnostic gap by applying four attribution methods to the PAIRS dataset, a controlled benchmark of parallel occupation images balanced across race and gender. We then seek to determine whether demographic stereotyping is detectable and measurable at the level of visual attention, rather than only through output statistics. Preliminary results are mixed: subject-level differences in face-focused saliency across race conditions are not statistically separable at the aggregate level, but under race-explicit prompting we observe the clearest race-conditioned saliency differences. These results suggest that attribution-based diagnostics can expose hidden visual biases, invisible to standard fairness metrics, and help explain how demographic bias emerges in multimodal AI systems. Furthermore, we comparatively analyze the behavior of the attribution methods and discuss their outputs with respect to the broader implications of visual bias diagnostics for fairness and transparency in deployed multimodal AI systems.

metadata_records.title: CHORUS: A proteome-scale atlas of membrane interaction interfaces constructed using cross-protein language model embeddings from sequences alone
metadata_records.abstract: Membrane proteins drive vital cellular signaling and bioenergetics yet resolving their physical interaction interfaces remains hindered by the paucity of experimental complexes and the breakdown of sequence alignments across hydrophobic bilayers. Here, we present CHORUS, a sequence-only deep-learning framework that decodes interaction sites across membrane proteins without requiring 3D structures, multiple sequence alignments (MSAs), or predefined partner identities. By systematically synthesizing complementary latent representations across diverse protein language model (pLM) families and functional layer depths, CHORUS outperforms 18 established sequence- and structure-based methods across 4,655 homology-isolated test contexts (average precision: 0.643), demonstrating amplified predictive capacity within the lipid-embedded core (0.746). We show that CHORUS delineates quaternary contact boundaries across megadalton respiratory supercomplexes directly from sequences alone (0.984). We deliver the CHORUS Atlas (https://chorus.atlas.sunnylab.org), providing precomputed, residue-resolved interaction landscapes for 80,619 reviewed transmembrane proteins spanning 4,918 species and 33.7 million residues to empower interactome-scale discovery and allosteric therapeutic design.
first_author_affiliations: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

metadata_records.title: EVFormer: An Egocentric Vision-EMG Bidirectional Attention Model for Bimanual Hand Pose Estimation
metadata_records.abstract: Egocentric bimanual hand pose estimation is important for virtual interaction, wearable control, and rehabilitation, but visual observations are often degraded by self-occlusion, hand-hand contact, and object manipulation. We propose EVFormer, a multimodal framework that combines the current RGB frame with the preceding 200 ms of bilateral wrist surface electromyography (sEMG) to estimate 44 finger and wrist joint angles. EVFormer separately encodes visual spatial features and sEMG temporal features, enables cross-modal information exchange through sequential bidirectional cross-attention, and integrates the two modalities using feature-wise gated fusion. We evaluate EVFormer in a single-participant feasibility study using one synchronized public EgoEMG recording with chronologically separated training, validation, and test splits. On 296 test samples, EVFormer achieves a mean absolute error of 11.482 degrees, compared with 13.228-13.610 degrees for vision-only, sEMG-only, late-fusion, and training-mean baselines. This corresponds to relative error reductions of 13.20% compared with the vision-only model and 14.23% compared with late fusion. EVFormer also achieves the lowest error in four of the five evaluated gesture classes. These results provide preliminary evidence that feature-level interaction between egocentric vision and sEMG can improve bimanual hand pose estimation. Further evaluation across participants, recording sessions, sensor placements, and real-world interaction conditions is required to establish the generalizability of the approach.

metadata_records.title: Language-Augmented Video Action Anticipation: Design Fundamentals, Benchmarks, and Open Challenges
metadata_records.abstract: Action anticipation predicts future human actions from partial video under incomplete context and temporal uncertainty. Recent systems introduce large language models (LLMs), vision-language models (VLMs), or language-derived semantics at different stages, but reported gains are difficult to interpret when task formulation, visual pretraining, supervision, decoder design, and evaluation code change simultaneously. The central contribution of this review is an evidence-aware design map that crosses task regime with the point at which language-derived information intervenes. We characterise task regimes along six axes. These axes organise the literature into five broad task families: single-action, sequence, object-interaction, cross-view, and planning-oriented settings. C1-C3 locate interventions in context construction, goal/intention modelling, and future decoding, while C4 is treated as an adjacent, emerging grounding/executability extension. Unlike a generic processing pipeline, the map links each intervention to an appropriate counterfactual, failure diagnosis, and permissible evidence claim. Supporting contributions include a protocol-level audit of Ego4D-LTA and EPIC-KITCHENS-100, a multidimensional evidence profile, and the Backbone-Aware Comparison and Ablation Protocol (BCAP). The unresolved EK-100 record is treated as a reporting-comparability case study and is not used as a leaderboard. Evidence for LLM benefits, goal ambiguity, and horizon effects is therefore formulated as testable hypotheses requiring matched validation, not as causal conclusions. The accompanying package contains the coded evidence, source locators, protocol metadata, and versioned catalogue used in the review.

metadata_records.title: Pose-Aware Multimodal Automatic Tagging for Greek Traditional Music
metadata_records.abstract: Automatic tagging is a core task in Music Information Retrieval (MIR), yet most tagging systems exploit only audio. Live music performance is inherently multimodal, as semantic labels such as instruments, regional styles, and dance forms are encoded simultaneously across acoustic, visual, and embodied performance cues. This is especially true of culturally specific repertoires such as Greek traditional music, which remain underrepresented in MIR benchmarks. In this paper, we investigate whether the use of dancer pose provides complementary information for automatic tagging in Greek traditional music beyond audio. Using the Lyra dataset, we extend prior audio-only work by extracting aligned video features and pose-derived skeleton streams, enabling an experimental setting for multimodal auto-tagging. We further introduce an automated pipeline for extracting primary-dancer skeleton sequences from in-the-wild dance footage, combining dance-scene detection, multi-person tracking, dancer selection, pose estimation, and quality filtering. We compare unimodal, all bimodal combinations, and trimodal systems using multiple fusion strategies. Audio remains the strongest single modality (AST: macro ROC-AUC 0.821), while skeletons, though weak in isolation, enhance performance through multimodal fusion. The best trimodal system improves macro ROC-AUC by about 4 percentage points over the strongest audio baseline.
first_author_affiliations: School of Electrical and Computer Engineering , National Technical University of Athens , Athens , Greece

metadata_records.title: Integrating Local Detail and Global Context: A Dual-Input Multi-Task Learning Framework for Bone Tumor Diagnosis
metadata_records.abstract: Primary bone tumors are rare but clinically aggressive neoplasms whose diagnosis from radiographs is challenged by heterogeneous morphology, subtle lesion margins, and overlapping bone structures. To address the limitations of existing single-view models, we present a dual-input, multi-task learning framework that, to our knowledge, is the first to apply bidirectional cross-modal attention between a lesion crop and the full radiograph for joint segmentation and subtype classification. Using the multi-institutional Bone Tumor X-ray Radiograph Dataset (BTXRD, n=3,746), we employ a YOLO-based detector to generate regions of interest, which are paired with full images as inputs to a dual-stream DenseNet121 architecture. Features are integrated via a novel cross-modal attention fusion strategy, refined by Hierarchical Multi-scale Feature Fusion, effectively balancing fine-grained lesion detail with global anatomical context. Evaluated on a held-out patient-level test split, the model demonstrates superior performance over single-input baselines, achieving an overall Dice Similarity Coefficient of 0.896 and a macro-averaged classification F1-score of 0.928. Notably, the system exhibits exceptional sensitivity for malignant osteosarcoma (AUC 0.999), validating the potential of dual-stream context modeling to support radiologists in accurate, early decision-making.
first_author_affiliations: Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering , Ahsanullah University of Science and Technology , Bangladesh

metadata_records.title: Depth-Guided Contrastive Learning for 2D Representations with 3D Spatial Awareness
metadata_records.abstract: Standard contrastive learning frameworks are mainly designed from a semantic perspective, yet learning 2D visual representations that preserve 3D spatial structure is also important for scene understanding. In this work, we propose Depth-Guided Contrastive Learning (DGCL), a simple auxiliary objective that injects 3D spatial awareness into 2D contrastive representation learning. Our key idea is to use depth to convert local 3D proximity into contrastive similarity: pixels that are closer in 3D space are encouraged to have more similar representations than pixels that are farther apart. Instead of relying on absolute depth values, DGCL formulates supervision through relative 3D distance comparisons among randomly sampled pixels, making the objective invariant to depth scale, efficient to compute, and easy to integrate into existing contrastive frameworks. Experiments across different datasets and models show that DGCL consistently improves 2D representation learning and benefits semantic downstream tasks by stronger spatial and geometric understanding. The code is available on https://github.com/LeungTsang/DGCL.
first_author_affiliations: KU Leuven Belgium

metadata_records.title: Propositional and imagistic incongruity: a dual-route cognitive account of humor processing
metadata_records.abstract: This paper develops a theoretical account of humor processing in terms of two interacting routes of cognitive processing. Building on the distinction between propositional and imagistic modes of language comprehension, it argues that humorous incongruity may arise through conceptual, perceptual, or cross-representational discrepancies. The propositional route involves relatively abstract and amodal representations, in which humor emerges from a mismatch between conceptual expectations and asserted or implied meanings. The imagistic route involves mental imagery, perceptual simulation, and sensorimotor representation, in which humor emerges from discrepancies between expected and activated perceptual or multimodal representations. In addition, the paper proposes that humorous effects may arise through between-route incongruity, where propositional and imagistic representations conflict, as in cases where verbal content and gesture, visual imagery, or embodied cues convey incompatible meanings. This dual-route account is not intended to replace existing theories of humor, but to specify a processing-level distinction that clarifies how incongruity is represented and resolved across verbal, visual, and multimodal forms of humor. By linking humor processing to conceptual processing, mental imagery, and embodied cognition, the account provides a framework for explaining why formally similar humorous expressions may differ in cognitive demands, perceptual salience, and affective impact. The paper concludes by outlining implications for future behavioral, cognitive, and multimodal research on humor processing.
first_author_affiliations: School of Foreign Languages, University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, Chengdu, China

metadata_records.title: GeoNLI - A Natural Language Interpreter for Satellite Imagery
metadata_records.abstract: Multi-modal multitasking models have shown strong performance on remote sensing datasets. However, because these models are trained on heterogeneous data and vary across tasks, designing a unified model that performs well in captioning, visual question answering (VQA), and visual grounding remains challenging. In this work, we evaluate several models on the VRS Bench and NWPU-VHR-10 datasets. The EarthMind model demonstrates strong results in both captioning and VQA. For grounding, we propose multiple pipelines - RemoteSAM-SAM-v1, RemoteSAM-SAM-v2, and DiffuSAM - and ultimately adopt a majority-voting ensemble across EarthMind, RemoteSAM, SAM3, Falcon, RemoteSAM-SAM3-v1, RemoteSAM-SAM3-v2, and DiffuSAM predictions. Our unified, modular pipeline integrates advanced SAM variants with multimodal LLMs to jointly perform captioning, VQA, and grounding. It achieves 82% accuracy on captioning and 83.32% on VQA, with 90.94%, 52.04%, and 92.06% for binary, numeric, and semantic question types respectively. For grounding, it attains 64.94% accuracy. By combining diverse VLMs with our custom RemoteSAM-SAM3 models through ensemble majority voting, the system delivers more accurate and consistent remote-sensing understanding than task-specific approaches.
first_author_affiliations: Indian Institute of Technology , Bombay

2609.28741.raw_abstract: Multi-modal multitasking models have shown strong performance on remote sensing datasets. However, because these models are trained on heterogeneous data and vary across tasks, designing a unified model that performs well in captioning, visual question answering (VQA), and visual grounding remains challenging. In this work, we evaluate several models on the VRS Bench and NWPU-VHR-10 datasets. The EarthMind model demonstrates strong results in both captioning and VQA. For grounding, we propose multiple pipelines - RemoteSAM-SAM-v1, RemoteSAM-SAM-v2, and DiffuSAM - and ultimately adopt a majority-voting ensemble across EarthMind, RemoteSAM, SAM3, Falcon, RemoteSAM-SAM3-v1, RemoteSAM-SAM3-v2, and DiffuSAM predictions. Our unified, modular pipeline integrates advanced SAM variants with multimodal LLMs to jointly perform captioning, VQA, and grounding. It achieves 82% accuracy on captioning and 83.32% on VQA, with 90.94%, 52.04%, and 92.06% for binary, numeric, and semantic question types respectively. For grounding, it attains 64.94% accuracy. By combining diverse VLMs with our custom RemoteSAM-SAM3 models through ensemble majority voting, the system delivers more accurate and consistent remote-sensing understanding than task-specific approaches.

metadata_records.title: A Unified Explainable AI Framework for Multimodal Chest X-Ray and Clinical Note Diagnosis
metadata_records.abstract: Chest radiography is the most common first-line imaging modality for diagnosing respiratory disease, but deep learning classifiers built for this task are largely opaque, which restricts their clinical adoption. This paper proposes a multimodal explainable-AI (XAI) framework that couples a DenseNet-121 convolutional network for chest X-ray classification with a RadBERT transformer for clinical-note analysis inside a single interpretability pipeline. Grad-CAM produces spatial saliency maps for the imaging branch, while SHAP-based token attribution explains the predictions of the language branch, whose pathology label is obtained through cosine similarity against class-prototype embeddings. On a representative case, the text branch assigned an 80.8% similarity score to pneumonia and highlighted clinical indicators such as fever and consolidation alongside demographic terms such as age and diabetes history. Rather than reporting a marginal accuracy improvement, the central contribution is a cross-modal consistency check that compares the imaging and textual explanations for the same patient and automatically surfaces discrepancies — for example, a mismatch between the anatomical location implicated by the image and the one described in the note — that neither modality reveals in isolation. Outputs are exposed through a standardized JSON schema together with a natural-language summary to support clinician review.
first_author_affiliations: Department of Computer Science and Engineering , Sri Venkateswara College of Engineering , Chennai , India

metadata_records.title: Biophysical modeling of excitation/inhibition imbalance in Alzheimer’s disease
metadata_records.abstract: Structured Abstract INTRODUCTION Alzheimer’s disease (AD) involves early sensory and perceptual changes that can precede memory decline. We developed a two-layer rate-based neural model of early and higher visual areas with feedforward, feedback, and recurrent connections to examine how excitatory/inhibitory (E/I) balance shapes visual motion perception in AD. METHODS Using Motion-Induced Position Shift and Altered Motion Repulsion stimuli, we factorially manipulated excitatory (E) and inhibitory (I) subfield power and connectivity to examine their effects on illusion representation across visual layers. RESULTS Increased E, decreased I, and increased E/I reduced illusion representation, consistent with reduced illusion susceptibility in AD, whereas the converse increased illusion representation, reflecting neurotypical processing. Higher-level layer 2 representations were more resistant to E/I perturbations than lower-level layer 1. Illusion representation was less affected by E/I increases in intra-areal (recurrent) connectivity than in inter-areal (feedforward/feedback) connectivity. DISCUSSION This mechanistic framework links E/I balance and connectivity to altered visual motion illusion representations in AD and suggests that E/I and connectivity measures may provide probes of early AD neurobiology. The framework may also generalize beyond vision.

metadata_records.title: Context-aware Bayesian Fusion for Multimodal Object Detection
metadata_records.abstract: Reliable detection of pedestrians and road users is essential for the safe operation of autonomous vehicles. However, this task becomes increasingly challenging under adverse environmental conditions, such as poor weather and low lighting, where the performance of state-of-the-art pre-trained object detectors and on-board sensors tends to degrade, which limits their effectiveness and reliability. Moreover, retraining models for each operating context imposes significant constraints due to high data requirements, computational resources, and time. Considering this, we propose a novel context-aware multimodal late fusion approach that integrates a lightweight gating network within our probabilistic calibration framework. The gating network extracts environmental context and dynamically modulates the detection outputs of pre-trained object detectors based on the inferred context, without retraining of the detectors. Our methodology is evaluated on a modified KITTI dataset, in which the camera images and lidar pointclouds are augmented for varying fog levels. Experimental results show that our approach yields an approximately 14% relative improvement over non-adaptive late fusion baselines, achieving a consistent average precision of 56% across different fog levels.

metadata_records.title: Resource-Efficient 3D Shape and Orientation Estimation of Road Users using Roadside RGB Camera and 3D Radar
metadata_records.abstract: End-to-end deep learning pipelines for camera-radar 3D object detection are well established in driver assistance systems and autonomous vehicles; however, adapting them to roadside-mounted infrastructure presents significant challenges. On vehicles, sensor heights, pitch angles, and relative geometries remain largely uniform, allowing end-to-end models to generalize effectively. On the contrary, roadside sensor installations vary drastically in height, tilt, and field of view across locations, rendering end-to-end models prone to failure and difficult to adapt without massive location-specific datasets. Hence, instead of designing a complex end-to-end pipeline for direct 3D bounding box estimation, a low-cost, resource-efficient two-stage approach is proposed for real-time 3D shape and orientation estimation. The first stage utilizes any off-the-shelf, state-of-the-art method to extract 2D camera bounding boxes and associated 3D radar points for each road user. The proposed second stage then processes these inputs to construct 3D oriented bounding boxes where radar data determines 3D position, predefined templates define size for each road user, and a tiny neural network predicts a site-specific and optimized yaw angle. The algorithm is successfully validated at a curved road with a junction for pedestrians, bicycles, and cars, where it achieves 25 frames per second on an NVIDIA Jetson ORIN for real-time applications.

metadata_records.title: Mining Cross-Modal Perception Gaps in Autonomous Driving: When Camera and LiDAR Disagree
metadata_records.abstract: Multi-modal fusion for 3D object detection assumes that cameras and LiDAR are broadly complementary. In practice, how much each modality is trusted at a given location is decided by learned weights that are neither characterized nor auditable. We label every ground-truth object by which modalities detected it, then mine the resulting 0.4M-object database across nuScenes, KITTI, and Waymo. Because the patterns shift with distance from the ego vehicle, we read the mined model through Spatially Stratified Feature Attribution (SSFA), which conditions Shapley attribution on distance zones and exposes structure that global attribution averages away. Three assumptions built into the current fusion design do not hold. The modality-preference boundary tracks the object itself: a traffic cone is nearly six times as likely as a truck to be seen by the camera alone (16.8% vs. 2.9%), regardless of range. Camera-only detections peak at 10-30 m, inside the band usually ceded to LiDAR, and fall away on either side. The drivers of failure are not additive either: the distance - density interaction alone outweighs the entire main effect of viewing direction. We further find that modality dominance is directionally non-stationary, with objects behind the vehicle being markedly more LiDAR-dominant than those in front. We compile the mined structure into a Modality Reliability Map and inject it into four pretrained fusion detectors through a lightweight attention layer. This improves performance by up to 1.3 mean Average Precision (mAP) while fine-tuning under 4% of their parameters in 2-3 GPU-hours. Our work lifts reliability out of the weights and treats it as a quantity that can be examined before deployment. That is what a safety measure for multi-modal perception must rest on.

metadata_records.title: Adversarial Robustness of Camera-Radar Sensor Fusion for Autonomous Driving
metadata_records.abstract: Autonomous driving (AD) relies on multi-sensor perception to interpret the surrounding environment. However, the robustness of camera--radar fusion under adversarial conditions remains largely unexplored. This paper presents a systematic measurement study of the robustness of camera--radar sensor fusion in AD. We construct a unified evaluation pipeline on the nuScenes dataset that simulates attacks on both sensing modalities, including eight camera-image perturbations and three radar point-cloud perturbations. We evaluate five camera--radar fusion algorithms across two perception tasks, 3D object detection and depth estimation, and quantify their performance under clean and attacked inputs using standard metrics. Our evaluation reveals a clear asymmetry in the robustness of fusion systems. Camera perturbations substantially degrade both object detection and depth estimation, and moderate attack strengths are already sufficient to cause severe performance degradation. In contrast, the evaluated radar perturbations produce smaller and task-dependent effects, with object-detection models showing particularly limited degradation. Our analysis attributes this difference to the strong dependence of existing fusion architectures on dense camera features, together with the filtering, association, and confidence-weighting mechanisms commonly applied to sparse radar measurements. These results demonstrate that sensor fusion does not inherently guarantee robustness and that the contribution and reliability of each sensing modality must be explicitly considered under adversarial conditions. Based on four empirical findings, we derive measurement-guided design implications for future robust camera--radar fusion, including modality-specific reliability estimation, cross-modal consistency checking, adaptive fusion, and graceful failover under severe sensor degradation.

metadata_records.title: Squeeze-Aware-YOLO: Early Channel Recalibration and Multi-Scale Fusion for Real-Time Traffic Sign Detection
metadata_records.abstract: Traffic sign detection plays a vital role in intelligent transportation systems, supporting the safe operation of advanced driver assistance systems and autonomous vehicles. Despite significant progress in real-time object detection, accurately identifying traffic signs under challenging conditions remains difficult. Variations in lighting, adverse weather, motion blur, and partial occlusion often reduce detection performance, especially for small or visually degraded signs where important spatial information can be lost. To address these challenges, we propose Squeeze-Aware-YOLO, a lightweight traffic sign detection framework that introduces a multi-branch bottleneck module combining convolutional kernels of different sizes with a Squeeze-and-Excitation mechanism to improve feature extraction and adaptive channel weighting. In addition, we integrate the Multi-Branch Auxiliary Feature Pyramid Network and Re-parameterized Heterogeneous Multi-Scale modules to strengthen multi-scale feature representation and feature fusion while preserving real-time inference efficiency for practical deployment. The proposed approach is evaluated on the Bangladeshi Traffic Sign Detection Dataset, the CSUST Chinese Traffic Sign Detection Benchmark 2021, and the German Traffic Sign Detection Benchmark, achieving mAP@0.5 scores of 74.7%, 79.4%, and 84.0%, respectively, while consistently outperforming recent state-of-the-art YOLO-based traffic sign detectors. These findings demonstrate that combining multi-scale receptive fields, channel attention, and enhanced feature fusion enables more accurate and robust traffic sign detection while maintaining the computational efficiency required for real-world deployment.

metadata_records.title: Safety-Oriented Trajectory Ranking from BEV Perception Outputs
metadata_records.abstract: Bird's-Eye-View (BEV) representations are increasingly used as compact inputs for autonomous driving perception and planning. However, lightweight and interpretable methods for evaluating candidate ego trajectories directly on BEV outputs remain useful for vehicular safety workflows, rapid prototyping, and human-in-the-loop validation. This paper presents a modular trajectory ranking pipeline that consumes BEVFusion object detections and map segmentations derived from nuScenes sensor data and ranks manually specified candidate trajectories according to safety-first criteria. The ranking prioritizes avoiding collisions and walkway violations, then smaller end distance to the target, and finally path efficiency. To study whether these rule-based rankings resemble human judgment, we created seven BEV traffic scenarios and compared the script output with preferences from a survey of 21 participants. Across 146 pairwise votes, 124 matched the trajectory ranked first by the evaluator, corresponding to an overall agreement of 84.9 %. The results indicate that simple BEV-centric safety heuristics can approximate human preferences in constrained trajectory choice tasks while remaining transparent enough for analysis, dataset curation, and autonomous driving studies.

metadata_records.title: WoVR+: World Model as Reliable Simulator for Versatile VLA Policy Optimization with RL
metadata_records.abstract: Action-conditioned world models can reduce costly real-robot interaction in reinforcement learning for Vision-Language-Action models (VLA-RL), but hallucinations can mislead policy optimization. Extending them to richer VLA interfaces and long-horizon tasks raises challenges in spatiotemporal and cross-modal consistency, exploration-reliability balance in RL, and compounding rollout errors. We present WoVR+, extending WoVR's hallucination-aware WM-RL framework by redesigning the learned environment and imagined interaction protocol: A VLA-interface-aligned world model provides multi-view prediction and proprioceptive updates while mitigating hallucinations. Chunk-wise noise preserves flow-based policy exploration while limiting prediction-degrading action jitter. For long-horizon tasks, stage-local imagined training combines stage-entry resets, stage-specific rewards, local horizons, and controllable sampling to shorten generated prefixes and balance training across stages. WoVR+ improves success over SFT by 21.09% and 16.7% on RoboTwin and 6 real-robot tasks. Long-horizon phone-packaging success rises from 30% to 75%. Videos are available at https://youmo445.github.io/WoVR_Plus.github.io/.

We present WoVR+, extending WoVR's hallucination-aware WM-RL framework by redesigning the learned environment and imagined interaction protocol: A VLA-interface-aligned world model provides multi-view prediction and proprioceptive updates while mitigating hallucinations. Chunk-wise noise preserves flow-based policy exploration while limiting prediction-degrading action jitter. For long-horizon tasks, stage-local imagined training combines stage-entry resets, stage-specific rewards, local horizons, and controllable sampling to shorten generated prefixes and balance training across stages. WoVR+ improves success over SFT by 21.09% and 16.7% on RoboTwin and 6 real-robot tasks. Long-horizon phone-packaging success rises from 30% to 75%. Videos are available at https://youmo445.github.io/WoVR_Plus.github.io/.

metadata_records.title: MMTA: Benchmarking Multimodal Temporal Analysis with Time Series, Text, and Vision
metadata_records.abstract: Time-series analysis is increasingly studied in multimodal settings, yet most benchmarks pair temporal signals with text or with visualizations derived from the same signal. This leaves open whether multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can integrate time series with real-world visual evidence. We introduce MMTA (multimodal temporal analysis), a benchmark of tri-modal tasks with diverse cross-modal complementarity patterns among time series, text, and vision. MMTA spans nine domains -- robotics, autonomous driving, human action, manufacturing, AR assistance, healthcare, recommendation, finance, and climate -- under video+TS and image+TS layouts, with a 3,524-sample test split covering classification and forecasting. The benchmark standardizes heterogeneous real-world sources into a shared schema with domain-specific prompts, provenance documentation, and success-weighted metrics that penalize both wrong answers and failed generations. Evaluating eight open-source and proprietary MLLMs reveals a shared bottleneck: representing time series as text creates very long token sequences and weakens fine-grained alignment with visual evidence, especially in long-video settings. We then introduce TimeOmni-v, a multimodal LLM extension with a dedicated time-series encoder, temporal positional alignment, modality-aware token layout, and a forecasting head. TimeOmni-v improves long-video classification and time-series inference efficiency, showing that MMTA not only exposes representation and grounding failures but also motivates targeted model design.

metadata_records.title: TartanMatch: Towards Universal Dense Correspondence Across Modalities
metadata_records.abstract: Robotic platforms combine multi-modal sensors to operate across diverse conditions, but most dense correspondence methods are limited to RGB-RGB or a small set of modality pairs. Training a model for each modality pair scales poorly with the number of sensors and forgoes potential positive transfer across modality pairs. We introduce TartanMatch, a unified model for dense correspondence across all 25 ordered pairs among RGB, event, thermal, depth, and projected LiDAR. TartanMatch adapts an RGB-pretrained correspondence model to all modality pairs within one shared network using lightweight modality adaptation and a mixture of real and synthetic data. On zero-shot real-world benchmarks, TartanMatch reduces Endpoint Error (EPE) over the strongest baselines by 61.9% for cross-modal matching and 49.6% for same-modal matching. We further show that joint training across all modality pairs improves average matching accuracy over pair-specific training, especially on challenging cross-modal pairs. These results demonstrate that a single model achieves broad multi-modal coverage and state-of-the-art matching accuracy.

metadata_records.title: Multi-modal Representation Fusion for Long-term Microsurgical Anastomosis Trajectory Anticipation
metadata_records.abstract: Microsurgical anastomosis is one of the most challenging and sophisticated procedures for surgical robotics, requiring accurate manipulation of surgical instruments within a limited space to achieve precise operations. Accurate surgical trajectory anticipation is essential for surgical scene understanding, intraoperative planning, robotic manipulation, and reliable behaviour analysis. However, existing approaches mainly focus on features extracted from surgical videos and historical trajectories, while overlooking rich semantic and motion information that can provide more discriminative multi-modal representations for complex surgical instrument-tissue interactions. In this work, we propose a cross-modal feature fusion framework for long-term 2D and 3D microsurgical anastomosis trajectory anticipation. The proposed framework consists of a multi-modal representation extractor and a cross-modal feature fusion network. Semantic recognition of surgical objects and consecutive motion estimation are incorporated as multi-modal visual cues, providing complementary spatial and temporal guidance for instrument-tissue interaction characterization. A coarse-to-fine progressive fusion strategy with a long-short-term memory mechanism is introduced to capture temporal dependencies step by step. The training and evaluation are conducted on our established robotic platform and a comprehensive dataset containing both phantom and ex-vivo surgical scenarios is constructed. Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms existing methods and exhibits improved robustness across different surgical scenes, highlighting its potential for both intelligent robot-assisted and autonomous surgical systems.

metadata_records.title: SenseWeather: Multimodal Sensing for Robust Robotic Perception under Extreme Conditions
metadata_records.abstract: Robotic perception must remain reliable when extreme environmental conditions severely degrade the primary RGB observation. Although robotic platforms commonly carry complementary sensors such as depth and infrared, much of the modern perception stack remains RGB-centric, creating a mismatch between multimodal onboard sensing and pretrained downstream models. We study whether complementary sensing can be used upstream to recover a task-compatible RGB observation that preserves existing perception capabilities without modifying or retraining the downstream stack. To this end, we introduce SenseWeather, a controlled multimodal benchmark for robotic perception under severe rain, snow, dust, fog, and darkness, with registered RGB, depth, and infrared observations, clean references, and grounded high-level perception tasks. We further develop Fusion-to-RGB, with two parameter-efficient sensor-fusion realizations based on token-space fusion for a diffusion transformer and residual latent conditioning for an inpainting UNet. Across frozen open-vocabulary grounding and vision-language models, RGB+D+IR fusion improves all paired downstream comparisons over the corresponding RGB-only restorers, including AP50 gains across all ten detector comparisons. Importantly, these perception gains do not consistently follow conventional image-fidelity metrics, and increasing weather severity does not induce monotonic downstream degradation. These results show that complementary sensing can preserve reusable robotic perception under extreme conditions, while highlighting task-level perception robustness as an objective distinct from visual restoration quality.

metadata_records.title: Two-Stage Multi-modal Learning for Dynamic Audio-Visual Navigation: From Physical Alignment to Scene Aggregation
metadata_records.abstract: Embodied Audio-Visual Navigation (AVN) requires an agent to locate sound targets by jointly leveraging visual and auditory cues. While prior work has achieved notable success with static sound sources, real-world scenarios often involve moving targets, giving rise to the more challenging problem of \textbf{Dynamic Audio-Visual Navigation (D-AVN)}. Existing approaches largely rely on semantic auditory features, which limits generalization to unheard sound categories and hinders fine-grained spatial reasoning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel \textbf{Two-Stage Multi-modal Learning} framework for D-AVN. In the Physical Alignment stage, the proposed \textbf{Intensity-Calibrated Geometry Encoder (ICGE)} performs physics-informed alignment of sound intensity with visual geometry to capture category-agnostic spatial correspondence. In the Scene Aggregation stage, a Transformer-based \textbf{Cross-Modal Scene Aggregator (CMSA)} dynamically integrates multi-modal features to construct a robust state representation for policy learning. Extensive experiments on Replica and Matterport3D demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art success rates, while significantly improving generalization and navigation efficiency in complex environments and under unheard sound scenarios.

metadata_records.title: Registration is a Representation Problem: Solving Whole-Body PET/CT Registration
metadata_records.abstract: Raw image intensities are a poor surrogate for similarity across images in correspondence problems. Further, while auxiliary segmentation labels can provide semantic identification and improve matching, they can assign only coarse identities to fine-grained anatomy and often cover only a subset of structures, particularly in whole-body settings. We present an approach that instead establishes correspondence using complementary representations of anatomy and demonstrate its utility for longitudinal whole-body PET/CT registration in the Learn2Reg 2026 PSMAReg Challenge. Our 3D foundation model, anatomix, is used to derive fine-grained, per-voxel semantic representations that are consistent across volumes, and we further employ off-the-shelf segmentation models to obtain coarse anatomical identities. Together, these representations drive a GPU-accelerated iterative registration solver (FireANTs) in a hybrid multistage framework: the first stage estimates alignment from dense multi-channel features, after which a second refines the deformation using both anatomix- and segmentation-based losses. Lastly, because registration should not introduce non-biological tumor volume changes across time, we develop lesion-specific component-wise volume preservation schemes. Without any task-specific training, our system won first place in the PSMAReg Challenge leaderboard. Code and interactive visualizations are available at http://www.neeldey.com/reps-for-reg.

metadata_records.title: Beyond the Encoder: Object-Centric Representations Emerging from Segmentation Foundation Models
metadata_records.abstract: Foundation models are increasingly used as feature extractors for downstream tasks with limited data, typically through representations obtained from their encoders. However, foundation models trained for structured tasks such as segmentation also form object-specific representations during task execution, whose transferability remains largely unexplored. We investigate Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2) object pointers, compact object-level representations produced through the segmentation pathway, as transferable representations for downstream tumour prediction. Through experiments on two PET/CT tumour prediction tasks, we find that object pointers learned using segmentation supervision alone already encode tumour-discriminative information, despite never being optimised for the downstream labels. We further introduce task-guided object pointers, where an auxiliary objective jointly shapes the object pointer space for the downstream prediction together with segmentation. Task-guided pointers improve cancer-type classification, outperforming conventional encoder-based transfer and radiomics, while segmentation-only pointers perform best on the more challenging recurrence prediction task. Representation analyses reveal associations between object pointers and interpretable radiomics features, class-dependent organisation of the learned representation space, and explicit spatial grounding around the segmented tumour. Together, these findings suggest that useful transferable representations can emerge through the execution of a foundation model's primary task, providing an alternative to conventional encoder-based transfer.

metadata_records.title: TRACE: Efficient Transfer Learning for Neural Whole-Body Control Across Humanoid Embodiments
metadata_records.abstract: Humanoid behavior foundation models (BFMs) enable diverse whole-body control, but adapting a pretrained controller to a new embodiment remains challenging because of kinematic and dynamic mismatch. We present TRACE, a framework for efficient cross-embodiment adaptation that preserves pretrained motion representations while specializing feedback control to the target robot.TRACE first injects kinematic priors into input and output projection layers and aligns nominal joint dynamics to reduce embodiment mismatch and support stable fine-tuning. It then combines encoder distillation with low-rank reinforcement learning on a compact, quality-screened motion set, using a two-phase curriculum to establish stable tracking before refining difficult motions. We apply TRACE to transfer SONIC from Unitree G1 to Unitree H2 using 10 million motion frames and approximately eight hours of training on a single RTX PRO 6000 GPU, at less than 0.1% of the GPU-hour cost of training SONIC from scratch. The adapted controller achieves 96.08\% success on 67,953 evaluation motions under a height-scaled tracking criterion. Real-robot demonstrations span dynamic motion tracking and whole-body teleoperation, with collected demonstrations supporting downstream vision-language-action policy post-training. These results demonstrate practical reuse of a pretrained humanoid controller across robots with different body scales and dynamics.

metadata_records.title: Improving Neural Symbolic Regression with a Diverse Prior and Post-training Alignment
metadata_records.abstract: Symbolic regression is the problem of finding an expression that fits a dataset. Solving it requires searching a combinatorial space of candidate expressions. Neural symbolic regression can amortize that search by training a model once on synthetic data and then predicting expressions for a new dataset. But existing models still underperform genetic programming on real, noisy data. We argue that the deficit lies in the training rather than in the paradigm, and present RASR (Reinforced Amortized Symbolic Regression), a method with two key changes to the training recipe. First, we design a synthetic prior that narrows the gap with real-world data: inputs come from the prior of a tabular foundation model; constants are sampled bottom-up, conditioned on the data; targets carry heteroscedastic and structured noise; and everything is standardized. Second, we split training into two stages. Supervised pre-training maximizes the token-level likelihood of a reference expression. This is followed by reinforcement-learning post-training that aligns the model with its inference-time use by rewarding held-out fit and penalizing expression size. On the black-box track of SRBench 2.0, RASR achieves the best mean test $R^2$ rank of all evaluated methods. Three RASR variants, trained with different size penalties, make up most of the accuracy-complexity Pareto front. On Strogatz, our method recovers more ground-truth expressions than any baseline, and on Feynman it is competitive with the best-performing methods.
