Neural symbolic regression can amortize that search by training a model once on synthetic data and then predicting expressions for a new dataset. But existing models still underperform genetic programming on real, noisy data. We argue that the deficit lies in the training rather than in the paradigm, and present RASR (Reinforced Amortized Symbolic Regression), a method with two key changes to the training recipe. First, we design a synthetic prior that narrows the gap with real-world data: inputs come from the prior of a tabular foundation model; constants are sampled bottom-up, conditioned on the data; targets carry heteroscedastic and structured noise; and everything is standardized. Second, we split training into two stages. Supervised pre-training maximizes the token-level likelihood of a reference expression. This is followed by reinforcement-learning post-training that aligns the model with its inference-time use by rewarding held-out fit and penalizing expression size. On the black-box track of SRBench 2.0, RASR achieves the best mean test $R^2$ rank of all evaluated methods. Three RASR variants, trained with different size penalties, make up most of the accuracy-complexity Pareto front. On Strogatz, our method recovers more ground-truth expressions than any baseline, and on Feynman it is competitive with the best-performing methods.

metadata_records.title: Benchmarking Self-Supervised 3D Medical Vision Foundation Models and Transferability Estimation
metadata_records.abstract: Self-supervised pretraining has expanded the pool of 3D medical foundation models, but published evaluations use different datasets, endpoints and fine-tuning protocols. Models also differ in architecture, pretraining objective and data, while downstream targets range from voxel-level masks to patient-level diagnoses and outcomes. As a result, published findings provide little directly comparable evidence for choosing a model for a new task. Direct comparison of adaptation performance requires fine-tuning candidates on labelled target data, at substantial computational cost. We benchmark 23 candidates across the same 14 segmentation, classification and regression tasks spanning multiple anatomies and modalities. No candidate ranked among the top three across all segmentation tasks or across all classification and regression tasks; a convolutional encoder could outperform a transformer trained with the same objective on one task but underperform it on another. We benchmark transferability estimators against the fine-tuned rankings and find that their agreement varies across dense segmentation, classification and regression. InsightRank uses task-appropriate frozen-feature statistics and architecture-aware pairwise comparisons to rank candidates before fine-tuning. Across the 23-model pool, mean Kendall tau-b was 0.431 for segmentation and 0.352 for classification and regression. The segmentation Top 3 contained a task winner on four of nine tasks; the image-level Top 3 contained none on the five tasks, despite better full-ranking agreement than the matched conventional estimators. A three-model shortlist reduced recorded extraction-plus-training job time by 85.8% across seven segmentation tasks. Together, the benchmark provides a common reference for model selection and InsightRank offers a lower-cost way to prioritize fine-tuning, with shortlist performance that differs by target type.

metadata_records.title: The Midas Touch for Metric Depth: Interpretable Metricization for Generalizable Depth Perception
metadata_records.abstract: Recent foundation models have drastically improved the generalization of monocular relative depth estimation, yet recovering accurate metric depth from their estimates for depth perception tasks remains challenging due to scale ambiguity and local metric-scale inconsistency. Existing approaches recover metric depth from sparse observations using either explicit global affine transformation algorithms or implicit data-driven depth completion networks. The former cannot accommodate spatially varying relative-to-metric relationships, while the latter are sensitive to the distribution of sparse observations and may not fully exploit generalizable relative depth priors. To simultaneously address these issues, this study extends our previous work MTD and proposes MTDv2, a hybrid metric depth perception framework that combines explicit depth metricization with data-driven metric depth refinement. The explicit depth metricization process performs segment-wise affine transformations to recover spatially varying metric scales while preserving the geometric structure of relative depth, followed by pixel-wise depth refinement that propagates metric observations along paths with minimal accumulated geometric variation. The data-driven depth refinement process subsequently extends the explicit single-path depth propagation to a learnable multi-path formulation while preserving its interpretability. Extensive experiments conducted on 16 public datasets demonstrate the robust and generalizable depth scale recovery capability of MTDv2 across diverse sources of sparse observations and different depth estimation paradigms, as well as its broad applicability to downstream 3D perception tasks. Code will be publicly available at https://mias.group/MTD upon publication.

metadata_records.title: Deep Speech Representations Track Word Timing along a Low-Dimensional Circular Trajectory
metadata_records.abstract: Speech timing is fundamental for speech models to recognize words accurately, but how word-timing information is represented in speech models remains underexplored. We study this question using the framework of representational geometry, which investigates whether and how concepts are represented in low-dimensional subspaces of the representation space. Prior work in cognitive neuroscience has shown that when HuBERT feature sequences are averaged across words of the same duration, they form near-circular trajectories from word onset to word offset in a two-dimensional "temporal subspace." Here we show that this circular structure of word timing is a general property of deep speech representations, by demonstrating its emergence in nine additional speech models covering both supervised and self-supervised. We then move beyond averaged word segments and show that in HuBERT, the circular trajectories are consistent enough at the level of individual words to perform word segmentation. Our approach, Rotary Segmentation (RoSeg), achieves 64.3% boundary F-score on Librispeech by detecting word boundaries when cycles complete in the temporal subspace. Although supervision is needed to identify a good subspace, nevertheless this result demonstrates much stronger implicit word knowledge in HuBERT than has previously been shown.

metadata_records.title: When Trackers Fail: VLM-Guided Verification and Recovery for Robust Video Object Segmentation
metadata_records.abstract: Recent trackers built on foundation models such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM) achieve strong performance by propagating object masks through memory. However, this strength is also a key source of failure: under occlusion, reappearance, or distractors, an incorrect prediction can enter the tracking loop and be propagated over time, resulting in persistent identity drift. Existing approaches seek to prevent such failures through improved memory and temporal modeling, but once a failure occurs, the tracker has no explicit mechanism to recognize or correct it. We address this gap with Dual-Agent, a failure-aware tracking framework that complements propagation with explicit verification and recovery. We address this gap with Dual-Agent, a failure-aware tracking framework that complements propagation with explicit verification and recovery. A vision-language verification agent first reasons over spatio-temporal context to determine whether the tracker is still following the target. When a failure is detected, a correction agent uses temporal context to recover the target before tracking continues. The correction agent is trained on real SAM3 failures, augmented with targeted identity-switch and distractor perturbations that expose it to challenging ambiguities during recovery. On LVOS-v2 and SecVOS, Dual-Agent improves SAM3 by 1.2 and 2.7 $J\&F$, respectively. Importantly, the proposed framework transfers without retraining to SAM2.1, SeC, and Cutie, as well as to long-term video object tracking benchmarks including LaSOT-ext, TNL2K, and VOT-LT2022. Our results show that explicitly reasoning about when tracking fails and how to recover provides a complementary path to robust tracking beyond improving propagation alone. Project page: valaybundele.github.io/Dual-Agent.

However, this strength is also a key source of failure: under occlusion, reappearance, or distractors, an incorrect prediction can enter the tracking loop and be propagated over time, resulting in persistent identity drift. Existing approaches seek to prevent such failures through improved memory and temporal modeling, but once a failure occurs, the tracker has no explicit mechanism to recognize or correct it. We address this gap with Dual-Agent, a failure-aware tracking framework that complements propagation with explicit verification and recovery. We address this gap with Dual-Agent, a failure-aware tracking framework that complements propagation with explicit verification and recovery. A vision-language verification agent first reasons over spatio-temporal context to determine whether the tracker is still following the target. When a failure is detected, a correction agent uses temporal context to recover the target before tracking continues. The correction agent is trained on real SAM3 failures, augmented with targeted identity-switch and distractor perturbations that expose it to challenging ambiguities during recovery. On LVOS-v2 and SecVOS, Dual-Agent improves SAM3 by 1.2 and 2.7 $J\&F$, respectively. Importantly, the proposed framework transfers without retraining to SAM2.1, SeC, and Cutie, as well as to long-term video object tracking benchmarks including LaSOT-ext, TNL2K, and VOT-LT2022. Our results show that explicitly reasoning about when tracking fails and how to recover provides a complementary path to robust tracking beyond improving propagation alone. metadata_records.title: P-BFM: Perceptive Behavioral Foundation Models for Humanoid Control via Unsupervised Reinforcement Learning
metadata_records.abstract: Behavioral foundation models (BFMs) provide humanoids with reusable repertoires of whole-body behaviors; in real-world humanoid control, the same behavioral intent may require fundamentally different motions under different terrain constraints. Covering such variation with terrain-matched demonstrations requires enumerating a combinatorial space of behaviors and terrain geometries. We introduce P-BFM, a perceptive behavioral foundation model that factorizes humanoid control into terrain-invariant intent and terrain-conditioned realization. A forward-backward representation maps motion references, target states, and reward functions into a shared intent space without terrain information, while a perceptive policy learns how to realize each intent under the surrounding terrain geometry. We further identify a complementary limitation of purely latent control: behavioral latents can preserve local motion patterns while losing precise global progress. We therefore introduce Explicit Root Instructions (ERI), which separates global transport (e.g., heading and planar velocity) from behavioral intent, while leaving local whole-body adaptation to the perceptive policy. This decomposition leads to a characteristic capability absent from conventional BFMs: one fixed intent induces different, terrain-appropriate behaviors, including changes in step height, stride, posture, foothold placement, and contacts, without terrain-specific demonstrations. Across challenging terrains, P-BFM improves motion fidelity, root-control precision, and perturbation recovery over strong baselines. A single frozen policy further supports motion tracking, goal reaching, reward inference, teleoperation, and terrain-aware recovery, and transfers zero-shot to a Unitree G1 using onboard depth sensing.

metadata_records.title: SlotAVS: Object-Centric Audio-Visual Segmentation via Bi-Modal Slot Attention
metadata_records.abstract: Audio-Visual Segmentation (AVS) requires predicting pixel-wise masks of sounding objects by grounding acoustic signals in visual space. In multi-source scenes, concurrent sound sources often remain entangled within shared visual representations, leading to merged masks or unstable specialization when using standard alignment-focused transformer architectures. To address this, we present SlotAVS, an object-centric framework driven by competitive bi-modal slot attention. While robust foundation models provide rich semantic priors, SlotAVS shifts the paradigm from global cross-modal fusion to explicit competitive binding. By initializing discrete object slots from temporal audio sequences and enforcing strict slot-wise competition over spatial visual tokens, our method structurally mitigates the blending of distinct acoustic entities. Further, to stabilize instance-level learning, we introduce a Hungarian matching strategy that optimally aligns slots with ground-truth objects using spatial and boundary overlap. Coupled with a numerically stable, confidence-aware mask fusion mechanism, SlotAVS robustly aggregates multi-source predictions. Extensive experiments on the AVSBench dataset demonstrate the efficacy of our approach, achieving 88.6% mIoU on the Single-Source (S4) split and 71.7% mIoU on the Multi-Source (MS3) split. These results show that explicit competitive binding is critical for complex audio-visual scene understanding and effectively leveraging foundation-model priors without relying solely on their capacity.

metadata_records.title: Sparse All-Layer Connector for Domain Generalised Semantic Segmentation
metadata_records.abstract: Domain generalised semantic segmentation (DGSS) has recently benefited from combining multiple foundation models, such as vision-language and vision foundation models, to leverage their diverse representations for generalisation. Existing multi-model approaches share a common design choice: cross-model fusion is restricted to depth-aligned layers, implicitly assuming that mutually beneficial information resides at the same depth across models. However, foundation models pretrained under different objectives may develop distinct representation hierarchies, making the optimality of depth-aligned fusion questionable. Moreover, we observe that the foundation models exhibit different depth-wise domain sensitivity. Motivated by these observations, we propose a Sparse All-Layer Connector (SALC) that enables each layer to access information from preceding layers of another model. As the number of accessible layers grows with depth, dense aggregation may hurt generalisation. SALC therefore learns to adaptively select a sparse subset of informative layers. We further introduce a candidate dropout regularisation that strengthens sparsity and encourages SALC to explore diverse layers, leading to more robust selection. Across four foundation model combinations and three DGSS evaluation settings, the proposed design demonstrates stronger generalisation than conventional depth-aligned fusion. The code is available at https://github.com/RuoyuGuo/SALC.

metadata_records.title: Gugak-VocalSet: A Multi-Genre Studio-Quality Dataset of Korean Traditional Singing with Sigimsae Annotations
metadata_records.abstract: We present Gugak-VocalSet, the first publicly available audio dataset for Korean traditional singing with dense annotations of sigimsae, a structured pitch contour system of vocal expressions. Gugak-VocalSet contains 24.5 hours of unaccompanied solo vocal recordings across 305 tracks of representative repertoire curated by the National Gugak Center, performed by 20 professional singers in a controlled studio environment with fixed key and tempo. In addition to genre, lyrics, and mood/timbre tags, the dataset provides a unified sigimsae ontology and approximately 68,000 segments (71,700 instances including multi-label) of audio-grounded sigimsae annotations; the ontology adopts a functional-position-based hierarchy designed for consistent application across genres, and 14 expert annotators specializing in Korean traditional music performed segment-level labeling accordingly. Baseline experiments on sigimsae classification and event detection show that domain-informed F0 representations remain competitive with, and on classification surpass, frozen probing of a general-purpose music foundation model, while pitch and spectral cues play complementary roles in event-level detection. Companion page: https://www.danbinaerin.com/Gugak-VocalSet/

In addition to genre, lyrics, and mood/timbre tags, the dataset provides a unified sigimsae ontology and approximately 68,000 segments (71,700 instances including multi-label) of audio-grounded sigimsae annotations; the ontology adopts a functional-position-based hierarchy designed for consistent application across genres, and 14 expert annotators specializing in Korean traditional music performed segment-level labeling accordingly. Baseline experiments on sigimsae classification and event detection show that domain-informed F0 representations remain competitive with, and on classification surpass, frozen probing of a general-purpose music foundation model, while pitch and spectral cues play complementary roles in event-level detection. Companion page: https://www.danbinaerin.com/Gugak-VocalSet/

metadata_records.title: Drive3R: Block-wise Streaming Geometric Foundation Models for Autonomous Driving
metadata_records.abstract: High-fidelity closed-loop simulation for autonomous driving increasingly relies on dense multi-view 3D reconstruction. While recent feed-forward geometric foundation models have revolutionized per-scene optimization, applying them to continuous, long-horizon driving sequences is computationally intractable due to GPU memory limits and the quadratic complexity of global attention. Existing scaling strategies are fundamentally limited, as causal streaming suffers from compounding scale drift and trajectory deviation, while rigid "chunk-then-align" heuristics fragment global context and produce trajectory discontinuities. To address these limitations, we introduce Drive3R, a block-wise streaming geometric foundation model. Its block-wise causal attention resolves the scalability bottleneck of fully bidirectional attention while avoiding the loss of local future context in purely causal streaming. Its confidence-aware re-anchoring further mitigates long-range drift by detecting unreliable streaming states, re-initializing the KV cache, and stitching refreshed segments through SE(3) alignment. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Drive3R establishes a new state-of-the-art on nuScenes, KITTI, and Waymo. Specifically, on nuScenes, it improves over the recent DVGT-2 baseline from 0.1806 to 0.1081 in AbsRel, from 0.6750 to 0.5344 in point-cloud Accuracy, and from 1.5812 to 0.9092 in ATE.

metadata_records.title: CowCare: A Unified Visual Framework for Viewpoint-Robust Cattle Tracking and Spatiotemporal Heat-Stress Analysis
metadata_records.abstract: Reliable individual monitoring is essential for dairy cattle welfare and early heat stress detection in Precision Livestock Farming (PLF). However, translating raw multi-camera videos into automated diagnostics remains challenging due to disconnected tracking and recognition pipelines and complex physical environments. Dense mutual occlusions and cross-camera viewpoint variations fragment identities, while environmental noise, including camera vibrations, and limited agricultural data obscure subtle heat stress cues such as rapid breathing and flank undulations. To bridge low-level visual features and high-level behavioral diagnostics, we propose CowCare, a unified framework combining viewpoint-robust tracking with spatiotemporal heat stress recognition. Its tracking module, CowTrack, maintains cross-camera identity consistency through a View-Decoupled Aggregation Network (VDA-Net). Instead of relying on static global representations, VDA-Net aggregates localized textures under heavy occlusion and uses a Viewpoint Decoupling Transformer (VDT) to suppress transient viewpoint variations. CowTrack further incorporates a causal online self-supervision mechanism for continuous adaptation to dynamic farm scenes. The resulting tracklets are subsequently processed by TSDF-Net, a fine-grained video understanding network. Its Temporal Stabilization and Aggregation Module (TSAM) suppresses high-frequency jitter, while a Diffusion Semantic Prior (DSP) uses frozen pre-trained diffusion semantics to enhance subtle behavioral signals and mitigate overfitting. Extensive evaluations on two real-world farm benchmarks demonstrate the framework's effectiveness: CowTrack achieves 83.48% HOTA and 87.72% IDF1 for global multi-object tracking on MVCow, and TSDF-Net achieves 87.72% Top-1 accuracy on HSCow. These results establish CowCare as a robust end-to-end framework for automated livestock health monitoring.

metadata_records.title: TAG: Calibrating SAM3 for Universal Image Segmentation without Dense Supervision
metadata_records.abstract: The recent Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM3) extends powerful promptable segmentation from spatial cues to concepts, raising the prospect of a single foundation model for universal image segmentation. However, this promise often fails to translate into reliable performance on downstream segmentation tasks. In this work, we empirically identify concept recognition, rather than mask quality, as the primary bottleneck: SAM3 accurately delineates the objects it recognizes yet struggles to robustly determine which concepts are present. Driven by this, we present \textit{\underline{T}ext \underline{A}nchor re-\underline{G}rounding (\TAG{})}, a simple yet effective framework that rectifies the concept recognition of SAM3 on the target domain without dense annotations. Specifically, \TAG{} introduces an \textit{Anchor Residual Pathway} comprising image-conditioned, low-rank adapters to re-ground text anchors in the target distribution and modulate subsequent text-conditioned interactions. Guided solely by image-level category labels, \TAG{} jointly optimizes binary cross-entropy with \textit{Soft Boundary Ranking} objectives to calibrate presence confidence and distinguish present concepts from confusable negatives. Building upon this, we devise \textit{Confidence-Weighted Distillation} to couple rich semantic context of a multimodal large language model with fine-grained spatial priors of SAM3, thereby achieving effective calibration in the absence of manual annotations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that \TAG{} unlocks SAM3's segmentation potential with only 3.1M trainable parameters, achieving impressive performance across diverse scenarios, and notably, even surpassing leading mask-supervised methods on several metrics. \href{https://github.com/MiSsU-HH/TAG_SAM3}{Our code will be publicly available at GitHub \faGithub}.

metadata_records.title: From Field to Planning: Learning Temporal Polar Gradient Fields for Vision-based AAV Trajectory Planning in Dynamic Environments
metadata_records.abstract: Autonomous Aerial Vehicle (AAV) trajectory planning requires real-time and accurate safety gradient guidance, especially in dynamic environments. Existing methods typically rely on static maps and dynamic obstacle tracking to construct gradient fields, imposing heavy computational burdens and yielding conservative trajectories. To address these limitations, we propose a two-stage Field-to-Planning (F2P) learning framework to provide accurate and efficient safety gradients for trajectory planning in dynamic environments. In the first stage, we introduce an Ego-centric Polar Occupancy (EPO) representation that naturally matches the geometry of the onboard camera frustum, while supporting unstructured scene modeling. Subsequently, we formulate a Temporal Polar Gradient Field (TPGF) via multi-kernel separable Gaussian convolution to provide unified safety gradients, without explicitly distinguishing between static and dynamic obstacles. To mitigate the inherent spatial ambiguity introduced by applying convolutions within the polar grid, we propose an ESDF-guided offline learning strategy that incorporates geometric priors into TPGF. In the second stage, we employ the calibrated TPGF to guide the trajectory planning policy in a self-supervised learning manner. Comparative results with other approaches demonstrate the superiority of our method. Extensive real-world experiments within various cluttered dynamic environments validate the real-time performance and robustness on resource-constrained onboard systems.

Existing methods typically rely on static maps and dynamic obstacle tracking to construct gradient fields, imposing heavy computational burdens and yielding conservative trajectories. To address these limitations, we propose a two-stage Field-to-Planning (F2P) learning framework to provide accurate and efficient safety gradients for trajectory planning in dynamic environments. In the first stage, we introduce an Ego-centric Polar Occupancy (EPO) representation that naturally matches the geometry of the onboard camera frustum, while supporting unstructured scene modeling. Subsequently, we formulate a Temporal Polar Gradient Field (TPGF) via multi-kernel separable Gaussian convolution to provide unified safety gradients, without explicitly distinguishing between static and dynamic obstacles. To mitigate the inherent spatial ambiguity introduced by applying convolutions within the polar grid, we propose an ESDF-guided offline learning strategy that incorporates geometric priors into TPGF. In the second stage, we employ the calibrated TPGF to guide the trajectory planning policy in a self-supervised learning manner. Comparative results with other approaches demonstrate the superiority of our method. Extensive real-world experiments within various cluttered dynamic environments validate the real-time performance and robustness on resource-constrained onboard systems.

metadata_records.title: Inspect Any Crack: An Automated End-to-End Crack Segmentation and Severity Assessment Framework
metadata_records.abstract: Image-based crack analysis is essential for automated infrastructure inspection to reduce the cost, subjectivity, and safety risks of manual surveys. Despite advances in visual crack detection, methods that translate predictions into physically meaningful and engineering-interpretable crack condition information remain limited. To bridge this gap, this study proposes Inspect Any Crack (IAC), an innovative end-to-end crack recognition and condition assessment framework that automatically derives physical geometric measurements and continuous severity scores from concrete-crack imagery. At its core, IAC introduces SACv2-Tiny, an efficient crack segmentation model adapted from a vision foundation model. Trained on the challenging OmniCrack30K dataset, SACv2-Tiny achieved a $62.49\%$ F1-score and $45.45\%$ IoU on the test set and a mean zero-shot F1-score of $69.89\%$ across three unseen datasets, demonstrating robust segmentation that enables downstream analysis with limited post-processing. IAC further processes the predicted masks to quantify physical crack width and affected area using ground-sampling-distance calibration. Validation at 41 caliper-referenced locations yielded a mean relative width error of $7.33\%$. Beyond geometric quantification, IAC introduces a novel continuous crack-condition metric, the Crack Severity Index (CSI), bounded on $[0,100]$, which combines maximum crack width and affected-area ratio into a unified, standards-informed severity measure. Through these developments, IAC advances crack inspection beyond pixel-level recognition toward interpretable and automated infrastructure condition assessment.

metadata_records.title: Terrain Traversal Without Motion Priors: Expert-Routed Humanoid Locomotion at Deployment Fidelity
metadata_records.abstract: State-of-the-art perceptive humanoid locomotion is mostly built on retargeted motion capture, a generative motion prior, and a distillation stage. We report a complete system that does not require this pipeline for a humanoid to cross varied terrain. In its place, we provide a five-expert mixture routed by a terrain classifier over a sensed elevation grid, and target every foothold with a model-based planner, refined by six closed-form-gradient steps on an interpolated terrain-cost field instead of picked from a fixed grid. Driven through the same perception-to-actuation software a robot would run, inside a second, deployment-fidelity simulator, it crosses an $85$\,m five-segment waypoint course $18$ of $20$ times end-to-end ($90\%$, Wilson $95\%$ CI $70$--$97$) and succeeds $20/20$ on four of five segments scored alone, where an ablated configuration without the mixture and without refinement reaches $0\%$ on both the stair and the hurdle segment. The continuous refinement moves $72.4\%$ of foot placements across at least one grid-cell boundary, which produces real sub-grid correction. We also ran matched component studies to report what does not account for it: one expert equals five on the training distribution, four label-free routers collapse to near-uniform activation, and a self-supervised terrain embedding loses to the privileged label.

metadata_records.title: GeoReader: Learning Latent Geometry for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
metadata_records.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) struggle with metric and multi-view relationships that remain implicit in RGB observations. Geometry foundation models recover this structure from RGB, but existing methods either fuse the estimated features with visual tokens and learn to use them from question answering alone, or align VLM latents with geometry features. Capturing geometry, however, does not ensure its use: zeroing the aligned latents of a released feature-alignment model leaves its accuracy unchanged. We introduce GeoReader, a framework that learns geometric representations for the VLM that reads them. First, we train lightweight Geometric Readers to produce continuous input tokens, supervising them with geometry descriptions decoded by a frozen VLM, so that the Readers express geometry in a form the target model can already read. We then freeze the Readers to preserve this interface while fine-tuning the VLM on spatial QA, with geometry injection conditioned on the question. Geometry descriptions serve only as training targets: at inference, the VLM answers directly from the continuous geometric tokens without generating a geometry chain of thought. With geometry predicted from RGB images, our approach reaches 94.3 on MindCube-Tiny with Qwen3-VL-4B and, with a multi-source QA mixture, an average of 72.5 across six additional spatial benchmarks with Qwen3.5-9B. These results suggest that a useful geometric representation is one the receiving model can use, not merely one from which geometry can be reconstructed.

metadata_records.title: Multimodal Fusion of RGB and Complementary Modalities for Semantic Segmentation
metadata_records.abstract: Multi-modal semantic segmentation adds an auxiliary sensing stream to RGB images (RGB-X), such as thermal, LiDAR, depth, event, polarization, or light field. This can improve robustness in poor lighting and under motion blur. But different sensors often produce features that do not match well, and fusion can become unstable. To alleviate these issues, we propose a bidirectional polarity-aware cross-modality fusion (BPCF) module that effectively captures complementary cues while enhancing feature alignment. We evaluate the framework on six modality pairings: RGB-Thermal, RGB-LiDAR, RGB-Depth, RGB-Event, RGB-Polarization, and RGB-Light Field. Our model achieve state-of-the-art (SOTA) results on eight public datasets, including MFNet, KITTI-360, DELIVER, DDD17, DSEC, MCubeS, ZJU, and UrbanLF. The codes and trained models will be released upon acceptance.

This can improve robustness in poor lighting and under motion blur. But different sensors often produce features that do not match well, and fusion can become unstable. To alleviate these issues, we propose a bidirectional polarity-aware cross-modality fusion (BPCF) module that effectively captures complementary cues while enhancing feature alignment. We evaluate the framework on six modality pairings: RGB-Thermal, RGB-LiDAR, RGB-Depth, RGB-Event, RGB-Polarization, and RGB-Light Field. Our model achieve state-of-the-art (SOTA) results on eight public datasets, including MFNet, KITTI-360, DELIVER, DDD17, DSEC, MCubeS, ZJU, and UrbanLF. The codes and trained models will be released upon acceptance.

metadata_records.title: Explicitly Aligned Multi-View Breast Cancer Risk Prediction from Variable-Length Screening Histories
metadata_records.abstract: Accurate breast cancer risk prediction from screening mammography is essential for improved risk stratification and personalized screening. It can benefit from both temporal breast tissue changes across longitudinal examinations and complementary anatomical information from craniocaudal (CC) and mediolateral oblique (MLO) views. Leveraging longitudinal information requires identifying corresponding tissue regions across examinations, yet most approaches rely on implicit feature alignment without explicitly enforcing spatial consistency. Recent work has demonstrated the benefits of explicit temporal alignment; however, existing methods model each view independently, preventing them from exploiting complementary CC and MLO information. Furthermore, explicit approaches have been limited to a single prior examination. To fill these gaps, we propose (github.com/sot176/FlexLMV-Net), a breast-wise longitudinal multi-view framework that jointly models CC and MLO views across screening examinations while accommodating a variable number of prior examinations. FlexLMV-Net explicitly aligns longitudinal feature maps and integrates complementary views through cross-view temporal fusion and a dual-stream attention block. Evaluated on EMBED and CSAW-CC, FlexLMV-Net consistently outperforms existing approaches across breast density, cancer subtypes, and demographic subgroups, highlighting the benefits of explicit longitudinal alignment, multi-view modeling, and flexible use of available screening history. We further introduce (github.com/sot176/BCRBench), an open-source benchmark that unifies state-of-the-art single- and multi-timepoint breast cancer risk prediction models under standardized preprocessing, training, inference, and evaluation protocols, enabling fair and reproducible comparison of existing methods.

metadata_records.title: EventLens: Event-Structure Reinforcement Learning for Video Understanding
metadata_records.abstract: Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) achieve strong results on video question answering, yet often fail to recover the temporal structure that makes a video coherent. They may merge neighboring events, miss single-event progression, or infer implausible relations across events. We study structured temporal understanding as the ability to recover event structure from visual evidence, including event boundaries, single-event progression, and multi-event relations. We argue that this gap arises from a mismatch between current post-training objectives and temporal reasoning, where caption-style supervision allows models to rely on language shortcuts rather than visual temporal grounding. To address this, we propose EventLens, a vision-centric reinforcement learning framework that learns video understanding through event-structure recovery. Instead of reconstructing captions, EventLens trains models to recover temporal structure under controlled perturbations, such as altered temporal granularity, reversed progression, and shuffled event order. We instantiate this framework with a three-level temporal ontology and derive three verifiable task families: event segmentation, progression discrimination, and multi-event relation reasoning. These tasks admit deterministic rewards, enabling task-specialized GRPO training without human preference labels or learned reward models. We further introduce multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MT-OPD) to consolidate specialized policies into a unified model. Experiments on Qwen3-VL backbones show consistent improvements on temporal grounding and event-sensitive reasoning benchmarks, while preserving general video-QA performance. Learning curves further demonstrate that EventLens achieves comparable downstream transfer with significantly reduced training cost compared to direct mixed RL optimization.

metadata_records.title: LightVAE: Towards Compact and Efficient Video Autoencoders
metadata_records.abstract: Latent diffusion models enable high-quality video generation, but video VAE encoding and decoding remain computationally expensive. Existing methods use stage-specific lightweight operators, yet either constrain spatial and temporal computation jointly or remove temporal computation altogether, without distinguishing their compression sensitivities in pretrained Conv3D. To address these limitations, we present LightVAE, a compression framework that exploits redundancy in temporal modeling and network depth. LightVAE exactly reparameterizes eligible causal Conv3D layers into an aggregate spatial response and a difference-driven temporal correction. Based on their distinct compression sensitivities, temporal low-rank compression (TLR) keeps the aggregate spatial kernel dense and applies layer-specific low-rank approximation only to the temporal correction. An algebraically equivalent folded implementation converts the arithmetic savings into practical acceleration. LightVAE further uses width-preserving block pruning to reduce depth and probe-guided feature alignment, guided by feedback from a frozen teacher suffix, to recover quality after compression. The framework also extends to video encoders. Across three video VAE backbones and two GPU platforms, LightVAE consistently accelerates decoding. For the Wan VAE family, it achieves up to $2.24\times$ and $1.11\times$ the decoding throughput of state-of-the-art efficient VAE decoders on NVIDIA H100 and RTX~5090, respectively, with higher DAVIS PSNR and lower LPIPS. On MiniMax-H3, it achieves up to $2.97\times$ the original decoding throughput while retaining 99.51\% of the original model's overall VBench-2.0 score. Our code is available at https://github.com/ModelTC/LightVAE.

metadata_records.title: Bidirectional Adaptive Transformers for Multimodal Anomaly Detection
metadata_records.abstract: The effective integration of features derived from RGB images and 3D point clouds presents a substantial challenge in the field of multimodal anomaly detection (MAD). Existing MAD methods typically rely on static fusion paradigms built upon frozen pre-trained encoders. While these frameworks facilitate spatial alignment, they lack the mechanism to establish latent semantic correspondence, thereby inducing cross-modal interference that degrades anomaly discriminability. To mitigate these limitations, this study proposes a Bidirectional Adaptive Transformers (BAT) framework, which constructs comprehensive and semantically aligned multimodal representations by leveraging complementary attributes across modalities. The BAT framework introduces a Bidirectional Feature Alignment (BFA) module, which employs a mutual predictive mechanism to bridge the gap between 2D textural patterns and 3D geometric structures. This bidirectional interaction explicitly enhances the textural granularity of point cloud descriptors while augmenting the spatial contextual awareness of RGB features. To ensure that the latent representations possess sufficient informational density for alignment, BAT incorporates a parameter-efficient adaptation architecture. By utilizing lightweight image and point cloud adapters, the framework facilitates specialized fine-tuning of pre-trained models, mitigating the information loss inherent in frozen encoders. Extensive experiments conducted on MVTec 3D-AD and Eyecandies confirm that BAT achieves state-of-the-art anomaly detection performance, significantly outperforming existing MAD methods.

To mitigate these limitations, this study proposes a Bidirectional Adaptive Transformers (BAT) framework, which constructs comprehensive and semantically aligned multimodal representations by leveraging complementary attributes across modalities. The BAT framework introduces a Bidirectional Feature Alignment (BFA) module, which employs a mutual predictive mechanism to bridge the gap between 2D textural patterns and 3D geometric structures. This bidirectional interaction explicitly enhances the textural granularity of point cloud descriptors while augmenting the spatial contextual awareness of RGB features. To ensure that the latent representations possess sufficient informational density for alignment, BAT incorporates a parameter-efficient adaptation architecture. By utilizing lightweight image and point cloud adapters, the framework facilitates specialized fine-tuning of pre-trained models, mitigating the information loss inherent in frozen encoders. Extensive experiments conducted on MVTec 3D-AD and Eyecandies confirm that BAT achieves state-of-the-art anomaly detection performance, significantly outperforming existing MAD methods.

metadata_records.title: Design Choices for Multimodal Transformer Learning with Missing and Longitudinal Healthcare Data
metadata_records.abstract: Multimodal learning offers the potential to improve predictions by integrating complementary information from heterogeneous data sources. However, multimodal datasets are frequently incomplete, raising important questions about how models should handle missing information. Although recent approaches increasingly rely on Transformer-based architectures for multimodal fusion, incomplete multimodal data introduces challenges such as missing modalities and intra-modal missingness, which motivate key architectural design choices, such as tokenization granularity. In addition, many datasets are longitudinal, with observations collected across multiple time points. The sequential nature of the Transformer architectures provides a natural framework for modeling such data, but introduces additional considerations, such as how temporal information should be represented. In this study, we systematically investigate these design choices using three different cancer datasets. We compare modality-level and feature-level tokenization and evaluate attention masking and imputation as strategies for handling missing information, both naturally occurring in the datasets and synthetically induced. We further investigate approaches for incorporating temporal information in our training process and how to model it. Experiments are conducted with unimodal and multimodal configurations, as well as different levels of missingness for binary survival classification and multiple time encoding strategies for discrete-time survival prediction. Our results show that while multimodal outperforms unimodal results, missing data heavily impacts predictions and thus effective design choices such as tokenization granularity, and intra-missing handling is essential for reliable prediction.

metadata_records.title: A Lightweight SAR Ship Classification Method based on VV/VH Dual-Polarization Fusion and Knowledge Distillation
metadata_records.abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) can acquire clear and reliable radar images under complex weather conditions such as rain and fog, offering significant research and application value in maritime surveillance, port monitoring, and ship target recognition. However, existing SAR ship target classification models still face challenges of large parameter counts and low inference efficiency in edge computing scenarios, and the classification performance for certain target categories remains unsatisfactory in practical situations involving limited samples and imbalanced data. To address these issues, this paper adopts a lightweight SAR ship target classification approach that combines VV-VH dual-polarization feature fusion with model compression. Using OpenSARShip_uint8 as the experimental dataset, the method first constructs dual-channel inputs that leverage the complementary scattering response information from VV and VH polarization channels to enhance the model's ability to represent ship structural and textural features, thereby improving classification stability. Second, to build a high-quality teacher model, this paper employs VGG16 pre-trained on ImageNet and designs a two-stage training strategy: in the first stage, the feature extraction layers are frozen and only the classifier is trained; in the second stage, all network parameters are unfrozen, and a differentiated learning rate strategy is applied for fine-tuning the entire network-a smaller learning rate is used for the feature extraction layers to preserve pre-trained features, while a relatively larger learning rate is used for the classifier to accelerate adaptation, combined with cosine annealing scheduling to gradually decay the learning rate. This strategy helps improve the model's capacity to represent fine-grained features in SAR images and mitigates, to a certain extent, the model bias caused by data imbalance. Furthermore, knowledge distillation is employed to transfer the feature learning capability of the teacher model to a lightweight student model, significantly reducing the model size while preserving recognition accuracy as much as possible. Experimental results show that the teacher model achieves a test accuracy of 74.08%, while the distilled student model attains a test accuracy of 73.86% with only a 0.22% accuracy degradation. Despite the moderate absolute classification accuracy limited by speckle noise, inter-class scattering ambiguity and dataset imbalance, the proposed distillation framework drastically shrinks the model scale: parameters drop from 18.92M to 1.24M, storage footprint falls from 72.17MB to 4.74MB, and single-image inference latency decreases from 1.93ms to 0.71ms.

metadata_records.title: A systematic review of digital twins as decision support systems: a classification framework and identification of organisational constraints
metadata_records.abstract: Digital twins (DTs) are increasingly framed as decision support systems (DSSs), yet no framework has systematically examined how DT configuration shapes the decision support they provide. This study presents a systematic literature review of 299 studies from four databases, using Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) to examine how DT configuration influences decision support and value realisation. We develop a four-dimensional classification framework comprising abstraction level, DSS mechanism, decision level, and value type, and statistically test the relationships between these dimensions. The results show that DTs support decisions through four distinct mechanisms that differ in how information flows and how involved the decision maker remains. Model-driven DTs, which compute answers through embedded models, take on more of the reasoning themselves, whereas knowledge-driven DTs, which let users explore scenarios, keep decision makers actively involved. Whether a DT delivers value depends on organisational conditions as much as on its technical capability. Fully automated decisions are rare and occur mainly in model-driven DTs, suggesting that governance and accountability, rather than technology, limit automation. Model-driven DTs are also seldom used for long-term strategic decisions, as are DTs that represent only a single component rather than a wider system or enterprise. These patterns have been stable over time and do not appear to be driven by the uneven spread of studies across industries. Overall, the findings indicate that DT value depends on alignment with organisational decision contexts rather than technical sophistication alone. This paper highlights organisational and governance factors that cannot be captured by purely technical analyses.
first_author_affiliations: University of Cambridge

metadata_records.title: SDPAD: A Fully Spike-Driven Pipeline for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
metadata_records.abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving demands trajectory planners that are both highly accurate and cheap enough for edge deployment. State-of-the-art artificial neural network (ANN) planners meet the accuracy requirement at the cost of heavy dense computation, while spiking neural networks (SNNs)---though promising orders-of-magnitude energy savings through sparse, event-driven arithmetic---still lag far behind in planning accuracy. We present \textbf{SDPAD}, a fully spike-driven end-to-end planning pipeline that closes this gap. SDPAD converts a pre-trained ANN perception stack into integer-spike form via quantized ANN2SNN conversion, lifts multi-view images into the bird's-eye-view (BEV) space with a spike-driven-max (SDM) depth distribution (Spike-3D-Lift), and plans through the Spike-QFormer, a spiking query transformer in which ego, agent, and map queries distilled from the BEV scene are fused by learnable waypoint queries via cross-attention, followed by deformable spike-cross-attention refinement. Every operation is gated by integer spikes and inference is a single feed-forward pass without temporal simulation loops. On the nuScenes open-loop benchmark, SDPAD achieves an average $L_2$ error of 0.40\,m and a collision rate of 0.12\%, on par with strong ANN planners while consuming 69.9\,mJ---less than 2\% of recent ANN baselines. In closed-loop evaluation on the NAVSIM navtest split, SDPAD reaches 86.3 PDMS, surpassing the previous SNN planner SAD by 4.3 points and matching mainstream ANN planners at a fraction of their energy. To our knowledge, SDPAD is the first fully spike-driven planner evaluated in end-to-end autonomous driving, demonstrating that SNNs can rival dense ANNs in complex driving tasks.

SDPAD 转换预训 ANN 通过定量将感官堆栈成整数-spike形式 ANN2SNN 转换,将多视图图像提升到鸟眼视图 (BEV) 带有 sping- max 的空间 (SDM) 深度分布(Spike-3D-Lift), 并通过 Spike- QFormer 计划, 一个尖端查询 Transformer 在其中,自我、代理和地图 查询从 BEV 场景通过可学习的路标查询通过交叉注意连接,然后是可变形的悬索交叉注意的改进. 每一个操作都通过整数突起来门,推论是没有时间模拟环的单个向导通道. 打开 nuScenes 开放基准, SDPAD 实现平均值 $L_2$ 错误 0.40\,m和碰撞率 0.12\%, 与强势相当 ANN 规划者在消费时 69.9\,mJ---less 超过 2\% 最近的报告 ANN 基线。 在对 NAVSIM 导航分割, SDPAD 达到 86.3 PDMS, 超过上一个 SNN 规划员 SAD 由 4.3 点和匹配主流 ANN 计划者们的能量只有一小部分 据我们所知, SDPAD 是首个在端到端自主驾驶中被评价的完全由尖锐驱动的规划师,表明SNN在复杂的驾驶任务中可以与密集的ANN进行竞争..

metadata_records.title: The rise of agentic AI in drug discovery from static tools to autonomous virtual scientists
metadata_records.abstract: Driven by large language models, AI agents are transforming drug discovery, enabling AI to break free from task-specific tools and advance toward the vision of autonomous virtual scientists. This perspective reviews applications across the R&D lifecycle. To evaluate system maturity, we introduce a 6-level "Spectrum of Agentic Autonomy." We advocate for novel evaluation paradigms centered on full-chain traceability and outline adoption barriers, positioning AI agents as pragmatic scientist-in-the-loop co-pilots.
first_author_affiliations: College of Pharmaceutical Sciences, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China

metadata_records.title: Joint detection and state recognition of traffic lights and signs through a lightweight hybrid CNN–transformer framework
metadata_records.abstract: Abstract Accurate detection of traffic lights and signs is a critical task for safe autonomous vehicle systems (AVS). Despite advances in deep learning, most methods treat traffic light detection, traffic sign detection, and state recognition as separate tasks, while CNN-based models lack global context modeling and transformer-based approaches incur high computational cost. To address these limitations, this study presents a unified and lightweight YOLOv11–EfficientViT framework that jointly performs traffic light detection, traffic sign detection, and traffic light state recognition within a single end-to-end architecture. The proposed method integrates convolutional block attention modules (CBAM) into the YOLOv11 backbone for enhanced local feature refinement and incorporates an efficient vision transformer (EfficientViT) module to capture global contextual dependencies with reduced computational cost. A multi-task loss formulation is adopted to simultaneously optimize localization and semantic state recognition. Experiments were conducted on curated, task-focused subset of BDD100K dataset for traffic light detection and state recognition and TT100K dataset for traffic sign detection. On BDD100K, the proposed model achieved 99.4% mean average precision (mAP@0.5), 92.2% mAP@[0.5:0.95], and 97.7% traffic light state recognition accuracy under the defined experimental setting while maintaining inference at 3.8 ms per frame. On TT100K, the framework attained 96.5% mAP@0.5 and 81.2% mAP@[0.5:0.95] with only 2.5M parameters. Cross-dataset evaluation on subsets of LISA and Bosch datasets further indicates promising cross-dataset transferability with limited performance variation under domain shift. The results indicate that the hybrid integration of attention-enhanced convolutional features and lightweight transformer-based global reasoning enhances detection performance and semantic consistency without compromising computational efficiency.
first_author_affiliations: Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj University, Kanpur, UP, India

metadata_records.title: Cross-Domain Outdoor Scene UnderstandingUsing PC-GAN and TL-SZKSE-DenseNet inAdverse Weather Conditions
metadata_records.abstract: In autonomous driving, Outdoor Scene (OS) understanding in unfavorable weather conditions is pivotal forenabling safe navigation. Conventional studies failed to capture the intricate pairwise object relationship within scenesin OS classification. To mitigate these challenges, this research introduces a dual framework bringing together aPanoptic Cycle-Generative Adversarial Network (PC-GAN) with a Transfer Learning-based Squeeze-and-ZeroKnowledge Spatial Excitation DenseNet (TL-SZKSE-DenseNet). The suggested PC-GAN achieves realistic crossweather image translation with semantically aligned representations in clear and degraded scenes. The TL-SZKSEDenseNet improves feature learning with the addition of a zero-knowledge spatial excitation mechanism that selectivelyenhances weather-independent and context-dependent features for enhanced discrimination in crowded scenes. Thisgenerative–discriminative hybrid method effectively overcomes structured and unstructured driving domain gaps, asdemonstrated on benchmark datasets such as BDD and IndiaScene365. Primarily, the OS images are generalized toadverse conditions using Panoptic Cycle-Generative Adversarial Network (PC-GAN). After that, using saliencymapping, the most significant regions in the generalized output are highlighted. In the meantime, the significant featuresare extracted utilizing the Orangutan Optimization Algorithm (OOA). In addition, from the detected objects, the ObjectFrequency and Relationship (OFR) is analyzed. Later, using TL-SZKSE-DenseNet, the OS are classified based on theOFR and the selected features. The performance of our proposed approach was tested on our newly developedIndiaScene365 dataset as well as various benchmark datasets such as BDD100k. Our newly developed dataset,IndiaScene365, includes 3000 images that entail three different weather conditions, which are foggy weather, rainyweather, and poor light conditions along with clear day weather. The proposed approach records 94.87% accuracy,93.24%, and 94.18% sensitivity on our dataset.

metadata_records.title: Real-time speed bump detection using YOLOv8 and embedded vision for adaptive braking assistance in electric vehicles
metadata_records.abstract: There are many unmarked speed bumps on our roads, which cause discomfort and damage to EVs and cars, including body damage, shock to occupants, and hard braking of the electric motor. This paper proposes a real-time embedded system for speed bump detection and a corresponding algorithm to activate the intelligent braking system of an EV, implementable in even the lowest grade of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS). The base model used is YOLOv8-small, trained using transfer learning weights on a custom dataset of approximately 2000 images scraped from Mendeley and Kaggle, covering a wide range of bump shapes and sizes. The images are annotated in Roboflow by drawing polygons for the class "speed bump." The model is trained on Google Colab GPU for approximately 150 epochs and implemented on a Raspberry Pi 4 with 8 GB of RAM and a Pi Camera V2. The vehicle braking is controlled via a PWM signal through the L298N H-bridge driver, with GPIO-based audio-visual alerting also implemented. The YOLOv8 model achieved a precision of 0.9777, recall of 0.9977, mAP@50 of 0.9958, mAP@50–95 of 0.8577, and an F1 score of 0.99. On the Raspberry Pi 4, the system achieves a raw inference rate of 0.84 FPS (~1522 ms) and effective decision pipeline throughput of 8–10 FPS via frame-skipping. Model performance on a Mac M3 GPU achieved 43.03 FPS. The proposed system is highly scalable and cost-effective, deployable as a low-cost ADAS module in EVs to improve passenger safety and extend vehicle life across varied road surfaces.

metadata_records.title: A monocular vision-based method using DL-YOLO for fire detection and localization in road tunnels
metadata_records.abstract: Vision-based fire detection and localization in road tunnels remain challenging due to complex illumination, multi-scale fire targets, the lack of realistic tunnel fire datasets, and the unsolved problem of smoke backflow front positioning. To address these issues, we propose DL‑YOLO, a unified framework integrating an enhanced YOLOv8n detector with a monocular geometric localization module. The detector incorporates SPD‑Conv to preserve fine‑grained details under low contrast, a global attention mechanism to suppress tunnel‑specific interferences, an auxiliary P2 head to improve small‑target recall, and Ghost modules for computational efficiency. A full‑scale tunnel fire dataset was constructed through experiments in six tunnels, and a relative‑scale criterion is proposed to define small targets adaptively across varying resolutions. The detector achieves 96.9% mAP@0.5 and 93.6% recall, outperforming the baseline by 2.1% and 4.7%, respectively. The localization module leverages tunnel structural priors and camera parameters to estimate spatial coordinates of both flame sources and smoke backflow fronts, achieving a mean absolute error of 0.51 m (1.55% relative) for smoke‑front positioning, and 1.00 m (1.80% relative) in longitudinal error and 0.12 m (2.7% relative) in lateral error for flame sources. Sensitivity analysis confirms that localization errors propagate predictably within practical uncertainty bounds. Both field experiments and controlled tunnel tests validate the method’s effectiveness for real‑time tunnel fire monitoring.

metadata_records.title: Oblique drone panoramic imagery for fine-scale human-induced land-cover change detection
metadata_records.abstract: Abstract High-Resolution Spatiotemporal Monitoring of Seasonal Land-Use and Land-Cover (LULC) Changes (HRST-MSLC) holds broad application prospects. However, existing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) change-detection benchmarks are predominantly based on nadir-view, bi-temporal imagery, providing limited lateral structural information and seasonal observations, while data-acquisition costs and multi-temporal registration constrain dataset construction. To address this, this paper introduces the Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Oblique Multi-View Panoramic Change Detection Dataset (UAV-OMVCD) for fine-scale human-induced LULC change monitoring. It contains 864 panoramic observations acquired in four study areas across Nanjing, Hefei, and Tangshan using DJI Matrice 4D/4TD and Matrice 4E platforms. Each panorama is exported at 1448 × 7200 pixels, with nominal nadir-equivalent source-frame ground sampling distances (GSDs) of approximately 3.7–8.5 cm, yielding 2,181 paired 512 × 512 samples. UAV-OMVCD documents seasonal changes in impervious surfaces, engineering machinery, buildings, greenhouses, and piled soil, including structural additions/removals and morphological evolution. Its oblique views capture lateral facades and occluded areas while reducing seasonal pseudo-change interference. Five benchmark models achieved overall accuracies of 0.9429–0.9492, macro-averaged F1-scores of 0.8861–0.9007, and macro-averaged Intersection over Union (IoU) values of 0.8049–0.8266. UAV-OMVCD provides a standardized benchmark for fine-scale human-induced land-cover change detection using oblique drone panoramic imagery.

To address this, this paper introduces the Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Oblique Multi-View Panoramic Change Detection Dataset (UAV-OMVCD) for fine-scale human-induced LULC change monitoring. It contains 864 panoramic observations acquired in four study areas across Nanjing, Hefei, and Tangshan using DJI Matrice 4D/4TD and Matrice 4E platforms. Each panorama is exported at 1448 × 7200 pixels, with nominal nadir-equivalent source-frame ground sampling distances (GSDs) of approximately 3.7–8.5 cm, yielding 2,181 paired 512 × 512 samples. UAV-OMVCD documents seasonal changes in impervious surfaces, engineering machinery, buildings, greenhouses, and piled soil, including structural additions/removals and morphological evolution. Its oblique views capture lateral facades and occluded areas while reducing seasonal pseudo-change interference. Five benchmark models achieved overall accuracies of 0.9429–0.9492, macro-averaged F1-scores of 0.8861–0.9007, and macro-averaged Intersection over Union (IoU) values of 0.8049–0.8266. UAV-OMVCD provides a standardized benchmark for fine-scale human-induced land-cover change detection using oblique drone panoramic imagery.

metadata_records.title: MESSENGER: Memory-Enhanced Sequential Scene Flow Estimation via Autoregressive Next-Frame Forecasting
metadata_records.abstract: Scene flow can capture low-level 3D motion displacements in dynamic scenarios. Early pairwise estimators relying on instantaneous two-frame motion lack long-term temporal correlation and also struggle with poor extrapolation ability in future prediction. Although some recent methods attempt to explore multi-frame scene flow estimation in a sequence-to-sequence manner, they typically suffer from heavy computational overhead with increasing input frames and long-horizon prediction degradation due to ineffective motion propagation. To address these problems, we propose a novel memory-enhanced sequential scene flow pipeline, called MESSENGER. To sufficiently mine long-term temporal dependencies naturally within consecutive sequences, a memory buffer is designed by explicitly storing multiple history flow estimates and latent states. For each input frame, the temporally stored flows and states are correlated and retrieved to predict the current initialized flow in a next-frame forecasting manner. Furthermore, we develop an uncertainty-aware reweighting module to filter unreliable retrievals and mitigate accumulated errors. Extensive experiments on nuScenes and Argoverse 2 demonstrate state-of-the-art performance of our MESSENGER, reducing EPE3D by 71.6% on nuScenes and 67.7% on Argoverse 2 in long-horizon future extrapolation. This superiority can be attributed to our designed autoregressive forecasting paradigm, which naturally forces the network to progressively learn the next-frame distribution based on history observations. Code will be released at https://github.com/liujiuming123/Messenger.
first_author_affiliations: University of Cambridge

translation.zh: 场景流可以捕捉动态情景中低级3D运动位移. 依靠瞬时双帧运动的早期对偶估计器缺乏长期的时间相关性,在未来的预测中也与差的推断能力作斗争. 虽然最近的一些方法试图以顺序到顺序的方式探索多帧场景流量估计,但它们通常会因输入帧增加而承受沉重的计算间接费用,而且由于运动传播效率低下而导致长视距预测退化。 为了解决这些问题,我们提出一个新的记忆增强 相继的场景流管道,叫做 MESSENGER. 为了充分挖掘连续序列中自然存在的长期时间依赖,设计了内存缓冲器,明确存储了多个历史流估计和潜伏状态. 对于每个输入框架,时间存储的流量和状态是互相关联和检索的,以便以下一个帧预测的方式预测当前初始化的流量. 此外,我们开发了一个意识到不确定性的重新加权模块,以过滤不可靠的检索并减少累积错误。 广泛试验 nuScenes 反转 2 展示我们最优秀的表演 MESSENGER, 减少 EPE3D 由 71.6% 打开 nuScenes 和 67.7% 向右转 2 在长视未来推断。 这种优越感可以归功于我们设计的自动递减预测范式,这种范式自然迫使网络在历史观测的基础上逐步学习下一个帧分布. 代码将在 https://github.com/liujiuming123/Messenger.

metadata_records.title: 3D modeling for crop applications in precision agriculture: a review
metadata_records.abstract: Background Advances in data acquisition and information processing have strengthened the role of precision agriculture (PA) in enhancing agricultural productivity and sustainability. Among emerging technologies, 3D crop modeling offers detailed representations of agricultural scenes, supports crop phenotyping, and enables autonomous operations such as harvesting, fertilization, and pruning. However, despite the rapid development of hardware and software for 3D modeling, a comprehensive synthesis of the available approaches and their applications in PA remains limited. Purpose This review aims to examine the broad range of 3D modeling approaches used in PA, focusing on their methodological characteristics, practical applications, advantages, and limitations to support the selection of suitable solutions for different agricultural requirements. Methods A total of 168 publications, identified through a Scopus literature search covering studies published up to March 2026, were reviewed. The analysis examines 3D data types and sensing technologies, sensor platforms and application environments, and data processing methods, including data registration techniques and methods for insight extraction. Applications of 3D models to agricultural crops were also analyzed and classified into three main categories: crop phenotyping, machinery navigation, and field operations. Conclusions The review highlights the widespread adoption of LiDAR, RGB, and RGB-D sensors deployed on Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles, Uncrewed Ground Vehicles, and robotic platforms, alongside increasing use of AI-based processing methods. Challenges related to sensor robustness, multisensor interoperability, and large 3D datasets remain. Future research should focus on overcoming these limitations to facilitate the transition towards reliable, large-scale implementation of 3D modeling technologies in practical agricultural operations.

metadata_records.title: GLIO2: A GPU-Parallelized Tightly-Coupled LiDAR-Inertial-GNSS System for Robust and Real-Time Global Localization and Mapping
metadata_records.abstract: Globally consistent, real-time state estimation in large-scale, perceptually degraded environments is essential for autonomous vehicles and aerial robots, and requires fusing LiDAR, inertial, and GNSS measurements. Existing fusion methods, however, share a scan-to-map front-end with two failure modes. First, each scan is aligned to an incrementally built map that drifts under degeneracy, and once the estimate diverges the error is irrecoverable. Second, even without divergence, a registration biased by dynamic objects or wrong correspondences is propagated as a single pose constraint with an over-confident covariance, leaving its correspondences unavailable for GNSS to re-weight or relinearize. We propose GLIO2, a tightly-coupled LiDAR-Inertial-GNSS system whose GPU-parallel front-end jointly optimizes scan-to-multiscan LiDAR, IMU pre-integration, and raw GNSS measurements in a single sliding-window factor graph, sustaining real-time operation on edge hardware. A complementary offline back-end reuses the same cached factors to refine the entire trajectory in batch, completing the 30-min, 4.51-km UrbanNav Whampoa sequence in about 24 s. Across three public benchmarks (UrbanNav, MARS-LVIG, M3DGR) and self-collected UAV and vehicle data, GLIO2 attains the best overall accuracy among evaluated systems. On a 5.66-km bridge traversed at up to 96 km/h, where every competing baseline diverges under LiDAR degeneracy, it maintains 1.6 m horizontal accuracy. On an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX, the full pipeline runs at about 25 Hz (39.60 ms per scan). The source code and datasets will be released.
first_author_affiliations: Department of Aeronautical and Aviation Engineering , The Hong Kong Polytechnic University , Hong Kong SAR , China

translation.zh: 在全球范围对大规模、感知退化的环境进行一致的实时状态估计对自主车辆和航空机器人至关重要,需要引信 LiDAR, 惯性,以及 GNSS 测量。 现有 融合 然而,方法与两个失败模式共享扫描到地图的前端。 首先,每次扫描都与一个在变质性下漂移的递增构造的地图对齐,一旦估计值出现差异,错误是无法挽回的. 第二,即使没有分歧,a 配准 被动态对象或错误的函证所偏颇,作为单一的束缚而传播,过于自信,使其函证无法使用。 GNSS 重新加权或重新线化。 我们提议 GLIO2, 一个紧密的结合 LiDAR-惯性-GNSS 系统 GPU-parallel 前端联合优化扫描到多扫描 LiDAR, IMU 预集和生 GNSS 在一个单一的滑窗系数图中进行测量,维持边缘硬件的实时操作. 互补的离线后端再利用相同的缓存因素,以整批完善整个轨迹,完成 30-分钟, 4.51-公里 UrbanNav 大约是Whampoa序列 24 s. 三个公共基准 (UrbanNav, MARS-LVIG, M3DGR) 和自我收集 UAV 车辆数据, GLIO2 在被评价的系统中实现最佳的总体准确性。 一个 5.66-公里大桥经过 96 千米/小时,每个相互竞争的基线在 LiDAR 变质,它坚持 1.6 m 水平精确度. 在一个 NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX, 整个管道运行在大约 25 赫兹 (39.60 每扫描毫秒). 将发布源代码和数据集.

metadata_records.title: Večmodalna hkratna lokalizacija in kartiranje iz zraka v realnem času z združevanjem vizualnih, inercialnih, magnetnih in barometričnih meritev
metadata_records.abstract: High-altitude nadir imagery from unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) provides wide coverage, but weak parallax, repeated appearance, large in-plane rotations, and long trajectories make visual simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) prone to scale and heading drift. We present LoMa-based Lightweight Sparse SLAM (L²S²), a real-time multimodal system combining learned sparse matching, geometric optimization, and sensor factors. We use XFeat to select keyframes and rotation-invariant LoMa-R to obtain correspondences. With CUDA bundle adjustment, we eliminate landmarks and pass the resulting pose system to a fixed-lag GTSAM graph that fuses inertial, altitude, magnetic-direction, and horizontal-position measurements. Through a separate submap graph, we apply delayed global position fixes for keyframes no longer in this graph, without deforming the local map. We evaluate the visual system against 5 reference methods on 5 datasets, then study visual-inertial estimation, sensor fusion, and delayed correction on GES, MARS-LVIG, and MUN-FRL. In visual-only evaluation, L²S² achieves the lowest pooled mean for all 3 horizontal error metrics over 28 completed runs. In the visual-inertial SLAM evaluation, L²S² completes all 19 sequences with its IMU factor enabled after using 2 position updates to initialize metric scale and yaw, whereas OpenVINS completes 6 using only camera and IMU. Reference positions supplied as simulated outputs from successful visual place recognition further show that sparse delayed fixes can correct long trajectory segments.

openalex:W7221745267.title: Večmodalna hkratna lokalizacija in kartiranje iz zraka v realnem času z združevanjem vizualnih, inercialnih, magnetnih in barometričnih meritev
openalex:W7221745267.abstract: High-altitude nadir imagery from unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) provides wide coverage, but weak parallax, repeated appearance, large in-plane rotations, and long trajectories make visual simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) prone to scale and heading drift. We present LoMa-based Lightweight Sparse SLAM (L²S²), a real-time multimodal system combining learned sparse matching, geometric optimization, and sensor factors. We use XFeat to select keyframes and rotation-invariant LoMa-R to obtain correspondences. With CUDA bundle adjustment, we eliminate landmarks and pass the resulting pose system to a fixed-lag GTSAM graph that fuses inertial, altitude, magnetic-direction, and horizontal-position measurements. Through a separate submap graph, we apply delayed global position fixes for keyframes no longer in this graph, without deforming the local map. We evaluate the visual system against 5 reference methods on 5 datasets, then study visual-inertial estimation, sensor fusion, and delayed correction on GES, MARS-LVIG, and MUN-FRL. In visual-only evaluation, L²S² achieves the lowest pooled mean for all 3 horizontal error metrics over 28 completed runs. In the visual-inertial SLAM evaluation, L²S² completes all 19 sequences with its IMU factor enabled after using 2 position updates to initialize metric scale and yaw, whereas OpenVINS completes 6 using only camera and IMU. Reference positions supplied as simulated outputs from successful visual place recognition further show that sparse delayed fixes can correct long trajectory segments.

metadata_records.title: Occlusion-aware test-time adaptation for robust traffic sign image-text matching
metadata_records.abstract: Traffic-sign image–text matching supports retrieval-based vision–language perception in driving scenes, but partial occlusion can hide the visual information needed to link a traffic sign to its description. The robustness can be enhanced by adding experimental data or retraining the model on corrupted image–text pairs. Both of these would need extra data, and the corruptions in the training data may not be the same as those at test time. We evaluate OATA, a source-free test-time adaptation pipeline that combines BatchNorm TENT with a lightweight image–text pair reranker. Given unlabeled occluded test images, TENT updates only the BatchNorm scale and shift parameters while the text encoder remains frozen. The reranker then uses image–text pair scores to reorder the Top-5 candidates. Under a dataset-level protocol with 1,512 images and 3,024 captions, full OATA achieves 96.69% image-to-text Recall@1 and 96.43% text-to-image Recall@1. These results suggest that a combination of source-free BatchNorm adaptation with lightweight pair reranking can improve the top-rank performance of traffic-sign image–text retrieval on controlled synthetic occlusion shifts. This study also provides an evaluation protocol for future robustness studies.

metadata_records.title: The Impact of Cyberworthiness on Corporate Organisations and Defence Organizations
metadata_records.abstract: The growth of interconnected digital systems and the Internet of Things (IoT) has enlarged the cyber-attack surface of modern corporate and defence organisations. In this setting, cyberworthiness denotes a system's capacity to operate securely, reliably, and continuously under adversarial conditions. This thesis treats cyberworthiness as a multidimensional construct that extends beyond conventional cybersecurity by combining security and reliability with resilience, adaptability, and mission assurance across complex cyber-physical systems that support corporate operations and defence-relevant deployments. ​The thesis makes four contributions, each responding to a distinct organisational challenge. First, it presents a structured review of cyberworthiness standards, governance frameworks, and software assurance models, identifying fragmentation and the lack of automated, end-to-end assessment mechanisms. Second, it proposes a federated deep learning intrusion detection framework for privacy-preserving cyberworthiness assessment in distributed IoT environments; a four-layer architecture yields strong detection performance, cross-dataset generalisation, and improved communication efficiency. Third, it introduces CyberFND-Net, a dual-stream convolutional network for fake news detection that combines semantic and structural features with a Cyberworthiness-Aware Loss to reflect asymmetric operational risks, and reports superior results across multiple datasets. Fourth, it presents a six-dimensional Digital Twin architecture for IoT-enhanced combat systems that embeds cybersecurity as an intrinsic design dimension and demonstrates improved detection, lower latency, and substantial reductions in mean time to mitigation. Collectively, these contributions advance a coherent cyberworthiness agenda and provide empirically supported methods for improving security, resilience, and mission assurance in corporate and defence digital ecosystems.

metadata_records.title: False data injection attacks in smart grids: a review
metadata_records.abstract: Abstract The integration of advanced information and communication technologies into modern power grids has transformed them into complex cyber-physical systems, commonly referred to as smart grids. This evolution has enhanced grid efficiency and sustainability but has also introduced cybersecurity vulnerabilities, particularly to false data injection attacks (FDIAs). FDIAs involve the malicious manipulation of sensor data and measurements, posing a threat to the integrity of grid operations. This paper provides a comprehensive review of FDIAs in smart grids, categorizes attack strategies, analyzes their impacts on grid stability and reliability, and evaluates existing detection and mitigation strategies. We also discuss the challenges associated with defending against sophisticated FDIAs and propose future research directions to enhance the resilience of smart grids against these evolving cyber threats.

metadata_records.title: Leveraging Human-In-The-Loop Demonstrations in Reinforcement Learning for Digital Twin-Driven Robot Flexibility
metadata_records.abstract: Growing automation makes collaborative robots work in more variable environments, increasing the need for adaptation. We propose a human-in-the-loop online training framework combining a digital twin (DT), reinforcement learning (RL), and human demonstrations. Unlike DTs used mainly to generate synthetic data before task execution, our DT is synchronized with the physical system in real time through camera feeds, allowing the virtual robot to update its observations and policy from real-world feedback. A dual actor framework integrates imitation learning (IL) without adding a direct imitation loss to the RL actor, so demonstrations can guide adaptation instead of manual reprogramming. The proposed framework is demonstrated on the Ufactory Xarm5 collaborative robot, where the robot's end-effector aims to reach the target position while avoiding obstacles. The experiments show that the framework can resume training after a change in the physical workspace and that, with a fixed set of non-optimal demonstrations, the dual actor framework achieves a much higher final success rate than two methods that add an imitation loss to the actor. The same pattern holds with real human demonstrations collected in virtual reality (VR): with demonstrations that never reach the goal, the dual actor framework reached 83-100% mean deterministic evaluation success, against 0-17% for the two imitation-loss methods.
