metadata_records.title: Adaptive multi-agent optimization in intelligent-connected vehicles based on deep reinforcement learning
metadata_records.abstract: In order to provide offloading services for computationally demanding and time-sensitive operations on vehicles, multi-access edge computing has emerged as a successful paradigm. However, there are typically spatiotemporal load mismatches across edge servers due to significant vehicle mobility. As a result, task migration is used to transfer excessive tasks from overloaded to underloaded servers in order to maintain dynamic workload balance. Deep reinforcement learning techniques are used in recent research to produce offloading and migration decisions based on system observations. On the other hand, task migration in the incorrect direction may result in further delays as the migration direction is said to be heavily reliant on vehicle movements. The challenges intelligent connected vehicles encounter during service migration in a highly dynamic Internet of vehicles environment, such as multi-user resource competition and dynamic changes in edge node availability, were addressed by a service migration technique based on multi-agent group relative policy optimization (MAGRPO). The formulation of the service migration problem as a long-term multi-user joint optimization problem with resource constraints led to the development of a MAGRPO approach that did not require an explicit critic network. A policy update signal based on the relative ordering of discounted returns within the group was developed to lower training expenses and effectively alleviate training instability caused by severe penalties (such as node overload or failure). Simulation findings show that the proposed method outperforms existing baseline methods in key metrics such as migration success rate, overall service delay, and migration energy usage. In situations where edge node resources are few and their availability fluctuates, it demonstrates greater resilience and scalability.

As a result, task migration is used to transfer excessive tasks from overloaded to underloaded servers in order to maintain dynamic workload balance. Deep reinforcement learning techniques are used in recent research to produce offloading and migration decisions based on system observations. On the other hand, task migration in the incorrect direction may result in further delays as the migration direction is said to be heavily reliant on vehicle movements. The challenges intelligent connected vehicles encounter during service migration in a highly dynamic Internet of vehicles environment, such as multi-user resource competition and dynamic changes in edge node availability, were addressed by a service migration technique based on multi-agent group relative policy optimization (MAGRPO). The formulation of the service migration problem as a long-term multi-user joint optimization problem with resource constraints led to the development of a MAGRPO approach that did not require an explicit critic network. A policy update signal based on the relative ordering of discounted returns within the group was developed to lower training expenses and effectively alleviate training instability caused by severe penalties (such as node overload or failure). Simulation findings show that the proposed method outperforms existing baseline methods in key metrics such as migration success rate, overall service delay, and migration energy usage. In situations where edge node resources are few and their availability fluctuates, it demonstrates greater resilience and scalability.

metadata_records.title: Parrot Mambo Minidrone as a benchmark platform for low-cost UAV research: a review of control, autonomy, software validation, safety and experimental evaluation
metadata_records.abstract: Low-cost minidrone platforms are increasingly used in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) research for safe indoor experimentation, controller development and engineering education. The Parrot Mambo Minidrone is particularly attractive because of its compact size, onboard sensing, MATLAB/Simulink compatibility and suitability for real-time validation. This review critically synthesises 137 studies published between 2018 and 2026 involving the Parrot Mambo, including studies where it appears alongside other UAV platforms. The literature spans modelling, state estimation, classical and intelligent control, robust nonlinear control, disturbance rejection, vision-based navigation, multi-UAV coordination, Human-Drone Interaction (HDI), software validation, cyber-resilience, education, safety analysis, energy-aware evaluation and hardware performance. A platform-centred taxonomy is developed to trace progression from Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID)-based stabilisation toward adaptive, intelligent, perception-driven, software-aware and safety-conscious autonomy. PID and Proportional-Integral–Proportional-Derivative (PI-PD) controllers remain important baselines, while fuzzy-PID, Sliding Mode Control (SMC), Model Predictive Control (MPC), Model-Free Control (MFC), Reinforcement Learning (RL), Observer-Based Control (OBC) and Fault-Tolerant Control (FTC) address nonlinearities, disturbances, uncertainty and hardware constraints. However, software testing, cyber-resilience, fault diagnosis, reachability analysis, actuator health, aerodynamic constraints and energy-aware evaluation remain weakly integrated. The principal gap is the absence of a standardised benchmark jointly assessing control accuracy, robustness, perception reliability, energy use, computational load, software dependability, cyber-resilience, safety, actuator constraints and real-flight repeatability. Accordingly, this review proposes a benchmark-driven framework for integrated, safety-aware, hardware-aware and reproducible Parrot Mambo research.
first_author_affiliations: School of Engineering and Built Environment, University of Greater Manchester

metadata_records.title: Dynamic periodic event-triggered adaptive PD-like composite neural control with iterative disturbance observer for 3D tracking of UUVs
metadata_records.abstract: This work focuses on the 3D tracking control issue for underactuated underwater vehicles (UUVs) subject to model uncertainties, external disturbances, and actuator mechanical degradation by mechanical wear. To reconstruct the uncertain dynamics within the system, an adaptive PD-like composite neural network (NN) is constructed. In contrast with conventional adaptive NNs, the constructed PD-like composite NN accelerates the network learning process and improves the reconstruction accuracy of uncertain dynamics. Furthermore, to counteract the adverse effects of external disturbances, an NN disturbance observer is designed with a gain iteration protocol. Unlike conventional disturbance observers that employ fixed gains, the designed observer dynamically adjusts its gains through an iterative protocol to achieve accurate disturbance estimation and enhance the robustness of the UUV system. To mitigate actuator wear and avoid unnecessary control updates, a dynamic periodic event-triggered protocol is proposed, which inherently precludes Zeno behavior. Building on these developments, a novel adaptive PD-like composite neural control law that integrates the aforementioned iterative disturbance observer and the dynamic periodic event-triggered protocol is formulated. The Lyapunov theory is employed to demonstrate that all signals within the closed-loop control system are bounded. Simulation results substantiate the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed control strategy.

metadata_records.title: Towards a Sustainable Food Supply Chain: Digital Transformation via Blockchain, IoT and AI
metadata_records.abstract: Supply chain management (SCM) plays a pivotal role in achieving competitive advantage, enhancing customer value, and ensuring efficient transformation of raw materials into finished food products. However, the increasing complexity and globalization of agri-food supply chains (AFSCs) have intensified challenges related to food safety, waste management, traceability, and sustainability. In response, digital transformation driven by Industry 4.0 technologies, particularly Blockchain, Internet of Things (IoT), and Artificial Intelligence (AI), has emerged as a critical enabler of sustainable food systems. This review critically examines the role of these technologies in enhancing transparency, efficiency, and resilience across food supply chains. Blockchain ensures secure, immutable, and transparent data sharing, thereby improving traceability and trust among stakeholders. IoT facilitates real-time monitoring of environmental and logistical parameters, reducing post-harvest losses and ensuring product quality. AI-driven analytics enable predictive decision-making, demand forecasting, and resource optimization, contributing to reduced food waste and improved operational performance. Collectively, these technologies support precision agriculture, smart logistics, and data-driven supply chain integration, thereby advancing sustainability goals. Despite these benefits, the adoption of digital technologies faces significant barriers, including high implementation costs, interoperability challenges, data privacy concerns, and limited technological infrastructure. This study highlights current advancements, identifies research gaps, and proposes future directions for scalable and secure digital integration to achieve sustainable and resilient food supply chains.

metadata_records.title: Digital Twins as Socio-Technical Decision Systems: A Comparative Systematic Review of Supply Chain Management and Healthcare
metadata_records.abstract: Digital Twin (DT) technology is rapidly evolving from a digital representation of physical assets into a decision-support infrastructure that integrates real-time data, analytics, and simulation. However, existing research remains fragmented across application domains, limiting understanding of how DTs enable decision-making under different socio-technical conditions. This study presents a systematic literature review and decision-centric comparative analysis of DT applications in two contrasting decision environments: Supply Chain Management (SCM) and healthcare. Following a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) protocol, 193 peer-reviewed studies (95 SCM and 98 healthcare) were identified, screened, and synthesized across six analytical dimensions: application domains, technological integration, decision-making levels, business value, stakeholder involvement, and implementation challenges. The findings reveal fundamentally different decision logics despite a shared technological foundation based on Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and cloud computing. SCM-DTs primarily support coordination, optimization, resilience, and organizational scalability, whereas healthcare-DTs emphasize personalization, patient safety, and ethical governance under stringent regulatory constraints. Building on these findings, the study proposes a decision-centric comparative framework and a value–complexity perspective suggesting that value realization is increasingly associated with technological, organizational, and governance complexity as DT ecosystems mature. The paper advances the conceptualization of DTs as socio-technical decision systems and provides practical guidance for researchers, managers, and policymakers seeking responsible and effective digital transformation.

metadata_records.title: Cell‐Based Micro/Nanorobots: From Living Carriers to Living Therapeutic Specialists
metadata_records.abstract: ABSTRACT Cell‐based micro/nanorobots (CMNRs) integrate intrinsic biological functions with engineered capabilities, constituting an emerging class of biohybrid robotic platforms. Unlike fully synthetic micro/nanorobots, whose functions depend entirely on artificial materials, CMNRs are constructed from living cells or cell‐derived components and can exploit unique biological capabilities. Over the past decade, CMNR research has progressed from the development of simple delivery carriers toward therapeutic specialists capable of performing diagnostic and therapeutic tasks within distinct organs. Although the complex and highly heterogeneous physiological environments of different organs impose formidable barriers, CMNRs possess intrinsic organ‐specific compatibility shaped by evolution, offering a promising strategy for improving their performance in specialized medical tasks. Here, we propose a novel framework for constructing organ‐specific therapeutic platforms. Guided by this framework, we systematically review and critically assess the biological properties, robotic functions, and recent in vivo applications of CMNRs. Despite substantial progress, a considerable gap remains between laboratory prototypes and clinical translation. This Review identifies key translational barriers that must be addressed to ensure the safety, controllability, and functional reliability of CMNRs in clinical use. Overall, a future trajectory toward organ‐specific theranostic systems is outlined to provide a conceptual basis for the clinical development of next‐generation CMNRs.

metadata_records.title: EHL-YOLO: hierarchical multi-scale feature extraction and efficient cross-level fusion for UAV object detection
metadata_records.abstract: Small-object detection in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery remains challenging because targets are small, densely distributed, and easily confused with complex backgrounds. This study presents EHL-YOLO, a task-oriented structural optimization of YOLOv10l that coordinates shallow feature preservation, hierarchical cross-scale interaction, and localization-quality-aware prediction. The backbone replaces selected C2f-based units with Efficient Adaptive Multi-Scale Feature Extraction (EAMFE), the neck reconstructs the P3–P5 fusion pathway through a Hierarchical Adaptive Feature Interaction (HAFI) design, and the detection head incorporates Location Quality Estimation and Dual-Branch Collaborative detection (LQEDC). On VisDrone-DET2019, EHL-YOLO increases Precision from 0.493 to 0.507, Recall from 0.374 to 0.402, mAP50 from 0.363 to 0.392, and mAP50–95 from 0.217 to 0.228, while reducing parameters from 24.317 M to 22.106 M and GFLOPs from 120.0 to 112.9. The expanded comparison includes RT-DETR-L and UAV-oriented detectors. Under its implementation-specific training and preprocessing configuration, RT-DETR-L obtains 0.3200 mAP50 and 0.1914 mAP50–95, whereas EHL-YOLO obtains 0.3920 and 0.2280, respectively. A Top-m sensitivity study shows that m = 4 provides the highest Recall, mAP50, and mAP50–95 among m∈{2,4,8}. Cross-dataset evaluation on the HIT-UAV infrared benchmark increases Precision from 0.8827 to 0.9221 but decreases Recall and mAP50–95, revealing a conservative prediction tendency and a remaining cross-modal limitation. These results demonstrate an improved accuracy–complexity balance for visible-light UAV detection under the reported protocol, while the HIT-UAV results reveal a remaining limitation under infrared domain shift.

metadata_records.title: Colour maps for representation of quantitative metrics in radiology: meaningful or misleading?
metadata_records.abstract: The increased utility of quantitative metrics in medical imaging has prompted the use of colour representation of the data. Colour schemes for image display can highlight pathology and distinguish normal anatomy, thus potentially aiding image interpretation. Adding colour schemes to images may serve the sole purpose of visualising an abnormality or may seek to represent and meaningfully convey a quantitative metric. An early use of colour representation is exemplified by colour Doppler in ultrasound (US), where a two-sided linear scale is commonly applied. More recently, many schemes have arisen, ranging from a single colour to depict a segmented region to a range of colours that embrace the entire colour spectrum. These may be applied as continuous or discrete palettes, depending on the software vendor or even on individual user settings. The lack of standardisation of colour schemes across the medical community, especially in medical imaging, risks misinterpretation of quantitative data and potential unintended negative clinical consequences. The purpose of this article is to review the colour schemes used for quantitative imaging across US, computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and positron emission tomography (PET), the way in which they are applied, the clinical applications where their use is desirable for enhanced interpretation, and the pitfalls where standardisation is lacking in a variety of clinical applications. Finally, we discuss some solutions that could be employed to enable standardisation and augment the use of colour in image interpretation. KEY POINTS: Question Colour schemes in medical imaging can highlight pathology, but standardisation is lacking for most imaging modalities, thus risking misinterpretation of quantitative data. Findings For T1, T2, and T2* maps and their inverses, colour map recommendations have recently been proposed, but are mostly lacking for other quantitative data. Critical relevance statement Standardised colour maps can enhance data analyses across scanners and institutions, which is important for multicentre studies and handling big data. Furthermore, standardised and harmonised colour maps could improve lesion conspicuity, cross-platform comparability, and longitudinal reliability.

metadata_records.title: Event-based vibro-mechanical sensing for hidden object classification at ultra-low data rates
metadata_records.abstract: We present an event-based vibro-mechanical sensing approach for classifying objects enclosed inside an opaque capsule under externally applied vibration. Hidden objects are probed with a sequence of controlled excitation modes, and the resulting capsule micro-motions are recorded by an event camera at high temporal resolution and low data rate. From the event stream, we extract frequency-domain features and classify the resulting samples with a linear support vector machine. On an 8-class classification task, the proposed method achieves a mean accuracy of 82.2% in five-fold cross-validation. Compared with a conventional high-speed frame-based setup at similar temporal resolution, the event-based representation reduces the data volume by approximately two orders of magnitude. These results demonstrate the potential of event-based vision for low-bandwidth vibro-mechanical inspection.

metadata_records.title: ECHO: Embodied Camera Observations of Human Object Carrying
metadata_records.abstract: Embodied and assistive agents must do more than recognize objects: they must reason about where an object belongs given the layout of an environment and the habits of the people who live in it. Progress on this problem has been limited, in part because no dedicated benchmark or dataset exists to define and evaluate it. Existing RGB-D scan datasets reconstruct static rooms without human activity, while human-object-interaction datasets capture motion without a navigable, fully reconstructed scene or a ground-truth notion of an object's natural destination. We introduce contextual object placement as a benchmark task: predicting an object's destination during an observed object-carrying episode. To support this task, we present Embodied Camera observations of Human Object carrying (ECHO), a large-scale synthetic dataset that pairs dense RGB-D scans of indoor scenes with recordings of an embodied human carrying everyday objects to context-appropriate destinations. ECHO is the first publicly available dataset to combine reconstructed scenes, human activity, natural language, and contextual-placement annotations. It comprises 3,805 human-annotated episodes across 159 floors of 115 HM3D scenes, involving 198 distinct objects. Each floor includes a complete RGB-D scan with human-annotated room labels and a surface list. Each episode provides synchronized RGB-D encounter clips; 6-DoF camera, human, and object trajectories; start and destination surfaces; an action caption; and a human-written context: a single sentence describing the inhabitant's routine that implies the destination without naming it. We evaluate contextual object placement using input-masked probes and an end-to-end baseline. Results show that no single input modality is sufficient, highlighting the need to jointly reason over scene structure, human activity, and contextual knowledge.

metadata_records.title: Proxy Interfaces for Enhancing Non-Visual Web Usability
metadata_records.abstract: People with blindness or visual impairments (BVI) face significant barriers when navigating the web, even when digital content is technically accessible. These challenges arise not from a lack of access, but from a mismatch between vision-centric user interfaces and the linear, audio-based interaction paradigms of screen readers. Sighted users rely on spatial layout, grouping, and visual cues to interpret structure quickly, while blind users must explore elements sequentially, often without sufficient context. As a result, they expend greater cognitive effort, become disoriented more easily, and struggle with tasks that are usually trivial for sighted users. Although accessibility initiatives have focused primarily on ensuring access, comparatively little attention has been given to usability. Motivated by this gap, this dissertation introduces intelligent proxy interfaces as a unifying approach to enhance non-visual web usability by transforming visually-encoded information into semantically meaningful, screen reader-friendly representations. Specifically, this thesis presents and evaluates novel proxy-based interface-augmentation techniques, each targeting a different domain of web interaction. First, I address general web navigation through the sTag proxy interface, a browser extension that enables blind users to create personalized Table-of- Contents (TOC) overlays by tagging and revisiting meaningful page segments, thereby reducing repetitive exploration and navigation fatigue. Second, I improve the usability of structured web data for blind users with the intelligent InSupport proxy interface that automatically extracts and reorganizes web items such as product listings and attributes into simplified formats that support efficient non-visual comparisons and natural-language queries. Lastly, I present the Standpoint proxy interface to enhance usability of unstructured web data such as user-generated content in discussion forums. Specifically, the Standpoint proxy interface analyzes and automatically restructures discussion threads into coherent, context-aware non-visual presentations aligned with users’ preferences. My evaluation studies demonstrate that, overall, the presented proxy interfaces significantly reduce cognitive load, improve navigation efficiency, and expand the range of web interactions both accessible and usable to blind users. Together, these contributions demonstrate how proxy-driven transformations can advance the shift from just accessible web content toward genuinely usable non-visual web experiences for BVI individuals.

metadata_records.title: A persistent accuracy ceiling in automated verbal deception detection
metadata_records.abstract: Automated methods have been proposed to overcome the limitations of human verbal deception detection, but evidence remains fragmented across disciplines. We systematically reviewed 25 years of research (289 reports, 6,136 classification models) and meta-analyzed 3,653 models nested within 97 datasets. Pooled accuracy was 74.4% (95% CI: 71.2%-77.4%) with substantial heterogeneity. Accuracy was driven by methodological quality (ground truth, data source, class balance, evaluation procedure) more than by model complexity: the adoption of embeddings and large language models has not translated into improved predictive performance. Only 12.46% of reports used data with verifiable ground-truth, and only 23.96% of models were evaluated on independent data. The pooled accuracy aligns with meta-analyses of manual approaches, suggesting a ceiling of 70-75%, unlikely to be lifted by current research conventions.

metadata_records.title: Humanity's Sixth Sense: Benchmarking Intuitive Visual Reasoning in Multimodal Models
metadata_records.abstract: Humans perceive far more in a scene than what is explicitly depicted: a single glance captures past causes and future trajectories; a quick peek determines if a vehicle can fit between two parked cars; a few seconds of video reveals who holds authority in a room; and a fleeting clip highlights subtle abstract patterns like unwritten rules or hidden labels. This capacity reflects a form of humanity's sixth sense: an intuitive reasoning mechanism that recovers implicit information beyond raw sensory perception. Crucially, this rapid, zero-shot visual intuition underpins everyday navigation and social interaction, making it a vital capability for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) deployed alongside people. Existing visual benchmarks, however, target either deliberate expert-level analysis in academic and mathematical domains or low-level perception, leaving the intuitive reasoning that people perform largely untested. To bridge this gap, we introduce Humanity's Sixth Sense (HSS), a benchmark for intuitive visual reasoning. HSS spans diverse image and video inputs, organizes items under a structured taxonomy, and pairs each with human-written prompts probing the implicit temporal, spatial, social, and abstract structure that people infer at a glance. Frontier MLLMs fall short of human performance: participants reach 93.1% accuracy, while the strongest model, GPT-6-astra, reaches only 53.6% even at maximum reasoning effort. Despite excelling in many complex tasks that require advanced perception and knowledge, current models still struggle significantly on these visual tasks that are intuitive for humans. We further explore agentic setup that apply dynamic visual manipulation to HSS, which narrows but does not close the gap. HSS establishes intuitive visual reasoning as a measurable axis and directs attention to a capability that scaling on current benchmarks has so far left behind.

metadata_records.title: Beyond aggregate metrics: diagnosing the long-tailed failure of oracle bone character detection and recognition
metadata_records.abstract: Oracle bone inscriptions, the earliest mature Chinese writing system, are a primary source for studying ancient Chinese civilization, yet their interpretation remains labor-intensive. Automatically detecting and recognizing visible characters on rubbing images is therefore an entrance task for AI-assisted interpretation. The Oracle Bone Inscription Multi-modal Dataset exposes the problem of extreme long-tailed class distribution: aggregate evaluation conceals severe performance defects on rare classes—the detector can reach an overall AP 50 of 0.63, while the few-shot class AP 50 is only 0.06. We conduct a systematic diagnosis with a frequency-aware stratified evaluation protocol. Controlled comparisons show that localization is less limiting than rare-glyph recognition, and that in-head and crop-level remedies trade aggregate accuracy against tail accuracy. We thus propose FAR-YOLO, a minimal decoupled baseline that separates localization and recognition training, optimizing the recognition branch only with frequency-aware sampling and morphology-preserving augmentation. While maintaining nearly unchanged overall AP 50 , FAR-YOLO improves the few-shot AP 50 by 10.5 percentage points. It ranks second on all four frequency-stratified metrics among representative long-tailed methods, with consistent tail gains across seven recognition backbones.

metadata_records.title: An Explainable Multi-Modal Deep Learning Framework for Investigating the Influences of Dynamic Environmental Exposure on Momentary Stress
metadata_records.abstract: Abstract Urban stressors pose critical public health concerns by adversely affecting residents’ mental health. However, past studies have mostly focused on single-modal stressors under static exposure paradigms, with limited exploration of nonlinear environment-stress relationships. This study proposes an explainable multimodal deep learning framework that integrates remote sensing imagery (RSI), street-view imagery (SVI), mobile sensor data, and points of interest (POIs) to accurately predict and explain momentary stress in urban environments. Using 4342 momentary stress records and 125,440 min-level environmental exposure records collected in Hong Kong, we validated the framework, achieving an accuracy of 78.26% and an AUC-ROC of 82.77%. A multilevel gradient-based explainability analysis reveals that (i) environmental exposure within the most recent 25 min exerts the strongest influence on momentary stress and notable spatial heterogeneity exists in stress prediction, highlighting the importance of capturing exposure dynamics; (ii) specific environmental thresholds were identified, including 55 dBA for noise, 25 μg/m3 for PM2.5, 32 °C for temperature, 40%–70% for humidity, and 25% for greenery visibility; and (iii) from an aerial perspective, open spaces consistently suppress stress, while the influence of buildings varies depending on surrounding spatial configuration. This study provides an integrative and explainable tool offering actionable insights for public health interventions.

metadata_records.title: Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning
metadata_records.abstract: Processing long visual token sequences from high-resolution images makes multi-step reasoning computationally expensive for multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). Existing one-shot pruning and aggregation methods compress visual tokens into a fixed context before decoding. However, visual evidence needs can shift as reasoning unfolds, making it difficult for a fixed compressed context to retain all the details needed across stages. To address this challenge, we propose ViMoD, a lightweight framework that maintains a compact visual context while preserving access to original fine-grained evidence as reasoning needs evolve. Deformable Aggregation of Region-wise Tokens (DART) learns content-adaptive groups and aggregation capacities, constructing compact Coarse representations linked to recoverable original Fine tokens. Temporal Routing for Adaptive Contextual Evidence (TRACE) integrates decoding history to anticipate upcoming evidence needs and select, retain, or replace active Fine-token groups. Selected Fine tokens augment the persistent Coarse context in the frozen backbone, enabling stage-specific evidence access without continuously attending to all visual tokens. On Qwen3-VL-4B, ViMoD outperforms all evaluated baselines on all eight reasoning benchmarks at a 20% target visual token budget, improving the mean normalized score by 39.0% over the strongest evaluated one-shot baseline. These gains are achieved with only 0.0546% additional trainable parameters relative to the frozen backbone.

metadata_records.title: SAGE: Sink-Aware Guided Emphasis for Visual Grounding in Vision-Language Decoders
metadata_records.abstract: Recent large vision-language models (VLMs) pair a visual encoder with a large language model (LLM) and perform well on diverse image-text tasks, yet their reliability is often limited by decoder attention pathologies that suppress visual evidence and exacerbate hallucinations. In this paper, we revisit visual attention sinks and uncover a structured, layer-dependent behavior: across prompts, early and late decoder layers exhibit prompt-invariant attention collapse onto the same few image regions, which we term PIS (Prompt-Invariant Sinks), whereas mid layers become prompt-conditioned and drive vision-language alignment. This split suggests that treating sinks as a uniform effect is incomplete. Building on this insight, we propose SAGE (Sink-Aware Guided Emphasis), a lightweight intervention that steers decoder attention away from PIS and toward query-dependent regions of interest (ROIs) using token-aligned ROI masks derived from standard vision backbones such as CLIP, ViT, and DINOv3. Evaluated on diverse vision-encoder + decoder-only LLM VLM families, SAGE improves visual grounding, reduces hallucinations, and yields consistent gains across public downstream vision-language benchmarks, including fine-grained visual discrimination settings where localized evidence is crucial, when instantiated with backbone-derived ROI masks.
first_author_affiliations: Department of Artificial Intelligence , Chung-Ang University

metadata_records.title: CARE: Constrained Attention Refinement for Fine-Grained Visual Classification via Teacher-Student Distillation
metadata_records.abstract: Fine-grained visual classification requires models to recognize subtle local traits while exposing the visual evidence behind their predictions. Class-specific attention pathways provide a natural basis for interpretable recognition, but their constrained prediction structure limits discriminative capacity and underuses intermediate representations from strong pretrained backbones. To address this problem, we propose CARE, a constrained attention refinement framework for interpretable fine-grained recognition via teacher-student distillation. CARE keeps the final prediction and explanation within a class-specific attention student, while introducing a training-only auxiliary query teacher that reads selected intermediate DINOv2 layers with learnable queries. The teacher fuses multi-level representations and transfers logit-standardized class-discriminative knowledge to the student. To further refine the explanation pathway, we design diversity and sparsity terms to regularize student attention heads, reducing redundancy and encouraging compact trait localization. Experiments on CUB, Oxford-IIIT Pet, Stanford Dogs, and Stanford Cars show that CARE achieves strong classification performance under an interpretable frozen-backbone setting, reaching 78.5% Top-1 accuracy on CUB. Faithfulness analysis with insertion and deletion metrics further indicates that the top-ranked attention regions retain class-relevant evidence for explanation.

metadata_records.title: Domain Adversarial Neural Networks withModel Agnostic Meta Learning Using SPECTImages for Brain Tumor Detection and Analysis
metadata_records.abstract: Brain tumor refers to the abnormal enhancement of a collection of tissues or cells within the brain, occurringwhen brain cells grow improperly. Brain Tumors have currently been recognized as a major cause of mortalityworldwide. As the most fatal category of cancer, brain tumors make detection and treatment critical for protecting lives.Single-Photon Emission Computed Tomography (SPECT) provides important imaging insights for detecting andevaluating brain cancer. However, variations in medical scenarios and imaging techniques make it difficult to improvemodels that are universally applicable across domains. This research suggests a novel framework for improvingSPECT-based brain tumor diagnosis by combining Domain Adversarial Neural Networks (DANN) with ModelAgnostic Meta Learning (MAML) and anisotropic diffusion filtering. The anisotropic diffusion filter reduces noisewhile maintaining tumor relevant structures, thereby preserving critical spatial properties for analysis. DANN supportsdomain adaptation by learning domain-invariant representations, allowing the model to perform consistently acrossdifferent datasets. MAML enhances the model’s capability to adapt to new, unfamiliar domains with insufficient data,hence boosting its therapeutic value. Experimental results of the proposed DANN-MAML model with anisotropicdiffusion filtering over diverse SPECT datasets outperformed existing strategies regarding both accuracy and flexibility,making it a promising tool for brain tumor identification.
metadata_records.venue: International Journal of Image Graphics and Signal Processing
first_author_affiliations: Department of CSE, UCE, JNTUK, Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh, India

doi:10.5815/ijigsp.2026.05.09.raw_abstract: Brain tumor refers to the abnormal enhancement of a collection of tissues or cells within the brain, occurringwhen brain cells grow improperly. Brain Tumors have currently been recognized as a major cause of mortalityworldwide. As the most fatal category of cancer, brain tumors make detection and treatment critical for protecting lives.Single-Photon Emission Computed Tomography (SPECT) provides important imaging insights for detecting andevaluating brain cancer. However, variations in medical scenarios and imaging techniques make it difficult to improvemodels that are universally applicable across domains. This research suggests a novel framework for improvingSPECT-based brain tumor diagnosis by combining Domain Adversarial Neural Networks (DANN) with ModelAgnostic Meta Learning (MAML) and anisotropic diffusion filtering. The anisotropic diffusion filter reduces noisewhile maintaining tumor relevant structures, thereby preserving critical spatial properties for analysis. DANN supportsdomain adaptation by learning domain-invariant representations, allowing the model to perform consistently acrossdifferent datasets. MAML enhances the model’s capability to adapt to new, unfamiliar domains with insufficient data,hence boosting its therapeutic value. Experimental results of the proposed DANN-MAML model with anisotropicdiffusion filtering over diverse SPECT datasets outperformed existing strategies regarding both accuracy and flexibility,making it a promising tool for brain tumor identification.

metadata_records.title: HYBRID FEATURE DESCRIPTORS WITH RESNET-BASED CLASSIFIERS FOR FAST TEXTILE FABRIC DEFECT DETECTION USING NOVEL HYBRID FEATURE EXTRACTION ALGORITHM
metadata_records.abstract: The detection of fabric defects through automation is important for ensuring the quality of the textile material because traditional detection methods are not only very time-consuming but also subjective and cannot be applied during the process of production. The traditional models that use techniques of image processing and deep learning have various limitations with respect to the detection of minor texture alterations, structure-based defects, and real-time defect identification in industrial settings. In order to address these issues, an innovative method of fabric defect detection based on the FTEFD model and ResNet classifier is proposed. What is particularly notable about the proposed technique is that it uses not only traditional handcrafted feature descriptors but also residual deep learning approaches. After this, the feature vector is fed into the ResNet classifier using residual blocks, fully connected layers, and softmax classification to detect various defect categories like holes, spots, broken threads, misweave, and normal cloth. In terms of experiment results, it was found that the proposed system gave a model accuracy of 97.48%, precision of 96.92%, recall of 96.35%, F1-Score of 96.63%, and specificity of 97.90%, which is better than CNN, YOLOv5-based, and ResNet systems. In terms of defect-wise analysis, the proposed system also gave average accuracy of 97.66%. The comparative detection results were precision of 0.92, mAP50 of 0.85, mAP50:95 of 0.55, F1-Score of 0.84, and FPS of 129.

metadata_records.title: Multimodal spatiotemporal knowledge graph construction for conflict-event analysis: an integrated framework with geographic entity-map association
metadata_records.abstract: Heterogeneous conflict-event information is distributed across textual reports, web images, and scanned maps, making it difficult to represent entities, events, geographic locations, temporal attributes, and multimedia evidence within a unified knowledge graph. This study proposes an integrated framework for constructing multimodal spatiotemporal knowledge graphs from event-oriented heterogeneous data. The framework combines textual entity, relation, and event extraction; visual object detection; scanned-map coordinate recognition; geographic entity grounding; cross-modal entity fusion; provenance-aware storage; and graph visualization. A cascaded YOLOv5-PaddleOCR procedure first detects and crops coordinate annotation regions from scanned maps and then reconstructs the map extent from the recognized coordinates. Textual place entities are geocoded using GeoNames and linked to relevant maps through point-polygon spatial intersection. Quantitative experiments showed F1-scores of 0.76-0.84 for the evaluated text extraction tasks. For aircraft, ship, and general web-image detection, YOLOv8 obtained mAP@0.5 values of 0.935, 0.890, and 0.922, respectively. On the 287-map scanned-map dataset, YOLOv5 achieved a region-detection F1-score of 0.977. In the 278-map paired out-of-fold OCR evaluation, complete map-coordinate recognition increased from 64.03% with direct PaddleOCR to 87.05% with the cascaded procedure, and the paired difference was statistically significant (exact McNemar test, p < 0.001). Under an event- and source-document-grouped evaluation protocol, the complete constrained cross-modal entity-fusion method achieved an F1-score of 0.884. A conflict-event case study further demonstrates the practical applicability of the framework.

metadata_records.title: Deep Acoustic Classification of Aircraft and Engine Types Using CNN–LSTM Models: Spectral–temporal Analysis, Cross-validation, and Performance Benchmarking
metadata_records.abstract: Detecting aircraft engine types has a wide range of applications in both defense and civilian sectors. In military settings, identifying the engine type of an aircraft helps distinguish between passenger platforms and potential threats, enabling appropriate situational response. Recognizing the aircraft category from its acoustic signature is also crucial for real-time situational awareness and sound-based monitoring. On the civilian side, airports and urban authorities use acoustic identification to monitor overhead aircraft, manage air traffic, and assess environmental noise impacts. In this study, we propose a deep learning–based model to classify aircraft into four categories: passenger airplane, drone, fighter jet, and helicopter. Log-frequency cepstral coefficients (LFCCs) are extracted as input features and fed into a custom hybrid architecture combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) layers. To evaluate performance, we applied 5-fold cross-validation and compared the proposed model with several baselines, including standard CNN, CNN-LSTM, CNN-GRU, CNN-RNN, and Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifiers. Experimental results show that our model outperforms all baselines in classification accuracy. The proposed model achieved an overall accuracy of 82.65% for the four-class task. After applying temporal consistency smoothing as a post-processing step, overall accuracy improved to 83.40%, with passenger airplane accuracy increasing from 70.7% to 73.44% and fighter accuracy from 81.5% to 84.62%. The binary engine-type classification task achieved 84.15% accuracy, which remained unchanged after smoothing. An ablation study confirmed the synergistic effect of combining CNN and LSTM components, as the CNN-only and LSTM-only models achieved only 61.4% and 53.9% accuracy, respectively.
first_author_affiliations: Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, Malek Ashtar University of Technology, Isfahan, Iran

metadata_records.title: Multi-Source Uncertainty Perception and Spatiotemporal Graph Fusion for Defect-Elimination Robots in Strong Electromagnetic Environments
metadata_records.abstract: To address perception distortion, difficulties in heterogeneous data fusion, and missed detection of small faults in defect-elimination robots for ultra-high-voltage transmission lines under strong electromagnetic interference, a physics-aware spatiotemporal graph fusion network PA-STGFN is proposed. The Middleton Class-A model is employed to estimate the parameters of non-Gaussian impulsive noise, combined with robust statistics for adaptive suppression. EfficientNet enhanced with coordinate attention and MS-TCN are used to extract visual and vibration–acoustic features, respectively. Modality uncertainty is quantified based on Dirichlet evidence, enabling dynamic reconstruction of graph connections and multi-source confidence-weighted fusion. The model is jointly trained using focal loss, reconstruction loss, and uncertainty regularization. Validation on transmission-line data shows that the feature-matching accuracy and anomaly-detection rate reach 95.8% and 96.5%, respectively, with a performance degradation of less than 3% at 10 dB and a single-frame inference latency of 78 ms. The proposed method can improve the perception reliability of defect-elimination robots in strong electromagnetic environments.
first_author_affiliations: Inner Mongolia Electric Power (Group) Co., Ltd

metadata_records.title: EC-RAG: Event Chain Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Long Video Understanding
metadata_records.abstract: Current large video-language models (LVLMs) still face challenges when dealing with long videos, mainly because frames are often processed independently, making it difficult to capture temporal dependencies across events. Although retrieval-augmented approaches have been introduced to provide additional context, most of them operate at the frame or snippet level, which limits their ability to model how events evolve over time and relate to each other. In this paper, we propose Event Chain Retrieval-Augmented Generation (EC-RAG), a training-free framework that organizes video content into an explicit event chain before question answering. Instead of retrieving isolated frames or text segments, EC-RAG first partitions the video into semantically coherent segments, represents each segment using multi-modal signals, and then links them into a structured chain that preserves temporal order and captures inter-event relationships. Given a query, the system identifies relevant events within this chain and gathers supporting evidence from the associated modalities. Our approach offers several practical advantages: (i) event-level abstraction that better reflects how video content is naturally structured, enabling more reliable localization compared to frame-level retrieval; (ii) structured multi-modal fusion that aggregates speech, text, and visual cues at the event level, allowing complementary information to be more effectively utilized during reasoning; and (iii) plug-and-play compatibility with existing LVLM backbones, requiring no additional training or reliance on proprietary models. Experiments on Video-MME, MLVU, and LongVideoBench show that this event-centric design consistently outperforms frame-level retrieval baselines, highlighting the importance of modeling temporal structure for long-video understanding.

metadata_records.title: Automated Root Canal Curvature Assessment From Periapical Radiographs Using Geometric and Deep Learning Features
metadata_records.abstract: AIM: To develop and validate a machine learning-based automated computational framework using periapical radiographs for the detection, segmentation and classification of root canal curvature in mandibular premolars with single canals, and to evaluate the contribution of geometric and deep learning features towards diagnostic performance. METHODOLOGY: A retrospective cross-sectional study was performed using 1644 periapical images of mandibular premolars. A four-stage multi-model framework was proposed using a single fixed 10-fold cross-validation partition applied consistently across all four stages to prevent data leakage between training and evaluation. The object detection models were YOLOv8, YOLOv11 and RF-DETR. For segmentation of the root canal, YOLOv8-seg, YOLOv11-seg and Attention U-Net were used. The multiparametric feature extraction included five geometric morphometric features automatically derived from a binary mask and 2048 deep convolutional neural network features from ResNet-50. Classification of curvature was defined using an eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) classifier with stratified 10-fold cross-validation, with Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and algorithmic class weighting applied within the training folds of each cross-validation iteration. RESULTS: The dataset included 633 straight, 885 moderately curved and 126 severely curved canals. RF-DETR achieved a recall of 97.5%, precision of 93.3% and F1-score of 95.4% for premolar detection. The YOLOv11-seg model was successful in segmenting the root canal with a Dice score of 85.8% and an IoU of 77.5%. All five geometric parameters were statistically significant for different severity groups (p-value < 0.001). For the end-to-end curvature classification, the hybrid feature fusion model produced the highest overall metrics, achieving an accuracy of 89.60%, a recall of 83.80% and an F1-score of 86.77%, compared to the models using either geometric features (88.38% accuracy) or deep learning features alone (82.42% accuracy). CONCLUSIONS: The hybrid feature-fusion model reached the highest overall classification accuracy at 89.60%. Although the geometric-only model had higher sensitivity for severe curvature with 80.6% compared to 69.1%, Lüiten's angle was the most prominent predictor of curvature severity. Due to the limitations of two-dimensional radiographs in displaying buccolingual curvatures, this framework works best as a screening aid as it helps identify canals that need adjunctive three-dimensional evaluation.
first_author_affiliations: Department of Conservative Dentistry and Endodontics Sri Venkateswara Dental College and Hospital  Chennai India

metadata_records.title: MCFR: A Mask-Guided Coarse-to-Fine Regression Framework for Robust Multi-Variant Board-to-Board Connector Assembly
metadata_records.abstract: Automated insertion of board-to-board (BTB) connectors in 3C manufacturing requires both high visual accuracy and strong deployment robustness. This problem remains challenging because multi-variant connectors exhibit significant morphological and appearance variations, making stable cross-variant generalization difficult, while the mismatch between training and deployment under fixed-view inspection settings induces background spurious correlation and degrades real-world performance. To address these issues, this paper proposes MCFR, a Mask-Guided Coarse-to-Fine Regression framework for multi-variant BTB connector assembly. By introducing an object-aware mask prior and explicit photometric refinement, the proposed method suppresses background interference and improves alignment accuracy and robustness in practical deployment. Experiments on a self-constructed multi-variant dataset, a BTB batch insertion testbed, and a real smartphone assembly task show that MCFR consistently outperforms representative baselines and achieves an average real-world insertion success rate of 99.25%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness and practical potential of MCFR for automated assembly of multi-variant BTB connectors.
first_author_affiliations: Department of Mechanical Engineering , Tsinghua University , Beijing , China

metadata_records.title: Scene Classification Using Deep Learning: A Critical Review of Representations, Benchmarks, and Evaluation
metadata_records.abstract: Scene classification assigns semantic categories to images by integrating information about objects, spatial layout, texture, and environmental context. Deep learning has shifted this task from manually designed descriptors toward transferable representations, but reported improvements remain difficult to interpret when datasets, supervision, and evaluation protocols differ. This narrative review examines deep learning for static visual scene classification across indoor, outdoor, and aerial imagery. It organizes the literature along three complementary axes: learning signal, representation architecture, and prediction task. The discussion connects convolutional feature extraction, local and global feature aggregation, semantic and graph-based reasoning, and generative representation learning with selected developments in vision transformers, self-supervised pretraining, and vision-language models. Benchmark characteristics are examined alongside the distinction between single-label, multi-label, and zero-shot evaluation. A source-checked numerical example illustrates why domain-specific pretraining can improve some benchmarks while leaving others unchanged or worse. The synthesis identifies dataset bias, incomplete split reporting, spatial leakage, semantic ambiguity, and deployment cost as persistent obstacles to reliable comparison. It also establishes a reporting framework covering class-wise performance, uncertainty, computational resources, and distribution shift. The review concludes that useful progress should be assessed through reproducible gains under matched protocols and credible transfer to new environments, rather than isolated accuracy values.

metadata_records.title: Adaptive Cortically Constrained EEG-Vision Alignment for Zero-Shot Brain-to-Image Retrieval
metadata_records.abstract: Zero-shot brain-to-image retrieval requires robust alignment between noisy EEG responses and visual representations. Existing EEG-vision alignment methods often operate in sensor space and apply fixed visual supervision to all responses, ignoring both spatial mixing in scalp EEG and response-wise variability in alignment reliability. We propose an adaptive cortically constrained EEG-vision alignment method for zero-shot brain-to-image retrieval. The method reconstructs EEG responses into predefined ROI-level source-pattern representations and encodes them with a Neuro-ROI Attention Encoder. To handle response-wise variability, we introduce an evidence-based adaptive visual supervision strategy that weights detail-controlled visual targets using model-based alignment evidence. On THINGS-EEG, the proposed method achieves strong 200-way zero-shot retrieval performance, with ROI-level attribution providing post hoc interpretability of the learned source-pattern representations. These results show that cortically constrained representation learning and adaptive supervision can jointly support EEG-vision alignment for zero-shot brain-to-image retrieval.
first_author_affiliations: School of Artificial Intelligence , Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications , Chongqing , China

metadata_records.title: Tri-FusionNet: Enhancing image description generation with transformer-based fusion network and dual attention mechanism
metadata_records.abstract: Captioning of images is a crucial step towards helping artificial intelligence to perceive images and create relatable language descriptions. Nevertheless, most current captioning models are not very effective at integrating fine-grained visual information with global contextual information, also leading to high correspondence between visual and text representations. We suggest Tri-FusionNet to resolve these difficulties, a new transformer-based image description generation model. The proposed model comprises a Vision Transformer encoder, a dual-attention mechanism, a RoBERTa-based decoder, and a CLIP-based integration model. The dual attentions of the visual encoder are performed to obtain both spatial and contextual information, which enhances the feature construct of images, whereas the decoder of RoBERTa produces coherent and correct text descriptions. The CLIP integration module matches visual and textual modalities by contrastive learning, which allows learning multimodal representations to occur. The Flickr30k, Flickr8k, and MS-COCO datasets have been evaluated experimentally to show that the proposed framework is effective. Tri-FusionNet attained the BLEU scores between 0.767 and 0.456, CIDEr scores between 1.679 and 1.483, METEOR scores between 0.478 and 0.358, and ROUGEL scores between 0.567 and 0.789, respectively, on Flickr30k and Flickr8k. The model scored 0.893 (B-1), 0.821 (B-2), 0.794 (B-3), and 0.725 (B-4) on MS-COCO. These findings indicate that Tri-FusionNet is highly effective in enhancing multimodal features fusion and provides more accurate and contextually relevant image descriptions.

metadata_records.title: Adaptive Spatial Neural Rendering System
metadata_records.abstract: Abstract Adaptive Spatial Neural Rendering System develops a research architecture for reconstructing, representing and rendering dynamic three-dimensional environments from heterogeneous visual, geometric and contextual observations. The system treats neural rendering not as an isolated image-synthesis task but as an adaptive spatial inference problem in which scene geometry, appearance, uncertainty, temporal change, sensor quality and downstream decision objectives are jointly modelled. The monograph integrates statistical explanation, causal inference, multimodal representation learning, neural fields, topological and tensor structure, out-of-distribution control, distributed data engineering and reproducible MLOps. Its methodological progression connects uncertainty-aware research design with explanatory statistical models, trustworthy prediction, scalable scene-data lifecycles and sector-specific deployment. The proposed architecture adapts representation density, sampling policy, model capacity and rendering strategy to spatial complexity and operational constraints while retaining traceable evaluation criteria. Applications are framed across cinema and virtual production, extended reality, robotics, digital twins, geospatial intelligence, scientific visualization and public-sector spatial systems. Across South Asia, Europe, Africa and the Americas, the framework emphasizes computational proportionality, interoperability, privacy, reproducibility and accountable deployment. The resulting system is positioned as both a scientific methodology and an engineering platform for high-fidelity spatial intelligence, adaptive view synthesis and policy-aware immersive computation. metadata_records.title: Leveraging multitask learning with partial supervision for super-resolution and semantic understanding tasks in earth observation
metadata_records.abstract: The super-resolution and semantic understanding tasks are known to benefit from one another, especially in the Earth observation context. However, learning multiple tasks in a joint model often requires all task annotations for each training example, which is impractical and expensive. In this article, we study the multi-task partially supervised learning paradigm for super-resolution, a generative low-level vision task, and semantic segmentation or object detection, a discriminative task. The main assumption is that each training example is annotated for only one task. To that end, we examine two multi-task architectural variants, sequential and shared, and propose a hybrid variant and a re-projection loss to leverage the shared representation and enforce super-resolution image quality when the training examples are annotated only for the semantic task. Experiments on both aerial and satellite remote sensing images yield competitive results against the state-of-the-art sequential learning variants. The source code and relevant data splits will be released at https://github.com/lhoangan/munera .

metadata_records.title: TrackShield: An Efficient Runtime Defense Against Availability Attacks on High-Performance Real-Time Multi-Object Tracking
metadata_records.abstract: High-performance camera-based perception pipelines must sustain per-frame real-time budgets on resource-constrained embedded GPU platforms. Availability attacks such as SlowTrack inflate the persistent state of multi-object trackers: data-association workload accumulates across frames, so per-frame latency increases and drives the pipeline past its deadline. Detector- and NMS-layer defenses do not directly control this persistent tracker-side resource. We present TrackShield, a lightweight runtime resource-management layer that protects the tracker at the point where attack-induced workload accumulates. TrackShield combines low-overhead anomaly monitoring with staged birth capping, pruning of young or weakly matched tracks, and per-stage association-input admission control. Its hard admission guard provides a deterministic bound on admitted association workload, independently of the heuristic monitor. On a Jetson AGX Orin, TrackShield reduces attacked tracking-stage latency from $139.90$ to $6.27$\,ms and whole-pipeline P99 latency from $190.9$ to $48.8$\,ms, at a benign MOTA cost of $1.06$ points. As an availability defense, TrackShield focuses on keeping the tracker responsive under attack instead of recovering the full tracking accuracy degraded by adversarial detections.

metadata_records.title: ACR-Net: Mitigating Semantic Dominance via Contrastive Acoustic-Semantic Decoupling
metadata_records.abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) models and Audio LLMs fail when vocal tone contradicts textual semantics. Extensive training on congruent data engenders a rigid semantic prior, causing "Semantic Dominance", a severe text bias during cross-modal conflicts. We introduce the ASPIRE benchmark of adversarial audio-text pairs across four conflict types, alongside two metrics: Semantic Overconfidence Penalty (SOP) and Latent Decoupling Degree (LDD). Unlike fusion methods that merely re-weight collapsed features, our Acoustic Conflict Resolution Network (ACR-Net) uses Cross-Modal Attention and Contrastive Decoupling Loss to disentangle contradictory representations into orthogonal latent spaces. Experiments show existing models fail under polarity conflicts due to extreme semantic overconfidence. Conversely, ACR-Net preserves acoustic fidelity, maintaining high LDD to drive SOP near zero, achieving superior Acoustic Accuracy (ACC) in both adversarial and standard scenarios.

We introduce the ASPIRE benchmark of adversarial audio-text pairs across four conflict types, alongside two metrics: Semantic Overconfidence Penalty (SOP) and Latent Decoupling Degree (LDD). Unlike fusion methods that merely re-weight collapsed features, our Acoustic Conflict Resolution Network (ACR-Net) uses Cross-Modal Attention and Contrastive Decoupling Loss to disentangle contradictory representations into orthogonal latent spaces. Experiments show existing models fail under polarity conflicts due to extreme semantic overconfidence. Conversely, ACR-Net preserves acoustic fidelity, maintaining high LDD to drive SOP near zero, achieving superior Acoustic Accuracy (ACC) in both adversarial and standard scenarios.

metadata_records.title: Benchmarking 3D Reconstruction for Under-Ice Robotic Perception in Arctic Environments
metadata_records.abstract: As the Arctic transitions toward a seasonally ice-free state, capturing the complex morphology of submerged sea ice is crucial for advancing models of ocean-ice-atmosphere heat exchange and monitoring under-ice habitats. Currently, sub-surface ice mapping is predominantly achieved through acoustic sensors such as multibeam sonar. While sonar provides robust large-scale geometry, it lacks spectral and high-resolution textural information required to record fine morphological features - a critical limitation in under-ice environments, where sparse visual features and degraded sensing conditions challenge the capture of detailed structural and optical surface properties. We present a benchmark for vision-based under-ice 3D reconstruction using real-world data from the MOSAiC expedition and synthetic data generated in an Unreal Engine-based underwater robotics simulator. The benchmark evaluates Structure-From-Motion (SfM) and monocular depth estimation, with quantitative comparison enabled through cross-modal registration to upward-looking multibeam sonar.

metadata_records.title: Anuvani-Diarization: Zero Shot Speaker Diarization and Annotation Conventions Across 22 Languages
metadata_records.abstract: India's 22 scheduled languages are spoken by over a billion people in conversations that mix languages, often within one turn, overlap freely, and take place over telephones, in meetings, and in media. Knowing who spoke when, the task of speaker diarization, is essential to speech applications for such conversation: voice agents conversing with several people at once, speaker attributed transcription of meetings and calls, contact center analytics, and media monitoring. We present a systematic study of speaker diarization across all 22 languages on IndicDiarBench and introduce Anuvani-Diarization, which adapts a self-supervised end-to-end segmentation model to Indian conversation with uncertainty aware silver supervision. Evaluated zero shot alongside nine recent diarization systems, it reaches a duration weighted diarization error rate (DER) of 16.78% on all 1,164 recordings, the lowest of all systems we ran and second only to the best published result (16.0%), and leads the three strongest rivals in 14 of 22 languages. It matches its parent on six international benchmarks. We also show that the benchmark's utterance level annotation convention is a hidden variable worth 1.9 to 4.1 DER points, depending on the system, and that a convention learned from other Indian transcriptions does not transfer.

metadata_records.title: Continual pretraining Prostate MRI ViT Encoder for task alignment
metadata_records.abstract: Building foundation models for MRI has emerged as a promising direction for advancing medical image analysis and improving accessibility of task specific models. Existing approaches primarily focus on effective pretraining strategies and evaluating their performance across diverse downstream tasks. While these methods show performance gains, limited attention has been given to understanding task alignment between pretraining and downstream objectives. Unlike language models, where the two stages are naturally aligned, such alignment is less evident in vision based applications. Motivated by this gap, we explore continual pretraining. Specifically, continually pretraining a pretrained ViT encoder using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) on a prostate segmentation task to enhance task alignment and downstream performance. We further perform layer-wise representational analysis using Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) to assess representational shifts and their correlation with task outcomes. Our experiments show improved performance in 3 of 6 downstream tasks and comparable results in the others. Our Feature analysis reveals that, for segmentation tasks, continually pretrained encoder features exhibit greater similarity to those of the finetuned encoder than the original pretrained encoder, correlating with observed performance gains.

metadata_records.title: GDBA-Net: A Gated Dual-Branch Adaptation of SAM2 for Robust Cross-Domain Nuclei Segmentation
metadata_records.abstract: Accurate nuclei segmentation underpins quantitative computational pathology, yet remains challenging due to morphological variability, weak boundaries, nuclear crowding, and pronounced domain shifts arising from differences in tissue preparation, staining, and acquisition. While deep learning and recent foundation models have improved segmentation performance under matched distributions with the original training data, their generalization across heterogeneous histopathology domains remains limited. We introduce GDBA-Net, a parameter-efficient nuclei segmentation framework built around the proposed Gated Dual-Branch Adapter (GDBA). GDBA-Net adapts a frozen SAM2 encoder by integrating pretrained semantic representations with explicit frequency-derived structural priors. The complementary representations are independently transformed through Grid MLP branches and dynamically integrated using sample-adaptive channel-wise gating, selectively emphasizing structural cues relevant to nuclear delineation. Despite using only 4.3 million trainable parameters, GDBA-Net achieves state-of-the-art in-dataset performance and consistently superior cross-dataset generalization across six diverse nuclei segmentation benchmarks under fully supervised, cross-dataset, and five-shot adaptation protocols, outperforming competing CNN-, transformer-, and foundation model based methods. Comprehensive ablations confirm that these gains arise from the coordinated design of semantic-frequency complementarity and adaptive gating rather than increased model capacity. By uniting transferable semantic representations with explicit structural priors, GDBA-Net provides a robust, annotation-efficient solution to domain variability in nuclei segmentation. https://github.com/biplabpoudel25/GDBA_Net

metadata_records.title: SAM3RL: Memory Control via Reinforcement Learning for Visual Object Tracking
metadata_records.abstract: Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3) is a foundation model for image and video segmentation that sets the state of the art in visual object tracking. Its tracker, inherited from SAM 2, stores information from past frames in a memory bank, managed by a simple First-In-First-Out rule, allowing temporal consistency in complex videos. Several recent methods improve SAM 2 with hand-crafted memory update rules, each targeting a specific failure mode, such as distractors, occlusions, or object motion. However, their gains transfer only partially to the stronger SAM 3 backbone. We instead present a more general, data-driven approach that frames memory control as a sequential decision-making task. SAM3RL is an extension of the SAM 3 tracker with a lightweight memory controller, trained by reinforcement learning, that decides which frames enter the memory bank in order to maximize tracking performance. SAM3RL sets a new state of the art on 10 of 12 tracking and video object segmentation benchmarks, outperforming all hand-crafted rules without any runtime overhead. The same approach applied to SAM 2 gives SAM2RL, which outperforms hand-crafted rules on 9 of the 12 benchmarks, showing the generality of our method across model generations.

Several recent methods improve SAM 2 with hand-crafted memory update rules, each targeting a specific failure mode, such as distractors, occlusions, or object motion. However, their gains transfer only partially to the stronger SAM 3 backbone. We instead present a more general, data-driven approach that frames memory control as a sequential decision-making task. SAM3RL is an extension of the SAM 3 tracker with a lightweight memory controller, trained by reinforcement learning, that decides which frames enter the memory bank in order to maximize tracking performance. SAM3RL sets a new state of the art on 10 of 12 tracking and video object segmentation benchmarks, outperforming all hand-crafted rules without any runtime overhead. The same approach applied to SAM 2 gives SAM2RL, which outperforms hand-crafted rules on 9 of the 12 benchmarks, showing the generality of our method across model generations.

metadata_records.title: Eye, Robot: Learning Expressive Gaze Dynamics via a VLM-Guided Transformer-VAE
metadata_records.abstract: Gaze coordinates attention in human interaction through coupled eye, head, and eyelid motion. A humanoid robot must choose where to look while generating a suitable movement toward that target; fixed tracking rules alone do not model the temporal structure of human gaze. We separate these tasks with an asynchronous vision-language model that selects a scene referent, a reactive perception module that maintains fixation, and a Realistic Gaze Transformer (RGT) that generates target-conditioned motion. RGT is a Transformer-VAE trained on markerless human recordings retargeted to the robot's 11-DoF joint space: self-supervised pretraining encodes recent full-head history, and autoregressive fine-tuning exposes the model to its own predictions during rollout. At inference, a four-dimensional binocular-eye trajectory conditions coordinated neck and eye motion; an auxiliary blink predictor triggers eyelid templates during playback. On a two-second benchmark in which all controllers receive the same ground-truth target, RGT-Base obtains the lowest reported overall seven-joint MSE, and physical demonstrations show the integrated targeting and control pipeline. The evidence establishes robot-space kinematic fidelity and real-time RGT inference; perceived naturalness and open-vocabulary target-selection accuracy remain questions for controlled evaluation.

metadata_records.title: FACT: A Multimodal Force-Action-Track Foundation Model for Human-to-Robot Dexterity
metadata_records.abstract: Human demonstrations offer a scalable alternative to costly robot data collection for dexterous manipulation, but most human datasets lack force measurements. Dexterous manipulation requires not only visual and proprioceptive understanding but also the ability to anticipate and regulate interaction forces. To scale force-aware human-robot co-training, we introduce EgoForce, a large-scale human tactile dataset capturing force-rich manipulation experience, and combine it with robot demonstrations for pretraining. We present FACT, a robot foundation model that cascades from prospective visual planning to force-aware refinement for dexterous manipulation. FACT comprises two jointly trained components. A Track-Guided Coarse Planner jointly predicts actions, future video, and visual tracks. Future video and visual tracks also provide a shared task representation that facilitates cross-embodiment knowledge transfer and coarse action generation. Building on this coarse plan, a Force-Action Joint Refiner jointly predicts future force and refines the coarse action, allowing anticipated force and action to shape each other during refinement. We evaluate the model on ten tasks requiring fine-grained coordination and force feedback, including tool use, musical instruments, and precision laboratory procedures. Using as few as 10 robot trajectories with 90 human trajectories for fine-tuning, FACT outperforms both baselines, with success-rate gains of up to 60 percentage points over T-Rex. Ablations show that force supervision in human pretraining data is crucial for downstream robot performance after fine-tuning, while visual track prediction and training with future-force prediction improve dexterous execution. Experiments varying the human-robot data ratio during fine-tuning further suggest that FACT learns from human demonstrations nearly as effectively as from robot demonstrations.

metadata_records.title: Physics-based deep learning for non-stationary adaptive multiple suppression
metadata_records.abstract: Surface-related multiple elimination (SRME) is an indispensable processing step in marine seismic exploration, comprising two main components: multiple prediction and adaptive subtraction. While the multiple prediction is theoretically data-driven and relies on the data itself, the adaptive subtraction step requires a fairly subjective manual control. Our approach introduces a purely data-driven and physics-based deep learning (PDL) algorithm for improving the adaptive multiple subtraction to significantly enhanced performance. There are two main innovations in the proposed deep-learning (DL) multiple subtraction approaches: first, being data-driven and self-supervised, which removes the dependence on inflexible label preparation and model training processes; secondly, being governed by the adaptive matching filtering (AMF) equation to guide the training process. The DL module serves as a strong regression filter analogous to the traditionally known AMF. We segment a moderately sized seismic profile and an initial multiple model into a large number of patches using a patching scheme for self-contained training. The number of patches is controlled by the patch size and the shift size to enable a sufficient number of training samples required by mainstream DL platforms. The patching-based self-training and regression approach, PDL, is inherently a non-stationary matching approach that aims to obtain a globally optimal matching from the initial multiple models to the input full wavefield data through iterative patching-based training. It is also closely connected with the non-stationary regression approach, which was developed almost two decades ago. However, the PDL approach achieves even stronger regression performance due to the backpropagation-based optimization mechanism in DL, and has shown significantly improved multiple subtraction performance over a number of examples.

metadata_records.title: On the Limits of Representation-Based Test-Time Adaptation for Multimodal LLMs
metadata_records.abstract: Vision-language models suffer significant accuracy drops under common corruptions. While test-time adaptation (TTA) successfully mitigates these shifts in CLIP-like contrastive models, its application to generative multimodal large language models (MLLMs) remains underexplored and uniquely challenging due to their sequential token generation. In this work, we demonstrate that representation-based TTA fails to recover performance in MLLMs. Our experiments reveal that even when violating standard TTA assumptions by leveraging target data offline, sample-blind feature alignment recovers only marginal accuracy. We attribute this failure to the nature of corruption shifts: unlike CLIP-like architectures, which benefit from a shared domain-shift direction within a single pooled classification embedding, MLLM visual token sequence shifts are nearly orthogonal and span the full embedding space.These findings bound what any sample-blind, position-shared correction at a single encoder site can achieve, establishing that representation-space interventions alone might be insufficient to ensure corruption robustness in MLLMs.
