metadata_records.title: Multi-Modal Graph Neural Network-Inspired Vessel Identification and Tracking for UAV-Based Maritime Surveillance
metadata_records.abstract: The unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based maritime surveillance is becoming an important part of maritime Internet of Things (IoT) and intelligent transportation systems. It provides a flexible and cost-effective way to large-scale maritime traffic monitoring. However, achieving robust situational awareness remains challenging in practical maritime environments. The main challenges arise from heterogeneous sensing modalities, adverse imaging conditions, and spatial misalignment caused by UAV motion. To address these problems, this paper proposes an airborne multi-modal graph learning-driven framework, termed AMGT, for vessel identification and tracking in UAV-assisted maritime IoT. Specifically, visible and infrared images are first aligned and fused through a multi-parameter perspective transformation model. This improves visual perception under low visibility and complex illumination conditions. Automatic identification system (AIS) messages are then temporally synchronized using interpolation and linear prediction. To detect small and oriented vessels, we develop a mixed-modality MAir-YOLOv8-OBB detector, followed by the MAir-SORT algorithm for stable vessel tracking. We further design a graph learning-driven association network to model temporal dynamics and spatial dependencies among vessels and between vessels and UAVs. A motion-aware coordinate unification (MCU) strategy is also introduced to reduce nonlinear misalignment caused by UAV motion. Experiments on the MAP-M2UAV50 dataset show that AMGT achieves high accuracy and efficiency. The results demonstrate its potential for UAV-assisted maritime IoT applications, including vessel monitoring, traffic situational awareness, and intelligent maritime transportation services. The dataset and code will be available at https://github.com/MAPGroup/AMGT.

metadata_records.title: Assessing the Effects of Artificial Intelligence on Nigeria's Security Intelligence Gathering and Coordination
metadata_records.abstract: This study discusses the impact of Artificial Intelligence on intelligence gathering and coordination in Nigeria’s national security system. With security threats like terror, banditry, cybercrime, and other criminal organisations becoming commonplace, our intelligence agencies must learn to handle the outrageous amount of information needed to be processed in record time; hence, the relevance of AI. In this qualitative literature reviews, we rely on peer-reviewed journal articles, books, government reports, newspapers and other academic material to look into the growing use of AI in intelligence and the relevant primary intelligence institutions in Nigeria: the NIA, DIA, DSS, FIB and other intelligence disciplines. Background Information Artificial Intelligence (AI) is now a major theme of analysis, policy and strategic thinking in security. Due to the hostile security environment (e.g., terrorism, cybercrime, marine crime, insurgency, banditry) and the increased complexity, frequency and technology-related nature of incidents in Nigeria (where there are now many complex threats to security), AI is the centerpiece of military and security operations, providing crucial strategic value in defence and risk mitigation . Research Objective To examine how AI is used in Nigerian intelligence collection and the management of national security and how the application of AI could serve to transform security operations from a reactive approach to a proactive one. Methodology The qualitative research method was used in this study. Secondary data sources for the research included online security reports, policy documents and academic literature. The theoretical framework used to guide the examination of the decision-making processes relating to the application of AI to security management was System Theory, with data being subjected to content and thematic analysis . Research Results The research results indicate the following ways in which AI improves intelligence collection and therefore enhances national security through the use of real-time data processing, automated surveillance and reconnaissance activities, and predictive modelling based upon emerging threats. Furthermore, the research demonstrates that AI improves a security response’s ability to anticipate, prevent and mitigate security issues, thereby improving the performance of security operations and supporting higher-level data analytics. Conclusion This study concludes that AI has the power to significantly improve Nigeria’s national security administration and intelligence collection. In addition, the shift from a reactive approach to a proactive approach will enhance the effectiveness of security responses while reducing vulnerability to sophisticated threats. Unique Contribution: This study contributes to the body of knowledge on AI and African security contexts by identifying AI’s significant potential for transforming intelligence collection and addressing long-standing weaknesses in Nigeria’s security framework. Key Recommendation The Nigerian government should invest in technology-based infrastructure, create a national AI ministry, with an AI minister, build capacity and promote inter-and intra-governmental collaboration in acquiring AI capabilities for a national security framework. The government’s policy should focus on ensuring that the long-term results of using technology are sustained through addressing the root causes of insecurity (e.g., poverty, poor governance) through the ethical implementation of AI.

metadata_records.title: FPGA-Based Neural Network Accelerators for Space Missions: A Survey
metadata_records.abstract: Space missions are growing ever more ambitious, placing greater demands on onboard computing. Field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) have garnered interest due to their reconfigurability and cost-effectiveness. At the same time, neural network (NN)-based methods are proving invaluable for critical spacecraft tasks such as autonomous operations, remote sensing, selective downlink, and data compression. This survey reviews and classifies the state of the art in FPGA-based NN accelerators for space missions. We examine current trends, highlight key challenges, and suggest directions for future research. This work highlights key aspects for integrating high-performance NN acceleration into next-generation spacecraft computing systems.

metadata_records.title: Adversarial Robustness of Camera-Radar Sensor Fusion for Autonomous Driving
metadata_records.abstract: Autonomous driving (AD) relies on multi-sensor perception to interpret the surrounding environment. However, the robustness of camera--radar fusion under adversarial conditions remains largely unexplored. This paper presents a systematic measurement study of the robustness of camera--radar sensor fusion in AD. We construct a unified evaluation pipeline on the nuScenes dataset that simulates attacks on both sensing modalities, including eight camera-image perturbations and three radar point-cloud perturbations. We evaluate five camera--radar fusion algorithms across two perception tasks, 3D object detection and depth estimation, and quantify their performance under clean and attacked inputs using standard metrics. Our evaluation reveals a clear asymmetry in the robustness of fusion systems. Camera perturbations substantially degrade both object detection and depth estimation, and moderate attack strengths are already sufficient to cause severe performance degradation. In contrast, the evaluated radar perturbations produce smaller and task-dependent effects, with object-detection models showing particularly limited degradation. Our analysis attributes this difference to the strong dependence of existing fusion architectures on dense camera features, together with the filtering, association, and confidence-weighting mechanisms commonly applied to sparse radar measurements. These results demonstrate that sensor fusion does not inherently guarantee robustness and that the contribution and reliability of each sensing modality must be explicitly considered under adversarial conditions. Based on four empirical findings, we derive measurement-guided design implications for future robust camera--radar fusion, including modality-specific reliability estimation, cross-modal consistency checking, adaptive fusion, and graceful failover under severe sensor degradation.

These results demonstrate that sensor fusion does not inherently guarantee robustness and that the contribution and reliability of each sensing modality must be explicitly considered under adversarial conditions. Based on four empirical findings, we derive measurement-guided design implications for future robust camera--radar fusion, including modality-specific reliability estimation, cross-modal consistency checking, adaptive fusion, and graceful failover under severe sensor degradation.

metadata_records.title: Deep Multimodal Sensor Fusion for Autonomous Driving: A Real-World Deployment on Little Blue
metadata_records.abstract: Accurate perception and control systems are essential for autonomous vehicles to safely interpret and navigate complex environments. Individual sensing modalities such as cameras, LiDAR, and inertial measurement units (IMUs) provide valuable environmental and vehicle state information; however, each sensor exhibits inherent limitations when used independently. Camera performance can degrade under varying lighting conditions, LiDAR measurements may be sparse or affected by environmental noise, and IMU measurements are susceptible to drift over time. Little Blue, a research autonomous vehicle platform from ODU (Old Dominion University), previously relied primarily on camera-based data for neural network training, limiting the system’s ability to exploit complementary information available from other sensors. This thesis introduces FusionNet, a multimodal heterogeneous deep learning sensor fusion framework that integrates camera imagery, LiDAR scans, and IMU measurements to predict vehicle control commands for autonomous navigation. A multimodal dataset was constructed from ROS2 bag recordings collected during testing and competition events involving ODU’s Little Blue platform. A preprocessing pipeline was developed to extract sensor data, synchronize measurements, normalize inputs, and organize the information into a structured dataset suitable for deep learning applications. Camera data were processed using convolutional neural networks based on a ResNet-18 architecture, while LiDAR and IMU measurements were encoded through dedicated neural network branches. Learned feature representations from each modality were combined through a fusion network to generate steering and throttle predictions. Training and evaluation were conducted using approximately 14,000 synchronized multimodal samples in an open-loop setting. The model demonstrated stable convergence during training and produced consistent steering and throttle predictions during rosbag playback, indicating that the fused sensor representation can be processed reliably within a real-time ROS2 inference environment. These results demonstrate the feasibility of heterogeneous sensor fusion for autonomous vehicle control, though full closed-loop validation and quantitative comparison against single-sensor baselines remain areas for future work. The proposed framework provides a scalable foundation for real-time autonomous vehicle operation and highlights the potential benefits of multimodal deep learning for robust perception and control. Future work will focus on deployment to embedded computing platforms, expanded datasets, closed-loop vehicle testing, and advanced autonomous navigation capabilities.

metadata_records.title: A THREE-CHANNEL NEURAL NETWORK DETECTION FRAMEWORK INTEGRATING SCENE, OBJECT, AND BEHAVIOR ANALYSIS
metadata_records.abstract: Three neural channels running side by side are the core of the detection framework presented here, and they let scene context, object recognition and behavior analysis be read together instead of one after another. Conventional pipelines either keep the three apart or chain them in a fixed order, and in both cases the dependencies among environmental context, object semantics and agent behavior drop out. Our pathways are the Scene Context Channel (SCC), which performs hierarchical spatial feature extraction; the Object Recognition Channel (ORC), built around a multiscale attention mechanism; and the Behavior Analysis Channel (BAC), which handles temporal dynamic modeling. A cross-attention fusion module joins them, learning adaptive weights that govern how much each channel draws on the others. Static images and video sequences are both accepted, and the three analysis dimensions are inferred jointly in real time. For validation we ran the method over several benchmark datasets covering surveillance, autonomous driving and human-computer interaction. Set against single-channel baselines and current multi-task architectures, it improves markedly on joint “scene-object-behavior” recognition and reaches state-of-the-art accuracy. Generalization holds across a range of environmental conditions, and the margin widens precisely where one would predict, namely in ambiguous scenes that no single modality can resolve. The ablations support the three-channel design as well, since each channel supplies information the others lack, and together they raise overall detection accuracy by 12-18% relative to isolated processing.

metadata_records.title: Spatially Adaptive Infrared–visible Fusion with EfficientDet for Night-time Multi-class Intrusion Detection
metadata_records.abstract: Night-time perimeter monitoring in low illumination remains challenging because cluttered terrain, partial occlusion, and thermal crossover conditions simultaneously distort object boundaries and visual cues. Visible spectrum sensing loses discriminative texture at night, while infrared sensing preserves thermal salience but lacks structural context. Conventional pipelines that rely on single-modality detection or simple blending commonly produce unstable recall or avoidable false alarms when the background changes. The present paper presents an EfficientDet Fusion Intrusion Detector (EFID) which combines registered infrared and visible frames using an attention-guided weighting module and a spatially adaptive activity-weighted pixel fusion step. The feature-level attention weights estimate the reliability of each modality and guide the activity-weighted pixel fusion stage. The fused RGB image is resized from 1024 × 768 to 896 × 896 before being processed by EfficientDet-D3. The resultant fusion retains visible structural edges, while infrared target evidence is simultaneously enhanced. The resulting three-channel representation is processed by an EfficientDet D3 detector augmented with a bidirectional feature pyramid network (BiFPN) for multi-scale localisation under night conditions and clutter. Experiments use the public Multi-scenario Multi-modality Fusion and Detection (M³FD) benchmark containing 4,200 aligned infrared and visible pairs at 1024×768 resolution, annotated with 33,603 bounding boxes across six classes. The proposed EFID achieves 91.7% mAP@0.5 and 67.3% mAP@0.5:0.95, with 93.4% precision and 89.8% recall at 34.2 FPS on an NVIDIA RTX 3080. Systematic ablation confirms the independent contribution of the attention module, the activity-weighted pixel fusion term, and each BiFPN iteration. Cross-dataset experiments demonstrate that zero-shot transfer retains 84.1% mAP@0.5, rising to 86.0% with 10% target fine-tuning. The results indicate practical night robustness and real-time feasibility, while extreme occlusion and calibration drift remain limiting factors that motivate alignment-aware training and lightweight deployment optimisation as future work.

metadata_records.title: GPU-resident Execution for Timing-predictable Sensor Processing Systems
metadata_records.abstract: Real-time embedded systems increasingly place GPU-accelerated processing of high-bandwidth sensor streams inside closed-loop systems, but the CPU (the host) remains the primary orchestrator of each iteration. The host observes sensor inputs, submits CUDA work, waits for completion, and commits actuation. This host-mediated path exposes the closed-loop end-to-end latency to I/O interrupts, host scheduler decisions, and CUDA API overheads even after common host-side mitigations such as GPU-memory RDMA or CPU core isolation. This paper presents GPU-resident Execution, a new execution model for real-time sensor processing pipelines that keeps I/O and GPU execution in a long-lived device-resident loop. Sensor inputs arrive in GPU memory, trigger GPU-side processing, and reach GPU-visible output endpoints without any host wakeups. We implement the model in the NVIDIA Holoscan C++ framework and provide reference components for building GPU-resident applications. We evaluate our system on NVIDIA GPUs and SoCs with inference, host-contention, multi-loop, and streaming camera workloads. On an industry-grade 1080p, 60 Hz real-time camera-to-display application, GPU-resident Execution reduces photon-to-display jitter from 4.83 ms to 0.66 ms (7.3x) relative to a CPU-driven GPU-memory RDMA baseline and reduces software-processing jitter from 1.70 ms to 0.01 ms (170x).

metadata_records.title: Indoor mobile target perception model construction based on fusion-EK algorithm in smart cities
metadata_records.abstract: In order to break through the current precision and sensitivity constraints of indoor mobile target perception methods, this paper introduces a model based on a multi-source data fusion algorithm through the extended Kalman filter to sense dynamic targets indoors. The model first combines multi-source information and performs nonlinear processing, then performs singular value decomposition for perception process enhancement, and lastly uses a gated recurrent neural network to implement mobile target tracking and localization. Experimental findings suggest that the model iterates over the York campus benchmark video dataset in 2.45 s and mean absolute error of perception accuracy is 2.39%. The optimized model achieves the perception accuracy of 0.952 and the average distance error of 0.281 m. The GSFE model overall has better feature recognition in perceiving dynamic targets and high precision and sensitivity, overcoming the current societal inadequacies of dynamic target perception.

metadata_records.title: FDCA-GRU: A dual-branch fusion network with frequency dynamic convolution attention for bearing fault diagnosis
metadata_records.abstract: Rolling bearing fault diagnosis is confronted with significant technical challenges, including the difficult extraction of weak fault features and the insufficient fusion of one-dimensional (1D) temporal dynamics with two-dimensional time-frequency patterns. To address this issue, this article proposes a novel dual-branch fusion network that synergistically integrates a ResNet optimized with frequency dynamic convolutional attention with a gated recurrent unit for accurate bearing fault diagnosis, termed FDCA-GRU. Firstly, a parallel dual-branch architecture is constructed. The image branch encodes the 1D signal into a Markov transition field image, which is then fed into an optimized FDCA-ResNet backbone. Innovatively, frequency dynamic convolution (FDConv) is introduced in this branch to replace standard convolution, enabling it to adaptively learn filter characteristics in the frequency domain. This significantly enhances the perception of specific frequency fault patterns. Meanwhile, the convolutional block attention module (CBAM) is integrated into the residual blocks. Through its channel and spatial attention mechanisms, features are adaptively weighted to enhance the model’s response to discriminative feature regions. On the other hand, the temporal branch utilizes a GRU network to directly model the 1D stacked sequences, thereby efficiently capturing long-term dynamic temporal dependencies and evolutionary laws. The two branches are complementary in that the image branch emphasizes state-transition textures and frequency-related spatial patterns, whereas the temporal branch preserves amplitude evolution, transient impact order, and long-range sequential dependencies. Finally, the deep features extracted by the two branches are fused via cross-modal concatenation to achieve synergistic optimization of time-frequency spatial patterns and dynamic temporal information. Test results on the Beijing Jiaotong University Rail Autonomous Operation bogie datasets (BJTU-RAO) and HUST public datasets show that the proposed method achieves average diagnostic accuracies of 99.52 and 98.61%, respectively. Furthermore, ablation experiments systematically validate the synergistic effects and respective contributions of the dual-branch fusion architecture, FDConv, and CBAM, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

metadata_records.title: MeshBind: Point-to-Mesh Binding for Non-Rigid Scene Flow Automatic Annotation
metadata_records.abstract: Scene flow estimation is essential for many autonomous driving (AD) and robotic applications, but obtaining ground-truth scene flow for non-rigid objects such as pedestrians is highly difficult. We present MeshBind, an automatic annotation method that uses mesh models to generate per-point scene flow for non-rigid objects. The novelty of this work is threefold: 1) developing a multi-view module that reconstructs an articulated mesh model from six surround cameras and registers it to the LiDAR frame; 2) developing a local-frame binding technique that attaches each point to the mesh via a per-triangle tangent-normal frame, invariant under rigid motion yet adaptive to articulated deformation; 3) developing a three-layer flow registration pipeline that combines ego-vehicle motion compensation, box binding, and mesh binding to produce full-scene per-point flow. We implement MeshBind in SF-Studio, an interactive annotation tool that visualises flow and allows human mesh corrections with automatic recomputation. We also release SFB (SUScape-Flow Benchmark), a large-scale benchmark built on the public SUScape dataset, covering 41k frames with per-point non-rigid pedestrian annotations and a Rigid/Semi-Rigid/Non-Rigid evaluation protocol. Experiments show that fine-tuning on SFB reduces three-way endpoint error (EPE) by 2-3x, and brings non-rigid EPE to the same level as rigid EPE.

metadata_records.title: Cognitively robust model using a deep learning framework for target recognition under suboptimal illumination in intelligent video surveillance system
metadata_records.abstract: This paper presents a cognitively robust deep learning framework for target recognition under suboptimal illumination, which is developed to enhance the recognition performance and stability of intelligent video surveillance systems. The proposed framework integrates three complementary modules: an Illumination-Adaptive Enhancement Module (IAEM) that performs LIME-based illumination estimation and correction followed by linear contrast adjustment; a Deep Recognition Backbone (DRB) based on transfer-learned CNNs for robust feature extraction; and a Cognitive Robustness Evaluator (CRE) that quantitatively assesses recognition stability across optimization and illumination conditions. Importantly, CRE operates exclusively as a post-training evaluation module and does not participate in model training, parameter optimization, loss computation, or inference. The framework was evaluated on the Extended Yale Face Database B and NIR Dataset for closed-set face recognition and on the BDD100K Night Subset for multi-class object detection. The proposed IAEM–DRB pipeline achieved classification accuracies of 99.81% and 99.62% on the two face-recognition datasets, respectively, while BDD100K performance was evaluated using detection-specific metrics. Under illumination levels ranging from 20 to 400 lx, recognition accuracy varied from 98.16% to 99.87%, with a Cognitive Robustness Index (R c ) of 0.981. Component-wise ablation experiments further examined the effects of input enhancement, backbone selection, and alternative enhancement methods. The results demonstrate high recognition accuracy and limited performance variation under the evaluated illumination conditions. The results demonstrate high recognition accuracy and limited performance variation under the evaluated illumination conditions, therefore, the framework showing its potential for illumination-robust video surveillance systems.

metadata_records.title: Evaluating architectural innovations in deep learning-based image semantic segmentation
metadata_records.abstract: Abstract Image semantic segmentation, a pivotal task in computer vision, involves partitioning images into meaningful regions for precise pixel-level classification. Although numerous review articles have summarized advances in deep learning-based segmentation, limited attention has been given to systematically examining how architectural innovations interact with the characteristics of benchmark datasets. To address this gap, this review systematically investigates deep learning-based semantic segmentation studies evaluated on four widely adopted benchmarks: Cityscapes, CamVid, PASCAL VOC 2012, and ADE20K. A structured literature search and screening process identified 374 eligible studies, from which representative high-performing models were selected for detailed analysis based on benchmark relevance, architectural novelty, methodological significance, and reported performance. For each study, architectural components, context modeling strategies, attention mechanisms, feature fusion approaches, segmentation performance, limitations, and future research directions were extracted and compared. The synthesis reveals that recent advances are increasingly driven by the integration of multi-scale context aggregation, attention-based feature refinement, transformer-based contextual modeling, hierarchical feature fusion, self-supervised pretraining, and vision-language alignment. Furthermore, the findings demonstrate that the effectiveness of architectural strategies is strongly influenced by dataset characteristics, including scene complexity, object scale variation, class granularity, temporal structure, and domain diversity. By establishing explicit links between dataset properties and architectural design choices, this review provides a dataset-centric taxonomy and a comprehensive synthesis of emerging design principles for developing robust and generalizable semantic segmentation models.

doi:10.1007/s00371-026-04759-6.title: Evaluating architectural innovations in deep learning-based image semantic segmentation
doi:10.1007/s00371-026-04759-6.abstract: Abstract Image semantic segmentation, a pivotal task in computer vision, involves partitioning images into meaningful regions for precise pixel-level classification. Although numerous review articles have summarized advances in deep learning-based segmentation, limited attention has been given to systematically examining how architectural innovations interact with the characteristics of benchmark datasets. To address this gap, this review systematically investigates deep learning-based semantic segmentation studies evaluated on four widely adopted benchmarks: Cityscapes, CamVid, PASCAL VOC 2012, and ADE20K. A structured literature search and screening process identified 374 eligible studies, from which representative high-performing models were selected for detailed analysis based on benchmark relevance, architectural novelty, methodological significance, and reported performance. For each study, architectural components, context modeling strategies, attention mechanisms, feature fusion approaches, segmentation performance, limitations, and future research directions were extracted and compared. The synthesis reveals that recent advances are increasingly driven by the integration of multi-scale context aggregation, attention-based feature refinement, transformer-based contextual modeling, hierarchical feature fusion, self-supervised pretraining, and vision-language alignment. Furthermore, the findings demonstrate that the effectiveness of architectural strategies is strongly influenced by dataset characteristics, including scene complexity, object scale variation, class granularity, temporal structure, and domain diversity. By establishing explicit links between dataset properties and architectural design choices, this review provides a dataset-centric taxonomy and a comprehensive synthesis of emerging design principles for developing robust and generalizable semantic segmentation models.

metadata_records.title: A web development method for transmission line O&M components based on multi-source data sensing and deep reinforcement learning algorithms
metadata_records.abstract: Transmission corridors in high-altitude and micro-topographic regions are chronically subjected to strong electromagnetic pulse interference, multi-physics field coupling, and extreme climatic stressors. This results in temporal asynchrony and spatial mismatch in multi-source monitoring data, while environmental disturbances cause confidence drift in single data sources. Furthermore, traditional O&M systems lack topological awareness and dynamic decision-making capabilities, leading to disruptions in the O&M process chain. To address this, we propose a Web development method for power transmission line O&M components based on multi-source data perception and deep reinforcement learning. The proposed method features a B/S architecture tailored for power transmission O&M, where the front end utilizes Vue 3 and Mapbox GL to construct a real-time interactive interface, and the back end integrates data fusion and decision-making modules via a microservices engine. We establish a tri-modal asynchronous spatiotemporal alignment mechanism that integrates UAV vision, micro-meteorological data, and online monitoring. By employing cubic spline interpolation and graph convolutional networks, we extract topological relationships and deep health states among components. We propose an adaptive weighted fusion strategy based on the exponential decay of historical variance to dynamically suppress confidence drift. The O&M decision-making process is formulated as a Markov Decision Process within a large-scale discrete action space, and we introduce a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm with Gumbel-Softmax relaxation to handle action discretization. Using O&M costs and failure risks as a multi-objective reward function, we train the system to generate Pareto-optimal policies. Through WebSocket full-duplex communication and ECharts-based dynamic visualization, the system achieves millisecond-level push of DDPG decision commands and enables human-machine collaborative execution. Experimental results demonstrate that in typical scenarios including conductor temperature rise, sudden wind speed increases, and abnormal leakage currents, the temporal causal consistency of multi-source perception exceeds 92%, and the cosine similarity of the health state vector remains between 55% and 85% under comprehensive noise interference; the cost-risk Pareto front exhibits a convex distribution toward the origin, confirming the near-optimality of the decision within the scope of our experimental settings of our experimental settings; the full-link closed-loop integrity rate reaches 100% (mean value across 10 repeated trials, n = 10, with zero variance, and the 95% confidence interval of [99.2%, 100%] was calculated using the Wilson score interval based on 10 independent repeated experiments), with no data reordering or command loss.

metadata_records.title: Learning-enabled collaborative intelligence in search and rescue robotics: a survey of paradigms, models, and challenges
metadata_records.abstract: Search and Rescue (SAR) robotics increasingly depends on collaborative intelligence to operate effectively in dynamic, uncertain, and time-sensitive environments. Modern SAR missions require coordinated interaction among heterogeneous robotic agents as well as structured collaboration between humans and intelligent systems for perception, decision-making, and adaptive mission execution. This paper presents a structured narrative review supported by a systematic literature search of learning-enabled collaborative intelligence frameworks in SAR robotics, organized around three paradigms: human-to-machine (H2M), machine-to-machine (M2M), and machine-to-human (M2H) learning. The review examines recent developments in reinforcement learning, federated and decentralized learning, knowledge distillation, swarm intelligence, semantic communication, and the growing integration of large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) for knowledge grounding, transfer, and explainability. Beyond algorithmic advances, the analysis emphasizes deployment-oriented challenges including partial observability, communication constraints, uncertainty management, model reliability, and real-time operational requirements. Rather than conducting a fully PRISMA-compliant systematic review, this work synthesizes representative and influential studies to identify emerging trends, architectural trade-offs, deployment limitations, and future research directions for scalable and trustworthy collaborative SAR systems.

metadata_records.title: Application of convolutional neural networks in spatio-temporal prediction of vehicular traffic
metadata_records.abstract: This paper systematically reviews how convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been used to predict vehicular traffic in space and time. To this end, research published between 2021 and 2026 in different academic databases was analyzed, with the aim of identifying the most used architectures, methodological approaches, evaluation metrics, as well as their main limitations and recent trends. From this review, it is observed that CNNs stand out especially in the identification of spatial traffic patterns. Their performance improves when combined with other approaches, such as recurrent models, attention mechanisms, and hybrid architectures, allowing traffic dynamics to be captured more completely. In particular, hybrid models have managed to increase accuracy by integrating both spatial and temporal information, in addition to incorporating external variables such as weather, accidents, events, and road conditions. However, the literature also points to several challenges: adequately representing complex road networks, avoiding the loss of topological information, modeling long-term dependencies, and reducing high computational costs, especially in real-time applications. Together, these findings offer a clear view of the current state of the field and serve as a starting point for the development of future solutions oriented to smart mobility systems.

metadata_records.title: Loosdorf-MSL: Benchmarking deep learning models for European NMCAs’ LULC schemes with multispectral LiDAR
metadata_records.abstract: Land Use Land Cover (LULC) classification is fundamental to national 3D mapping programs, geospatial analyses, resource management, and sustainable development planning. While multispectral (MS) LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) technology offers synchronized spatial-spectral information and Deep Learning (DL) has shown promise in 3D semantic segmentation, several challenges remain. Specifically, the application of 3D DL models to MS LiDAR data has received limited attention. Moreover, consistent class definition schemes aligned with the requirements of National Mapping and Cadastral Agencies (NMCAs), along with publicly available MS LiDAR benchmark datasets based on such schemes are still lacking. Furthermore, the potential of MS LiDAR data for supporting NMCA applications has not been systematically evaluated, limiting its integration into operational mapping workflows. Therefore, this study addresses these gaps by reporting NMCAs’ current (L1) and prospective (L2) LULC classification schemes, presenting a novel LiDAR benchmark dataset at two levels of detail (L1 and L2), evaluating seven state-of-the-art DL models, and finally conducting rigorous spectral ablation analyses at the two levels of detail. Benchmarking results demonstrate the superiority of the Point Transformer V3 model at both levels, achieving high mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) values of 78.4% for LULC-L1 (eight classes) and 58.9% (20 classes) for LULC-L2 by leveraging a two-wavelength commercial MS LiDAR system (532 nm and 1064 nm). Furthermore, spectral ablation studies highlight the significant potential of MS LiDAR data over purely geometric features. While the spectral advantage is marginal at LULC-L1 (a 1.1 Percentage Points (PP) improvement in mIoU by leveraging a vegetation index), it becomes considerably more pronounced at LULC-L2 (a 7.8 PP improvement). Our findings underscore the capacity of LiDAR reflectance and MS LiDAR for surface material identification, supporting the prospective transition of NMCAs schemes toward fine-grained LULC classification. The Loosdorf-MSL dataset contributes to improving consistency across LULC products. The dataset and code are available at https://github.com/3DOM-FBK/3D-LULC-classification .

metadata_records.title: Geographic Information Science and Earth Surface Processes
metadata_records.abstract: The surface of the Earth is constantly in motion. Valleys are cut by rivers, soil is washed away and glaciers melt. To mitigate hazards and ensure water security and climate adaptation, it is important to have an understanding of these processes occurring on the earth surface. Geographic Information Science and Earth Surface Processes combines geographic information science (GIScience), geographic information systems (GIS), remote sensing and Artificial Intelligence. It demonstrates landscape monitoring, modelling and prediction. It's just a simple motive. Data resulting from earth observation comes in with amazing volume and speed. These sources are satellites, drones, LiDAR and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) and in-situ sensor networks. Process-based numerical models and field surveys will still continue to be indispensable, but without being able to “harvest” this big data. Now, geospatial artificial intelligence (GeoAI), machine learning and deep learning fill that gap. To do this, they should satisfy spatial autocorrelation, scale, and uncertainty and physical knowledge. The book is opened with GeoAI and machine learning for Earth surface process modelling and prediction. The topics of geomorphology, erosion, flooding, coastal modifications, glaciers and permafrost and aeolian activity are discussed. The second chapter focuses on remote sensing and multisensor data fusion for spatiotemporal monitoring. It includes information about optical and SAR integration, LiDAR and interferometric SAR (InSAR) and cloud platforms like Google Earth Engine. The third examines geospatial foundation models and generative AI for the Earth observation – including self-supervised learning, transfer learning, explainable AI and aspects of ethics and energy cost. It's followed by water and slopes. GIS based hydrological modelling is introduced in the fourth chapter: watershed delineation, digital elevation models (DEMs), SWAT and HEC-HMS hydrological modelling, climate downscaling and climate change impact assessment. It connects the terrain analysis to the transport of sediments and extremes. The fifth applies to AI-created landslide susceptibility maps, hazard prediction and spatial risk assessment with emphasis on the aspects of validation and interpretability. The last chapters describe geospatial digital twins and real-time simulation. These are related to data assimilation, physics-informed machine learning, interoperability, open standards and FAIR data. They also discuss land use and land cover change, and the environmental vulnerability assessment for disaster risk reduction and sustainable development. There are two thoughts that motivate through. One, GIS is no longer ‘just a mapping tool.’ It is the integrating platform to link data, models and decisions. Second, the facts are that technology isn't enough. Valuable geospatial modelling can be achieved only when there is robust validation, documentation of uncertainty and commitment to open science and reproducible code, and equal treatment of local knowledge and availability of data. The book is designed for applied urban hydrology practitioners and researchers at the graduate level, as well as anyone working in natural hazards and climate resilience, the geosciences, and the environment. Every chapter is written as an independent unit, thus the reader can choose the sequence or go straight to the subject of interest. Limits and gaps in the research are identified and discussed providing support for teaching and research/policy. We hope that this volume will inspire readers to purse GED-geographic information science with ESS-earth surface science and use these technologies wisely for a changing planet and sustainable land management.
first_author_affiliations: Department of Nautical Science, AMET University, E.C.R , Kananthur

metadata_records.title: Event-based Action Recognition by Pre-Training on Multi-Frame Representations
metadata_records.abstract: Action recognition is a crucial task in domains like robotics, patient monitoring, or surveillance. Recently, event-based action recognition has attracted much attention due to the event camera's ability to capture fast motions and its improved privacy over conventional vision cameras. While frame-based event representations work well for short event sequences, their discriminative ability declines sharply with longer and more complex event sequences. In this work, we introduce a multi-frame representation that greatly improves recognition performance over its single-frame counterpart. We adopt a masked auto-encoding framework to pre-train a Vision Transformer using a sparsity-aware masking algorithm and token selection mechanism to improve downstream performance and control computational complexity. We also introduce multiple mask tokens for the decoder with a position-aware attention mechanism, leading to further improved performance. Our proposed method shows impressive performance for challenging long-duration and complex event sequences, yielding state-of-the-art performance on THU-EACT-50 CHL and DailyDVS-200.

metadata_records.title: Federated Distillation: A Survey
metadata_records.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without centralizing clients’ raw data, but parameter exchange can impose substantial communication costs and usually requires compatible model architectures. Federated distillation (FD) instead transfers predictive or intermediate knowledge through knowledge distillation (KD), which can support heterogeneous models and reduce communication in suitable settings. These benefits are not automatic: their magnitude depends on the transmitted knowledge, reference data, communication schedule, and threat model. This survey provides a challenge-centered synthesis of FD. We first formalize a representative public-data, response-based FD protocol and then organize existing methods by the FL challenges they address, including data, system, and model heterogeneity, client drift, catastrophic forgetting, communication cost, and privacy risk. We further review applications in industrial engineering, computer vision, natural language processing, and healthcare, including recent federated adaptation of large language models. Finally, we identify five research priorities: richer transferred knowledge, joint treatment of interacting forms of heterogeneity, communication-aware distillation, threat-model-driven privacy protection, and standardized theory, benchmarks, and evaluation.

metadata_records.title: Generative AI and Large Language Models: Transformers, Prompt Engineering, and AI Agents
metadata_records.abstract: Generative AI has transitioned from the lab to the classroom, hospitals, software teams, and boardrooms. Large language models (LLMs), transformer-based foundation models, are at the heart of this paradigm change, with their ability to write texts, reason, summarize, translate, and code. However, these developments have left many students and researchers, as well as practitioners, with disjointed bits of knowledge. This book was developed with that knowledge in mind in order to streamline all that information in a single comprehensive and hands-on natural language processing (NLP) and generative AI guide. The book follows the path of the technology itself. Chapter 1 covers transformer architectures ranging from the self-attention mechanism to encoder-decoder and decoder-only architectures. The course also includes lectures on mixture of experts, scaling laws, pretraining, fine-tuning, alignment and multimodal models. Targeting prompt engineering and in-context learning is the focus of Chapter 2. It uses zero shot, few shot, chain of thought prompting, system prompts and context engineering as skills to learn and test. Chapter 3 focuses on LLM reasoning and test-time compute, presenting various ways in which deep learning systems can be extended to form reasoning models, self-consistency, and search over reasoning paths. As it is not possible to know everything, Chapters 4 and 5 discuss retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). They start with embeddings and vector databases, chunking strategies and semantic search. They then transition to advanced RAG – hybrid search, reranking, knowledge graphs, GraphRAG, and agentic RAG, all while also focusing on evaluation and LLMOps for production. The strands are woven together in Chapter 6 under the umbrella of agentic AI and AI agents. It examines the use of tools, the calling of functions, the memory of an agent, as well as planning and multi-agent systems and the way autonomous agents are transforming work. Chapter 7 ends with trustworthy and responsible AI. It speaks about hallucination, bias/fairness, explainability, data privacy, AI safety, AI ethics and AI governance, as without trust, the capability cannot be sustained. The chapters are designed with learning and reference in mind for each. It introduces the foundations and outlines the key techniques side-by-side in summary tables, covers present open challenges and future directions, and concludes with practical advice. Benchmarking and evaluation is handled very transparently with regard to the deficiencies in existing approaches – and I do hope readers will take the shortcomings as a challenge and a starting point for their own work. The working levels that the book is aimed at are graduate and undergraduate students, academic researchers, machine learning engineers, data scientists, and technology leaders. Can also be used as a textbook in the course where it was used or as a builder's handbook or as a literature map for those preparing an indexed study in a Scopus journal. I'm focusing more on enduring principles than fleeting tools because no one can stay current in a science that is evolving monthly. We hope this book empowers you to grasp generative AI, create responsibly, and shape the future of AI together.

metadata_records.title: Location-Based Safety Management with Wearable Seamless Indoor-Outdoor Positioning
metadata_records.abstract: Reliable worker localization is essential for real-time industrial safety management, but seamless outdoor-indoor positioning remains challenging. GNSS performs well outdoors yet degrades near buildings and fails indoors, while many indoor systems require costly infrastructure or extensive calibration. This paper presents a practical safety-oriented positioning system that uses resource-constrained wearable tags and a device-cloud split architecture for continuous outdoor-indoor worker tracking. The tag integrates GNSS, IMU, barometric sensing, LTE Cat-M communication, and performs lightweight sensor fusion, while the cloud server executes map-aware fusion for continuous tracking. Developed as an operational platform, the system also includes a database, a map tool, and a dashboard that provide real-time monitoring, geofencing-based access alerts, and safety and productivity analysis. Experiments with multiple participants, each walking an approximately 1400 m outdoor-indoor route, using LTE Cat-M communication, achieve mean errors of 1.32 m indoors and 3.30 m outdoors, while maintaining low positioning latency and efficient power consumption. These results demonstrate the feasibility of wearable-based seamless positioning for scalable real-time safety management.

metadata_records.title: A Black-Box Positioning Solution for Effortless Integration in Wearable Navigation
metadata_records.abstract: Accurate localization is critical for a wide range of applications, including navigation, augmented reality, safety management, and healthcare. However, achieving accurate positioning remains challenging, especially in GPS-degraded environments. Pedestrian Dead Reckoning (PDR), which estimates position based on inertial sensor data, offers a promising alternative but typically demands substantial effort in algorithm design and system integration. This complexity often leads to prolonged development timelines and elevated costs. To address these challenges, we present the PDR Sensor (PDRS), a plug-and-play, black-box PDR module optimized for seamless integration into wearable and IoT platforms. PDRS integrates a microprocessor and an inertial measurement unit (IMU) within a compact, low-power module. It executes real-time sensor fusion onboard, providing position updates via standard interfaces (I2C, SPI, UART). Experimental evaluations demonstrate its high robustness, achieving a step detection error of just 0.16% over 1250 steps and a traveled distance error of 1.87% under diverse conditions. The system further exhibits low latency (2.5 ms) and modest power consumption (52.35 mA). Unlike conventional studies, the PDRS leverages a holistic co-design of hardware and software to enhance performance and integration aspects, simplifying adoption without requiring deep expertise. By lowering technical barriers, PDRS enables developers and researchers to prioritize innovation in IoT and wearable technologies, accelerating prototyping, reducing development time, and advancing industry progress. Future work aims to enhance accuracy, reduce power usage and module size, and integrate AI-driven techniques to better mitigate drift.

By lowering technical barriers, PDRS enables developers and researchers to prioritize innovation in IoT and wearable technologies, accelerating prototyping, reducing development time, and advancing industry progress. Future work aims to enhance accuracy, reduce power usage and module size, and integrate AI-driven techniques to better mitigate drift.

metadata_records.title: What Visual Representations Do World Action Models Need?
metadata_records.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) inherit powerful priors from pretrained video generation models, but their variational autoencoder (VAE) representations are optimized for visual reconstruction rather than manipulation. External visual representations can improve manipulation, but existing methods couple representation choices with different integration mechanisms, obscuring their individual effects. We systematically compare visual representations, five integration mechanisms, and feature combinations under controlled settings. Our study yields three main findings. First, strong general-purpose visual representations provide broader robustness gains and can match or outperform representations pretrained for specific visual capabilities. Second, channel-wise joint prediction achieves the highest average success rate; further analyses suggest that future-feature prediction and the action expert's effective use of added visual information contribute to its gains. Third, additional sources should be selected for the task-relevant information they contribute beyond existing representations, as the same source can help one combination but harm another. However, even the best evaluated composition provides a smaller additional gain than the initial improvement from adding a strong general-purpose representation to the VAE-only baseline. We instantiate the resulting Representation Recipe as R$^2$-WAM. It achieves state-of-the-art performance on RoboCasa GR1 Tabletop with an 84.7% success rate and reaches 92.8% on RoboTwin 2.0, improving over the VAE-only baselines by 5.9 and 2.2 percentage points, respectively. Taken together, these findings suggest that future work should prioritize stronger general-purpose visual representations and more effective mechanisms for integrating them into WAMs, with feature composition serving as a supplementary route to improvement.

metadata_records.title: HAAF-RT-DETR: hybrid attention and high-resolution feature fusion based RT-DETR for kidney stone detection
metadata_records.abstract: Accurate localization and detection of kidney stones in computed tomography (CT) images are important for computer-aided medical image analysis. However, accurate detection remains challenging due to the small size of stones, weak boundaries, and complex renal anatomical backgrounds. To address these issues, this work proposes HAAF-RT-DETR (Hybrid Attention and High-Resolution Feature Fusion Based RT-DETR) for kidney stone detection. HAAF-RT-DETR integrates hybrid attention mechanisms and high-resolution feature fusion strategies into the RT-DETR framework to enhance feature representation and improve small-object detection performance. Within this framework, the HGBlock-AssemFormer module is introduced to jointly model local convolutional feature aggregation and Transformer-based global dependencies, thereby strengthening high-level semantic representations. In addition, a Convolution–Attention Fusion Module (CAFM) is employed to further refine high-level feature representations and reduce background interference. Furthermore, a high-resolution P2 feature level is incorporated, extending the original three-scale pyramid (P3–P5) to a four-scale representation (P2–P5), enabling fine-grained spatial details to participate in the DETR-style unified decoding process. Experiments on stone-positive CT slices from TEZ_ROI_AUG and the Kidney Stone Dataset demonstrate improvements in mAP, Recall, and F1-score over the evaluated YOLO-based detectors and RT-DETR baseline.

metadata_records.title: Aero‐ VLM : Vision‐Language Guided Oriented Aircraft Detection for Remote Sensing Imagery
metadata_records.abstract: ABSTRACT Fine‐grained aircraft detection in remote sensing (RS) imagery is challenged by limited labelled data, domain shifts, high intra‐class similarity and complex environmental conditions. Conventional detectors rely heavily on dense supervision, whereas vision–language models (VLMs) often lack the geometric precision required for accurate localization in aerial scenes. To address these challenges, we propose Aero‐VLM, a hybrid CNN–Transformer framework that combines self‐supervised visual representation learning with pretrained vision–language semantic embeddings for data‐efficient fine‐grained aircraft detection. An oriented detection head with knowledge distillation is integrated with the vision–language representation to improve geometric localization and support efficient inference. We further introduce Aero‐RSI, a 10,000‐image high‐resolution benchmark comprising ten visually similar aircraft categories for fine‐grained detection. Aero‐VLM achieves 64.6% mAP@50 in zero‐shot evaluation on unseen classes, outperforming CLIP, BLIP‐2, Grounding DINO and VisionLLM by up to 44.1 percentage points. With only 10 labelled samples per class, Aero‐VLM improves mAP@50 by 16.1 percentage points, whereas competing models achieve gains of less than 10 percentage points. Cross‐domain evaluation on DOTA, MTARSI and FAIR1M demonstrates strong generalization without additional fine‐tuning, with Aero‐VLM achieving gains of up to 11.0 percentage points over CNN‐based detectors and up to 46.0 percentage points over adapted VLMs. Under full supervision, Aero‐VLM achieves 90.2% mAP@50, exceeding YOLOv11s by 2.5 percentage points and Grounding DINO by 39.7 percentage points. Despite a 33% increase in inference latency relative to YOLOv11s, Aero‐VLM requires approximately 45% less inference time than Grounding DINO, demonstrating a favourable accuracy–efficiency trade‐off.

metadata_records.title: Privacy-preserving techniques in visual computing: applications, challenges, and future directions
metadata_records.abstract: The proliferation of imaging technologies across healthcare, agriculture, environments, and consumer applications has heightened concerns regarding the privacy and security of visual data, which may contain biometric, medical, spatial, and location-specific information. Although federated learning (FL), differential privacy (DP), and secure multi-party computation (SMPC) have been reviewed as individual privacy-preserving approaches, existing surveys have predominantly examined these mechanisms in isolation from privacy-aware design principles. Moreover, limited attention has been given to imaging as a data modality, despite modality-specific privacy, and information leakage risks that differ from those associated with tabular and textual data. To address this research gap, this mini-review adopts a PRISMA-guided systematic review methodology to examine the literature on privacy-preserving approaches for imaging applications. An initial corpus of more than 5,000 records was screened and refined to a final set of 50 high-quality journal and conference publications based on publisher reliability, venue quality, and reporting rigor. The review establishes four dimensions of novelty in comparison with existing surveys and provides a characterization of five imaging sectors. For each sector, representative applications derived from implementations are examined alongside mathematically formalized challenges associated with federated learning, differential privacy, and secure multi-party computation. Trends in publication activity, application domains, and privacy-related challenges are analyzed through narrative and tabular presentations. Based on the synthesized evidence, the review contextualizes current adoption patterns and delineates prospective research directions for privacy-aware visual computing systems, distinguishing direct empirical observations from conceptual research trajectories.

metadata_records.title: Hjort-YOLO: a lightweight and explainable computer vision framework for wildlife detection
metadata_records.abstract: Introduction Automated animal detection is an important component of ecological monitoring and may in the future be used also for wildlife vehicle collision mitigation by constructing efficient alert systems. However, the often complex environmental background in habitats along roads and different sizes due to the distance from the camera lens of animals in the images may reduce the detection accuracy, whereas high-precision detection requires computationally expensive object detection methods. This paper presents Hjort-YOLO, an efficient computer vision framework for detecting wildlife from camera-trap images acquired under challenging background conditions. Methodology The proposed framework was developed by enhancing the lightweight YOLOv11n architecture through targeted modifications to the backbone and detection head by improving the cross-stage partial convolutional block (C2f-W), an area attention block (A2C2f-W), and reducing a detection head compared to the YOLOv11n algorithm, enabling an optimal balance between detection accuracy and computational efficiency. Hjort-YOLO is evaluated on the custom Svanøy deer dataset and the African Wildlife dataset, which include complex forest scenes, occlusions, background clutter, and motion blur. Results Experimental findings indicate that the Hjort-YOLO achieves detection accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art object detection models while significantly improving runtime performance. Hjort-YOLO provides 0.2 percent, 13 percent, and 17 percent better mean average precision, frames per second, and inference time, respectively, while detecting wildlife compared to YOLOv11n. The computation complexity, such as Giga Floating Operations per Second, was reduced by 19 percent compared to the YOLOv11n algorithm. Discussion These performance gains show the suitability of the proposed framework for detecting wildlife from ground-based sensors like camera traps, providing real-time performance and high detection accuracy in resource-constrained platforms.

metadata_records.title: Complex scene green walnut target detection method based on improved YOLOv11n
metadata_records.abstract: To meet the efficiency and accuracy requirements of agricultural product inspection, deep learning-based object detection technology has been widely adopted. However, factors such as varying lighting conditions and foliage occlusion cause green walnuts in complex scenes to exhibit low texture contrast and a tendency to lose edge information. To address these issues, this paper proposes GPL-YOLO, an object detection algorithm for green walnuts based on an improved YOLOv11n architecture. First, the GhostModuleV2 module is introduced into the backbone network to enhance global modeling capabilities and enrich the detailed information of walnut targets within high-level feature maps. Second, a PPA module is integrated into the multi-scale feature fusion stage of the neck; this module effectively filters and enhances fused features across spatial and channel dimensions, thereby highlighting the target regions of green walnuts while suppressing background noise. Finally, a DW-LAE feature enhancement module is embedded in the downsampling fusion branch to adaptively preserve and enhance shallow-level detailed features during downsampling, thereby minimizing the loss of edge, texture, and shape information and improving the effectiveness of deep semantic features. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to the baseline model, this algorithm achieves improvements of 8.6%, 5.7%, and 8.7% in Precision, Recall, and mAP50, respectively. The improved model outperforms the original YOLOv11n in detection accuracy and effectively mitigates missed detections and false positives in complex backgrounds, providing technical support for intelligent harvesting, yield estimation, and precision management in green walnut orchards.

metadata_records.title: Replaying the Movie in Your Mind Decoding Dynamic Visual Perception and Recall from EEG
metadata_records.abstract: Decoding dynamic visual content from EEG has advanced rapidly for visual perception, yet it remains unclear which aspects of neural representations are preserved when people internally replay dynamic scenes. We introduce PAIR, an EEG benchmark collected from 20 participants using an interleaved, clip-wise paradigm that pairs naturalistic video viewing with immediate visual recall. This design enables a comparison between externally driven perception and internally generated recall for the same stimulus content within a fixed trial sequence. We benchmark multiple decoding models on hierarchical semantic classification at both fine-grained and coarse-grained levels, meta-feature decoding tasks covering motion, color, object number, face, and human presence, and a state-decoding task that discriminates perception from recall. Within-subject validation results show numerically similar performance for several model--task combinations, alongside higher perception accuracy in two coarse-grained comparisons after multiple-comparison correction. In contrast, perception and recall are highly separable at the state level under the present validation protocol. State accuracy remains high after alpha-band ablation, although this does not exclude ocular or other task-related contributions.

metadata_records.title: REFLECT: Role-Aware Detection of Sentiment, Emotion, Politeness, and Formality
metadata_records.abstract: Detecting communicative meaning in dialogue requires modeling not only lexical content but also the participant-role structures through which sentiment, emotion, politeness, and formality (SEPF) are expressed. Existing approaches rely on contextual language representations while leaving semantic roles implicit. We introduce a role-aware transformer architecture that maps the four SEPF dimensions to theory-grounded Semantic Role Labeling (SRL) configurations, incorporating these configurations directly into the transformer's self-attention mechanism. Role-aware attention models non-directional internal states (sentiment and emotion), while directional role-aware attention captures initiator-to-recipient relations for external cues (politeness and formality). The resulting role-aware representations are fused with contextual embeddings through a learned gate that adaptively weights how much role information each input contributes, rather than appending semantic roles as an auxiliary feature vector. Across four benchmark datasets, the framework yields statistically reliable gains over strong BERT-based baselines for emotion, politeness, and formality, with gains concentrated in theoretically predicted cases such as low-frequency, complex emotions and highly polite expressions; sentiment improvements are marginal and non-significant, suggesting that sentiment is conveyed more through lexical choice than participant-role structure. Additional evaluation on real-world data demonstrates that the framework improves both predictive performance and model traceability. These results demonstrate that linguistically grounded modifications to transformer self-attention improve the detection of communicative meaning, generalize beyond benchmark datasets to real-world mental-health data, and yield traceable, role-grounded explanations that extend beyond predictive performance to interpretability.

metadata_records.title: Mediated Givenness and Scientific Object-Formation: Infrared and Ultraviolet Radiation Beyond Direct Perception
metadata_records.abstract: Scientific instruments make imperceptible phenomena knowable, but it remains unclear whether such access enlarges perception itself or only other forms of epistemic availability. This article develops a layered relational realist account of mediated givenness to explain how scientific objects become available without being constituted by human access. It distinguishes three functional layers of mediation—embodied-phenomenal, translational-display, and integrated-substitutive—and four directional modes of availability: existential, structural, predictive, and qualitative. On this account, translational-display technologies convert object-dependent effects into bodily receivable carriers, whereas integrated-substitutive technologies become part of the perceptual medium that organizes a subject’s experiential field. The article further reconstructs scientific object-formation as a sequence from object-dependent effects and carrier appearance to mediated anchoring, operational stabilization, communal validation, and theoretical integration. Historical cases involving Herschel’s infrared and Ritter’s ultraviolet experiments illustrate how imperceptible effects became stable public objects of inquiry through measurement, calibration, comparison, and theoretical incorporation. The analysis shows that science can expand existential, structural, and predictive access without producing new qualitative experience. It therefore locates the limits of direct perception in embodied or technologically integrated perceptual organization while treating broader cognition as extendable through reliable technical, symbolic, mathematical, and theoretical mediation.

metadata_records.title: The Evidence Anchoring Boundary: Where Visual Interventions Matter and When They Help in Multimodal LLMs
metadata_records.abstract: Visual interventions provide a training-free way to reduce hallucinations in multimodal large language models. However, an intervention may have little leverage at some layers and may damage a correct answer even when it changes the output. We investigate where visual interventions retain leverage and when they improve predictions. First, we apply the same visual-residual edit at successive decoder layers, matching its RMS strength across depth. Across six checkpoints from three model families, we observe a persistent drop in intervention effect and define its operational onset for this edit as the \textbf{Evidence Anchoring Boundary (EAB)}. With boundaries fixed on calibration queries, held-out effects on disjoint evaluation queries before EAB are $13.78\times$--$26.10\times$ larger than those after it. Comparison with intermediate readouts shows that the edit can lose leverage before answer preferences stabilize. Second, we compare counterfactual subtraction across presence, attribute, and relation questions. Subtraction can correct a misleading preference, leave a decision unchanged, or remove a preference supporting the correct answer. Based on these observations, we develop calibrated selective routing, which preserves the original prediction unless calibration supports an intervention for the question type. It improves full-set attribute accuracy by $1.56$--$1.81$ percentage points across three checkpoints, while universal subtraction is neutral or harmful.

metadata_records.title: Hybrid open-vocabulary and closed-set helmet detection with slicing-aided hyper inference for robust drone-based construction-safety monitoring
metadata_records.abstract: Introduction Manual monitoring of helmet use is impractical in dynamic, congested, and safety-critical construction environments, particularly when unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) capture workers from varying altitudes, viewpoints, illumination conditions, and occlusion levels. This study proposes a hybrid helmet-detection framework integrating YOLO-E and YOLOv12 to improve detection accuracy, small-object recognition, color fidelity, and open-set awareness for real-time construction safety monitoring. Methods The proposed framework combines the language-guided open-vocabulary capabilities of YOLO-E with the real-time feature extraction and object-detection capabilities of YOLOv12. Slicing-Aided Hyper Inference (SAHI), image preprocessing, synthetic-weather augmentation, and prompt-sensitivity analysis were incorporated to improve robustness under challenging operating conditions. The framework was evaluated using a publicly balanced PPE dataset and a newly developed UAV-based helmet dataset containing 6,471 annotated helmet instances captured across different altitudes, viewing angles, lighting conditions, weather scenarios, helmet colors, and occlusion levels. We conducted ablation experiments to measure the contribution of each component of the framework. Results The SAHI-enhanced hybrid framework increased mean average precision at the 50% IoU threshold from 89% to 97%, improved small-object recall from 0.41 to 0.80, and reduced localization error to 2.25 pixels. The proposed approach also achieved scores of 0.96 for weather robustness and 0.97 for color fidelity. Comparative experiments showed that the hybrid YOLO-E + YOLOv12 framework achieved superior precision, recall, and F1-score relative to the evaluated baseline and existing detection architectures, including Mask R-CNN, Faster R-CNN, RetinaNet, and SSD. Discussion The results demonstrate that combining open-vocabulary recognition, closed-set detection, SAHI-based small-object enhancement, and robustness-oriented preprocessing provides a scalable solution for UAV-based helmet monitoring. The framework is particularly suitable for construction safety auditing and large-scale surveillance scenarios requiring real-time detection under variable environmental conditions, while its open-set awareness improves adaptability to previously unrecognized visual conditions.
first_author_affiliations: Department of Cybersecurity and Information Sciences, Arkansas Tech University

metadata_records.title: A comprehensive review and bibliometric analysis of deep learning applications in plant disease detection
metadata_records.abstract: Abstract Agriculture is a major component of many countries’ economies worldwide, especially in developing nations. The major challenge farmers face is the rapid spread of plant diseases, which often goes unnoticed and causes major yield and economic losses. Traditional methods such as human inspection and laboratory testing are often time-consuming, inaccurate, labor-intensive, and unsuitable for large-scale farming. To overcome these challenges, advanced technologies like Machine learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) have emerged in recent times, providing early and accurate detection of plant diseases. This paper focuses on recent advances in applying deep learning techniques, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), to detect plant diseases. Across 1081 publications from 2014 to 2024, studies show that CNNs are well suited to extracting and analyzing features from plant images and clearly distinguishing healthy from diseased specimens. The models discussed in the surveyed literature generally report performance in terms of key parameters such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, which this review compiles and discusses rather than benchmarking through new experiments. The results show high accuracy and strong potential for real-world agricultural applications. The bibliometric analysis reveals growing interest and collaborative efforts in the research domain, especially among institutions specializing in artificial intelligence and agriculture. Moreover, the results support the practical application of deep learning in agriculture for plant health monitoring and highlight the importance of comprehensive studies in solving agricultural problems. The study provides a foundation for further innovations in automated plant disease detection and supports the transition to smart farming solutions.

metadata_records.title: A Multi-Scale UAV Cluster Detection and Counting Framework Based on Multi-Source Information Fusion and Enhanced YOLOv9
metadata_records.abstract: To address the safety hazards posed by unauthorized "black flight" of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) clusters, as well as the limitations of existing detection methods in tiny target recognition and complex environment adaptability, this paper proposes a real-time detection and counting method based on a feature fusion framework. The core contribution of this work is a novel multi-level fusion architecture that aggregates multi-scale visual features to enhance detection robustness under challenging conditions. First, we construct a multi scene UAV data set containing 7,113 images, and design a dedicated feature fusion module based on improved YOLOv9 backbone. The Haar Wavelet Down-sampling (HWD) module is introduced to fuse high-frequency edge details with low-frequency approximation features, preserving critical texture information that is essential for tiny target detection. The Programmable Gradient Information (PGI) mechanism is adopted as an auxiliary reversible branch, which propagates reliable deep-layer gradient information to shallow layers to effectively mitigate the information bottleneck problem. Second, a decision-level fusion strategy is developed to aggregate confidence scores and localization outputs from multi-scale predictions. The strategy is further optimized with a tailored Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) algorithm to resolve occlusion issues in dense UAV clusters. Evaluations on the self-built dense UAV dataset show that the proposed method achieves a detection accuracy of 85% with a per-frame processing time of 0.10–0.15 s. Tests across diverse scenarios validate that the method can accurately locate and identify UAV targets. By achieving a favorable balance between detection accuracy and real-time performance, the proposed method effectively alleviates the missed detection and false detection problems in dense UAV cluster detection tasks.

metadata_records.title: Target-focused supervision and fine spatial evidence improve sparse landslide detection in remote-sensing imagery
metadata_records.abstract: Introduction Regional landslide screening must retrieve sparsely annotated failures among visually similar terrain while limiting false review candidates. Small scars can lose spatial detail during downsampling, and extensive background regions can dominate semantic supervision. Methods We developed the Sparse Landslide Detection Transformer (SLD-DETR) by adapting RT-DETRv4. It combines scale-guided focused distillation (SGFD), which concentrates teacher–student alignment near annotated landslides; high-resolution scale-aware supervision (HRSS), which supervises stride-4 features; and stride-4 decoder memory (S2-Mem), which exposes fine spatial features to query selection and cross-attention. We evaluated five independent training seeds on a source-scene-disjoint 6:2:2 split of the Multi-Scale Landslide Dataset (MSLD). For screening performance, confidence thresholds were calibrated on validation to a false-positive rate of no more than 0.10 false positives per image (FPPI), then frozen for testing. We also assessed zero-shot transfer to LRSTTC-New. Results On the held-out MSLD test split, SLD-DETR achieved a mean average precision of 58.07 ± 1.10 % across IoU thresholds 0.50–0.95 (mAP@50:95) and 63.43 ± 1.23 % mAP@75, compared with 53.90 ± 0.96 % and 58.34 ± 2.65 % , respectively, for RT-DETRv4-S. At the validation-calibrated operating points, test miss rate was 15.82 ± 2.18% for SLD-DETR and 18.63 ± 0.99% for the baseline. Under zero-shot cross-region transfer, all detectors degraded substantially; SLD-DETR had the highest AP within the RT-DETRv4 family, while RF-DETR-S performed best overall. Discussion The coordinated modules improved box-level screening on the evaluated source-disjoint MSLD split. SGFD and HRSS are training-only, whereas S2-Mem remains at inference and adds approximately 0.06 million parameters. Runtime and memory costs increase with image resolution.
first_author_affiliations: School of Computer Science, Yangtze University
